title: Gaining the upper hand
TLR5 drives metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis through lipid- and flagellin-induced hepatocyte injury signaling
abstract: Liver fibrosis is a strong predictor of clinical outcomes in metabolic dysfunction–associated steatohepatitis (MASH). Fibrosis is a consequence of persistent liver cell injury and inflammation in which Toll-like receptors (TLRs) play a key initiating role. Here, we test the hypothesis that TLR5 is involved in the development of MASH and fibrosis using a combination of clinical data from multiple independent patient cohorts, single-cell liver transcriptomics, and human in vitro and ex vivo models. Hepatic TLR5 expression, but not TLR2 or TLR4, is associated with liver fibrosis and mortality. Plasma levels of TLR5’s cognate ligand flagellin are increased in MASH with advanced fibrosis and fall with liver disease improvement. Mechanistically, we identify two parallel TLR5-mediated routes to hepatocyte injury: one elicited by flagellin and the other indirectly by lipid injury. Furthermore, hepatocyte TLR5 inhibition abrogates paracrine activation of hepatic stellate cells to suppress collagen production. This is also seen ex vivo in patient-derived precision-cut liver slices where TLR5 inhibition significantly reduces lipid-induced collagen deposition. These findings reveal a new role for TLR5 signaling, specifically in the development of advanced MASH fibrosis and may offer a novel disease-specific therapeutic approach.

title: Non-invasive, high-precision, and independently controllable neuromodulation via optimized multiple temporal interference stimulation
abstract: Non-invasive neuromodulation is an important approach in clinical and translational neuroscience, yet existing techniques remain limited in precisely and flexibly targeting spatially distributed brain regions. Temporal interference stimulation (TIS) enabled non-invasive selective targeting; however, conventional implementations lack sufficient spatial focality, steerability, and scalability for network-level modulation. Here, we introduce optimized multiple temporal interference stimulation (omTIS), a computationally optimized framework that achieves high spatial focality, flexible steerability, and scalable control for distributed neuromodulation. Using a multi-electrode architecture, finite element analysis (FEA)–based optimization, and carefully selected multiple carrier frequencies, omTIS generates focal interference envelopes that can be positioned across multiple brain targets, enabling simultaneous and independently controllable multi-focal stimulation with minimal mutual interference. Across simulations, tissue-mimicking phantom experiments, and in vivo mouse studies, omTIS outperformed conventional TIS in spatial selectivity, steering flexibility, and cross-talk-free multi-focal modulation. These results establish omTIS as a scalable platform for precise, non-invasive control of distributed brain networks.

title: Postimpact evolution of the South Pole–Aitken basin revealed by Chang’e-4 and Chang’e-6
abstract: South Pole–Aitken (SPA) basin has recorded complex geological histories of the Moon. It is a critical region for solving lunar fundamental questions but remained unexplored until the Chang’e-4 and Chang’e-6 missions of China. Their in situ measurements and the Chang’e-6 samples provided the first ground truth for the SPA evolution. On the basis of these constraints, we found that the SPA impact occurred ∼4.34 billion years ago, generating a thick melt sheet that differentiated to form moderately magnesium (Mg)–rich norites. They are exposed at the SPA central peaks and currently investigated by the Chang’e-4 mission in Von Kármán crater, transported by the Finsen impact to the site. Highly Mg-rich materials were found within SPA, likely products of Mg-suite magmatism, including those exposed at the Apollo western peak ring. They were initially excavated by the Apollo impact at ∼4.2 billion years ago and delivered to the Chang’e-6 site by the Chaffee S impact. A series of other events occurred in the SPA basin subsequently (e.g., the Orientale impact ∼3.87 billion years ago); all of them shaped the architecture of the Moon’s largest impact basin.

title: Genome-wide association study identifies a functional myostatin variant increasing lean mass in humans
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Muscle mass is central to physical function and metabolic health, but can decrease with disease, aging and weight loss interventions. As weight loss interventions become more widely used, agents that preserve or increase muscle mass are needed. To identify such therapeutic opportunities, we perform genome-wide association meta-analyses of arm, leg, trunk and total lean mass measured by dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry, a widely used method to estimate muscle mass. We identify 63 loci, including a rare missense variant in MSTN (p.Ile225Thr, rs143242500), which has the largest effect on leg lean mass (β = 0.28 SD [95% CI: 0.19, 0.37], P = 1.9 × 10-9). MSTN encodes myostatin, a negative regulator of skeletal muscle mass and a therapeutic target for muscle wasting disorders. Here, we identify a genome-wide significant association at MSTN in humans and characterize its functional consequences, providing genetic evidence that may inform the long-term systemic effects of myostatin inhibition.

title: Auditory cortical coding of spectrotemporal modulations is sufficient to support perceptual categorization of speech and music
abstract: Auditory processing is typically described as hierarchical, culminating in neural representation of abstract categories. However, it remains unclear whether category-selective responses in auditory cortex require representational mechanisms beyond the coding of acoustic features or whether the acoustic representations already available in the auditory cortex are sufficient to account for categorization. Here, we test whether cortical coding of spectrotemporal modulation (STM) features is sufficient to support speech-music categorization by combining human intracranial recordings with continuous behavioral judgments of a naturalistic soundtrack in which speech and music occur both separately and simultaneously. We show that temporal and spectral modulation patterns largely characterize speech and music, respectively, and that cortical auditory regions robustly track these features over time, with distinct oscillatory frequency bands preferentially encoding temporal and spectral modulations. Critically, cortical representations of STMs predicted perceptual categorical judgments gathered in an independent sample. Last, speech- and music-related STM representations showed stronger tracking of category-specific acoustical features in left versus right cortical auditory regions, respectively. These findings indicate that the efficient neural coding of acoustical features provides a sufficient basis for the categorical distinction between speech and music and that the temporal and spectral components of this representation are implemented through distinct oscillatory mechanisms.

title: Ribosome-associated vesicles promote activity-dependent local translation in neurons
abstract: Local protein synthesis in axons and dendrites underpins synaptic plasticity. However, the composition of the protein synthesis machinery in distal neuronal processes and the mechanisms for its deployment to local translation sites remain unclear. Here, we employed multi-scale imaging that combines cryo-electron tomography, volume electron microscopy, and live-cell imaging to identify endoplasmic reticulum-derived KDEL-positive vesicles, a subset of which are decorated with ribosomes (Ribosome-Associated Vesicles, RAVs) in neurites. We demonstrate that neuronal stimulation triggers compartment-specific responses: dendrites accumulate stationary KDEL-positive vesicles at sites of enhanced translation, while axons accelerate vesicle transport. cLTP stimulation additionally increases the proportion of KDEL-positive vesicles that carry ribosomes, expanding the local RAV pool. Real-time imaging of translation at single mRNA resolution reveals that RAV-associated translation sites exhibit ∼30% greater nascent-peptide signal amplitude compared to periods without RAV association, indicating that RAVs boost local translation output. These findings establish RAVs as specialized platforms that integrate activity-dependent signals with local protein synthesis, providing a mechanistic framework for understanding how neurons achieve precise spatiotemporal control of translation.

title: The interferon-gamma response pathway is a targetable driver of FSHD muscular dystrophy progression
abstract: Facioscapulohumeral muscular dystrophy (FSHD) is a leading neuromuscular disorder caused by the aberrant expression of the transcription factor double homeobox 4 (DUX4) in skeletal muscle. While DUX4 is normally restricted to early embryonic development, its reactivation in FSHD triggers chronic inflammation and progressive muscle degeneration. However, the precise molecular links between DUX4 and persistent immune activation remain poorly understood. Here, we show that DUX4 induces a viral mimicry-like pathway that is fundamentally uncoupled from canonical type I interferon (IFN) activation. Instead, DUX4 establishes a non-canonical innate immune state dominated by IFN-γ signaling, providing a mechanistic explanation for the non-resolving inflammation characteristic of the disease. We demonstrate that while IFN-γ treatment alone is sufficient to recapitulate key DUX4 pathogenic effects, its inhibition rescues muscle inflammation and halts disease progression in FSHD models. These findings define a “skewed viral mimicry” process driven by a disease-specific transcription factor and identify IFN-γ as a primary therapeutic target for tissue-informed immunomodulation in muscular dystrophy.

title: Phylogeny explains differences in the crystal structures and chemistry of vertebrate tooth enamel and enameloid
abstract:
A phylogenetically diverse suite of modern tooth enamel/enameloid bioapatite from fishes, mammals, and reptiles from 22 species were chemically and structurally analyzed to establish whether crystal structure and chemistry are phylogenetically correlated. Rietveld refinement analysis of x-ray diffraction data suggests variable crystallographic parameters across vertebrates. Coupled chemical data show correlations between the
                    a
                    -axis of bioapatite and the proportions of sodium substitution for calcium, the introduction of vacancies, and carbonate substituting for phosphate (B-type substitution) or channel anions (A-type substitution). Principal component analysis of all variables suggests that
                    a
                    -axis lengths are highly influenced by the introduction of carbonate in both crystallographic sites. Phylogenetic variations in chemistry and structure of enamel/enameloid crystals show how biomineralization processes have changed through evolutionary time with implications for variation in biomineralization processes across vertebrate lineages. The predominant controls on tooth enamel/enameloid crystal structure are phylogeny rather than primary diet or habitat. Crystal structure variations also influence material properties across organisms, which may control how teeth are fossilized.

title: Chromatin loci move coherently due to spatially correlated fluctuations
abstract:
From enhancer-promoter communication to DNA repair, essential genome functions require chromosomal loci to encounter each other. While live-cell imaging enables direct measurement of pairwise locus dynamics, a quantitative framework for interpreting them is lacking. Here, using imaging data from
                    Drosophila
                    embryos and mouse stem cells, we show that nearby loci diffuse relative to each other far more slowly than expected from polymer chain–mediated effects. We propose that this slowdown is caused by spatially correlated fluctuations (SCFs) which couple loci via the nucleoplasm. We theoretically predict how these fluctuations scale with space, time, and genomic separation and confirm these predictions using live-cell imaging. Using polymer simulations, we demonstrate that while spatially correlated equilibrium noise fails to reproduce the observed SCF scalings, coupling the polymer to actively driven flows recapitulates the experimental statistics. Consistently, we experimentally show that SCFs couple locus motion across chromosomes and that their magnitude depends on adenosine 5′-triphosphate (ATP)–dependent activity and cohesin-mediated loop extrusion. By reducing encounter frequencies while prolonging encounter durations, SCFs generate a trade-off with direct implications for gene regulation. Our results provide a quantitative framework for chromatin dynamics, revealing how nuclear activity governs chromatin encounters in living cells.

title: An integrative single-cell long noncoding RNA atlas reveals regulatory programs in the pan-cancer tumor microenvironment
abstract: Long noncoding RNAs (lncRNAs) have been shown as critical components in cancer genomics, yet their functionality and regulation remain elusive. Here, we present an integrative lncRNA atlas covering more than 370,000 cells from 18 cancer types. In addition to multiple lineage- and cellular state transition–associated lncRNAs, we identify a set of lncRNAs that are embedded within cell type–specific regulons, suggesting associations between lncRNA expression and cell type–enriched transcriptional programs. By integrating CRISPR-based functional genomic screens and clinical data, we further prioritize not only CRISPR-supported candidate lncRNAs linked to tumor cell fitness and immune cell state features but also specific lncRNA signatures correlated with patient survival and immunotherapy response.

title: Tunable spectral correlations of highly multimode visible light via broadband quantum frequency conversion
abstract: Multimode squeezed states of light are a resource for achieving quantum advantage in computing and sensing, where spatial or temporal modes have been the experimental norm. In our experiments, we generated highly frequency-multimode infrared quantum light and showed how adiabatic frequency conversion can be used to convert the quantum state to visible wavelengths while concurrently manipulating the joint spectrum by realizing a configurable many-port frequency-domain beamsplitter unitary transformation. We report near-unity efficiency quantum frequency conversion over a bandwidth >45 terahertz, which allowed us to measure the state with an electron-multiplying CCD (EMCCD) camera-based spectrometer, at noncryogenic temperatures. The parametric amplification and conversion of >400 frequency modes yielded an overall mean of ∼700 visible photons per shot and photon statistics consistent with squeezing. Our work shows how many-mode quantum states of light can be generated, manipulated, and measured with efficient use of hardware resources, motivating the use of frequency encoding in quantum optics.

title: Hydrogen radical-participating spatiotemporal sequential therapy via hypoxia aggravation for hypoxia-amplified immunotherapy
abstract: The hypoxic characteristics of the tumor microenvironment and endogenous antioxidant defenses compromise the efficacy of oxygen-consuming oxidative therapy, positioning oxygen-free reductive stress as a new paradigm in tumor treatment. Nevertheless, the immunosuppressive characteristics of hypoxia and reductive stress pose significant challenges for advancing reductive stress-induced immunotherapy. Here, we constructed a hydrogen radical (H•) generator synergistically activated by near-infrared light and thiols, and first elucidated that photocatalytic H•-mediated reductive stress can elicit a robust antitumor immune response via the H•-featured mechanism. Nanoplatform HA@UFTL was engineered using lactate oxidase as an ideal H• partner, with the synergistic contribution enabling cross-amplified antitumor immunotherapy. The H•-participating spatiotemporal sequential strategy highlights a triple spatiotemporal sequential cascade, including dual sequential hypoxia exacerbation, sequential oxidative-reductive stress, and sequential organelle damage. By aggravating rather than alleviating hypoxia, HA@UFTL overcomes immunosuppression induced by hypoxia and reductive stress with H• as a universal building block, providing new insights for hypoxia-based immunotherapy.

title: Bionic skin with hair follicle regeneration capability from acoustic fluids-mediated 3D printing
abstract: Tissue engineering holds substantial potential for constructing normal skin with appendages such as hair follicles, directly restoring skin’s complete physiological functions. The current challenge lies in recreating biomimetic hair follicle organs with high-level cell density and architecture. Here, we developed an acoustofluidic-assisted 3D bioprinting platform to fabricate bionic skins with efficient hair follicle regeneration capability. Pre-formed hair follicle germs, derived from co-cultured epidermal and dermal mesenchymal stem cells, were encapsulated within a hydrogel bioink. Controlled acoustic fields generated flow vortices that directed cell migration and promoted organized cellular assembly from initially disordered states. Guided cell aggregates were then patterned through bioprinting to construct a grid-structured bionic skin. This architecture provided stable 3D support while maintaining high porosity, enabling efficient gas exchange. The printed bionic skin exhibited well-organized spatial cell distribution, high cellular viability, and promising differentiation potential. Further in vivo experiments demonstrated the efficiency of the bionic skin in accelerating mature hair regeneration, showing promise for clinical alopecia treatment.

title: Dynein-dependent positioning of multiple organelles regulates adaptive gene expression during oxidative stress
abstract: Cells respond to environmental insults through well-characterized changes to their transcriptome and proteome. The contribution that reorganization of intracellular architecture makes to the adaptive stress response is much less understood. Here, we reveal a conserved spatial response to oxidative stress in which the microtubule motor dynein enhances perinuclear clustering of multiple membrane-bound organelles. These events are triggered by reactive oxygen species and protein kinase C and occur without increased association of dynein with its activator dynactin, pointing to a noncanonical mechanism for stimulating retrograde transport. Using a chemically inducible system for dispersing individual organelles, we show that perinuclear localization of multiple compartments potentiates oxidative stress–induced gene expression, with distinct genes depending on inputs from either combinations of organelles or individual compartments. Together, these findings implicate positioning of multiple membrane-bound compartments in gene expression regulation and identify coordinated organelle trafficking by dynein as an additional regulatory layer in the cellular stress response.

title: Environment-adaptive molecular neural networks enabled by heterogeneous threshold DNA neuron
abstract: Molecular neural networks enable autonomous information processing in biochemical environments, yet most existing DNA-based implementations operate with fixed connectivity after assembly, limiting their ability to adapt network topology to changing environments. Here, we report an environment-adaptive molecular neural network enabled by DNA neurons with sequence-programmed, heterogeneous activation thresholds. These neurons incorporate triplex-based proton-gated DNA switches with tunable pH-response windows, which regulate the accessibility of toehold and recognition domains to switch pre-encoded weighted connections between inactive and signal-propagating states, thereby reconfiguring network connectivity without changing molecular composition. We demonstrate this principle in a DNA neural network that processes 64-bit inputs, where environmental acidification activates dormant neurons and reconfigures the computational topology from a sparse convolutional neural network for coarse two-class categorization into a fully connected neural network for fine-grained discrimination among four distinct patterns. Our results establish DNA-based neural circuits capable of adapting their computational architecture to environmental cues, offering a framework for molecular information processing in fluctuating biochemical environments.

title: Posttranscriptional regulation by TIA1 and TIAL1 controls the transcriptional program enforcing T cell quiescence
abstract: Immune protection against infections relies on long-term maintenance of a highly diversified naïve T cell repertoire. Transcription factors cooperate to enforce T cell metabolic quiescence and maintenance. However, less is known about the posttranscriptional networks that preserve naïve T cells. Here, we describe the RNA binding proteins T cell antigen 1 (TIA1) and TIA-like 1 (TIAL1) as key promoters of CD4 and CD8 T cell quiescence. T cells deficient in TIA1 and TIAL1 undergo premature T cell activation, exhaustion, and death in the absence of cognate antigens. Mechanistically, TIA1 and TIAL1 promote the messenger RNA translation of quiescence-associated transcription factors such as forkhead box P1, lymphoid enhancer factor 1, and T cell factor 1 to restrain homeostatic T cell proliferation and activation. In summary, our study highlights a previously unrecognized dependency on posttranscriptional gene regulation by TIA1 and TIAL1 for implementing the quiescent transcriptional programs for long survival of T cells.

title: Spatially multiplexed microneedle biosensors for low-abundance protein biomarker monitoring in dermal interstitial fluid
abstract: Microneedle (MN) biosensors offer a minimally invasive approach for molecular analysis of interstitial fluid (ISF), but multiplexed detection of low-abundance protein biomarkers remains limited by poor spatial functionalization and analytical sensitivity. Here, we introduce a high-resolution transfer-printing strategy that functionalizes individual MNs with distinct biorecognition elements on a single patch, enabling simultaneous capture and on-needle analysis of multiple protein biomarkers. Combined with plasmonic-enhanced ultrabright fluorescent nanolabels, the platform enables sensitive multiplexed quantification of low-abundance immune and kidney function biomarkers in mouse models and human subjects. ISF biomarker concentrations showed strong correlations with corresponding plasma levels, supporting the physiological relevance of MN-based measurements. The MN patch enabled painless, blood-free sampling with rapid skin recovery and no irritation. This scalable platform provides a versatile approach for minimally invasive biomarker profiling and may facilitate frequent disease monitoring and timely clinical decision-making.

title: Small and large earthquakes driven by inelastic deformation in weak fault zones
abstract: Earthquakes manifest across a wide range of magnitudes, corresponding to a diversity of rupture sizes and amounts of slip. Classical earthquake models consider rupture processes solely on the fault plane, but the surrounding fault zone rocks can host inelastic deformation. Here, we show, via a dynamic seismic cycle model incorporating spontaneous fault zone evolution through damage and healing, that both small and large earthquakes on a single fault emerge naturally from the interplay of fault slip and fault zone inelastic deformation. Our simulations reproduce key observations: frequency-magnitude distribution consistent with the Gutenberg-Richter law, magnitude-invariant static stress drop, and the dual-regime scaling of fracture energy density with earthquake magnitude. The results underscore the coevolution of earthquakes and fault zone damage as a fundamental mechanism governing earthquake behavior in nature. Fault zone deformation causing multiscale seismicity indicates that continuous monitoring of fault zone material properties may reveal fault stress states and earthquake potential.

title: Intestinal BMP SMADs impart the mid-villus pattern through a transcription factor cascade mechanism
abstract: Differentiated cells of the intestinal villus are not a monolith of equivalent cell types, but an exquisitely patterned continuum of transdifferentiated cells with evolving functions. Villus patterning requires BMP signaling; however, the transcriptional regulators downstream of BMP are unclear. We find that SMAD1 and SMAD5 are necessary for middle villus pattern. Spatial transcriptomics reveal a homeotic-like shift in the villus pattern of SMAD1/SMAD5 mutants, with the villus bottom and tip domains expanding at the expense of the middle. Disruption of mid-villus patterning corresponds to decreases in lipid uptake and runted pups in SMAD1/5 mutants. Unexpectedly, SMAD1/5 is not required for regulation of villus tip identity, which is dependent on SMAD4. Epigenomics approaches reveal a mechanism in which SMAD1/5 directly activate some mid-villus genes and control others via a transcription factor hierarchy, including TBX3. An intestine-specific TBX3 mutant phenocopied the SMAD1/5 mutant. These findings contribute mechanistic details to intestinal villus patterning.

title: Unblockable communication with gravity
abstract: All modern wireless communication technologies are based on electromagnetism. However, electromagnetic signals are readily susceptible to screening and blocking, so their availability cannot be guaranteed in adverse environments. This raises a fundamental question: Can information be transmitted through an unblockable channel? Here, we show that gravity, under physically realistic conditions, offers such a path. We propose and implement a wireless communication protocol in which a broadcaster encodes a binary message by moving a mass, while a receiver detects the resulting gravitational signal with a gravimeter. We validate this scheme experimentally, successfully transmitting a gravitational message a distance of ≈0.7 meters through a brick wall at a rate of 1 bit per minute. These results establish gravity as a viable platform for practically unblockable communication.

abstract:

Here, we developed a destructive technology that does not require external photo-, electro-, or heat energy input, relying simply on Fenton-like cycles (peroxymonosulfate activation) under nanometric spatial confinement. title: Engineering interfacial nucleation and growth for long-life, ultrahigh-rate anode-free sodium batteries
abstract: The practical application of anode-free sodium batteries (AFSBs) is limited by the poor reversibility of sodium plating and stripping on current collectors. Here, we show that conventional graphite unexpectedly regulates sodium plating and stripping through a dynamic, interactive interface that enables multidimensional charge transport. This behavior arises from the combination of ultrafast mixed ion-electron transport, reversible ether solvent cointercalation, and the anisotropic flake architecture of graphite, which together promote efficient charge exchange and edge-dominant nucleation. The resulting adaptive interface forms an ultrathin, mechanically robust SEI that stabilizes sodium plating and stripping across a wide current density range (1C to 10C). Ampere hour–level anode-free pouch cells based on this design exhibit an initial Coulombic efficiency of 92.3%, retain 84.9% capacity after 1100 cycles at 3C, and display exceptional safety characteristics, including minimal temperature rise at high rates and no thermal runaway during nail penetration. These results establish a platform for controlling interfacial metal nucleation and growth in AFSBs.

title: Cortical population codes for embedding sensory inputs into the prior context
abstract: According to theories of the brain as a predictive network, perceptual decisions result from integrating incoming sensory inputs with prior experience. A neuronal population implementing this form of computation must not only retain information about past events but also combine this information with current sensory evidence. To examine how this integration occurs, we recorded extracellular activity from both primary sensory cortex and a target frontal region in rats performing stimulus categorization. Psychophysical analysis showed that judgments were history dependent. Sensory cortex represented the current stimulus largely independently of prior stimuli and failed to account for the history dependence seen in behavior. In contrast, frontal cortex embedded current input within a representation of prior sensory information, with the two variables aligned along partially overlapping coding dimensions. This mechanism predicted choice bias in the behavioral data and involved a disproportionate contribution from putative fast-spiking units. These findings suggest distinct contributions of sensory and frontal cortical regions to predictive processing and point to frontal cortex as a potential site where sensory history may be integrated with incoming evidence to influence perceptual decisions.

title: GenNA: Conditional generation of nucleotide sequences guided by natural language annotations
abstract: Deciphering the mapping between biomolecular sequences and complex biological functions is a central challenge in genomics. While existing generative nucleotide models capture sequence distributions, they lack explicit access to gene-associated biological semantics, limiting semantics-guided design. Here, we present GenNA, a generative nucleotide foundation model guided by natural language annotations. Pretrained on a multimodal nucleotide-text corpus spanning 2221 eukaryotic species (∼416 billion characters), GenNA internalizes relationships between sequence syntax and functional semantics within a unified autoregressive framework. Without explicit rule-based supervision, GenNA yields distinguishable perplexity responses to sequence-annotation mismatches, mutational variants, and species-label perturbations. Furthermore, across diverse generation tasks, GenNA produces statistically plausible nucleotide sequences consistent with target semantics, structural constraints, and species contexts. Overall, GenNA provides a versatile framework for controllable nucleotide generation, establishing a practical route to integrate functional descriptions with sequence design.

title: Seasonal effects of simulated marine heatwaves on temperature-dependent growth performance
abstract: Marine heatwaves (MHWs) are increasingly longer and more frequent globally, but the cumulative impacts of multiple events on organism performance remain poorly understood. Using thermal performance models, we simulate the effects of simple seasonal MHW scenarios on the predicted growth of 36 mariculture species across the western Pacific Ocean. Simulations suggested that winter MHWs could generally benefit growth, while summer MHWs produced generally negative impacts, especially at higher latitudes where species experience summer growth periods. When combined, winter and summer MHW scenarios indicated a cumulative negative effect for most species. Vulnerability was highest at the warm- and cold-range edges of species’ distributions. These simulations suggest that temperature-dependent growth may be closely linked to the seasonal timing and frequency of extreme events, with multi-season MHWs posing potential challenges for mariculture species in the future. Our simulations highlight the importance of considering multi-season impacts in climate adaptation strategies.

title: Pten regulates neurogenic radial glia lineage progression and tunes neocortical astrocyte production in Mapk1/3 -dependent pathway
abstract:
The cerebral cortex consists of immense numbers of diverse cell types derived from radial glial progenitor (RGP) cells. How RGPs generate appropriate quantities of distinct cell types to safeguard a brain of correct size is not well understood. However, genetic aberrations in human, including mutations in
                    PTEN
                    , lead to cortical malformation such as macrocephaly, albeit with unknown etiology. Here, we used mosaic analysis with double markers (MADM)–based clonal analysis and single-cell phenotyping to decipher the role of
                    Pten
                    in RGP lineage progression during cortical ontogeny. Although neurogenic RGP lineage progression was altered and projection neuron production doubled in the absence of
                    Pten
                    , cortical astrogenesis was drastically increased. Through epistasis experiments, we show that the loss of
                    Pten
                    uncouples astrogenesis from essential growth factor signaling hubs, funneling into MAPK (mitogen-activated protein kinase). Collectively, our results suggest that
                    Pten
                    regulates RGP lineage progression with distinct sequential functions in corticogenesis to safeguard the emergence of a correctly sized cortex.

title: Somatostatin 6, a master maternal mRNA driving early development
abstract:
Vertebrate genomes contain six somatostatin (SST) gene family members, of which only SST1 and cortistatin (CORT or SST2) are present in mammalian genomes. These genes encode peptides that predominantly exert inhibitory effects on growth, metabolism, reproduction, and the immune system. However, their roles in nonmammalian vertebrates remain poorly understood. Here, we examined zebrafish
                    sst6
                    (
                    sst6.2
                    ) loss of function and discovered that maternally inherited
                    sst6
                    mRNA is vital for embryonic cleavage and gastrulation. Its absence impaired calcium release from stores, calcium wave propagation, F-actin assembly, furrow ingression, and overall embryonic development. Moreover, maternal
                    sst6
                    mRNA is crucial for degrading maternal mRNAs, for calcium-dependent phosphorylation of Stat3 and Smad1/5, and for activating zygotic gene transcription, including
                    pou5f1
                    ,
                    nanog
                    , and
                    sox2
                    , as well as downstream pluripotency factors. This suggests that maternal
                    sst6
                    mRNA acts as a master regulator of early development, a function likely conserved in other vertebrates.

title: Spheroid-laden hydrogels with dual biomimetic intra- and perispheroidal niches for enhanced bone healing
abstract:
Stem cell spheroid–hydrogel platforms offer promise for bone defect repair, but implantation-associated oxidative stress, poor vascular ingrowth, and insufficient osteogenic cues limit their clinical translation. Here, we developed dual-NICHE (dual niche-instructive construct for bone healing and engraftment), a gelatin methacryloyl hydrogel containing human adipose–derived stem cell spheroids with spatially distinct intra-/perispheroidal niches. Within a single construct, these two niches provide complementary functions to simultaneously address the key bottlenecks in bone regeneration. The intraspheroidal niche incorporated bone morphogenetic protein-2–immobilized fibers to promote osteogenic differentiation, whereas the perispheroidal matrix contained Sr
                    2+
                    –tannic acid nanoparticles (NPs). Upon implantation, the NPs mitigated oxidative stress and supported vascular infiltration. Concurrently, the osteogenic cue promoted differentiation, while the NPs facilitated mineral nucleation and growth, as further supported by molecular dynamics simulations. Together, this spatial integration enhanced vascularized bone formation with a bone volume fraction of ∼13.5% using only 5208 cells per defect in a mouse calvarial model, providing a potentially translatable framework for bone regeneration.

title: A floss-based platform for native gingival crevicular fluid analysis enables noninvasive systemic and oral health monitoring
abstract:
Gingival crevicular fluid (GCF) is a serum-derived biofluid in the gingival sulcus, offering access to systemic metabolic signals and localized oral inflammation. However, its diagnostic utility remains underutilized because native submicroliter volumes cannot be analyzed without specimen pooling and reagent-mediated dilution. We overcome this barrier using a floss-based platform that enables on-demand GCF analysis during routine flossing. The device integrates a dual-fiber system exploiting shear-dependent property for efficient mobilization, liquid-bridge retention, a pyramidal microfluidic sensor stack, and real-time electrofluidic volume correction. This architecture supports multiplexed electrochemical quantification of glucose, uric acid (UA), pH, and H
                    2
                    O
                    2
                    from native GCF within minutes. In human studies, GCF glucose and UA correlated with capillary blood (glucose:
                    r
                     = 0.89, UA:
                    r
                     = 0.78). Site-specific pH and H
                    2
                    O
                    2
                    levels differentiated inflamed from healthy periodontal sites, correlating with probing pocket depth. By converting a daily hygiene practice into a dual tool for systemic and oral health monitoring, this platform advances comorbidity management for chronic disease populations.

title: A state-dependent neural circuit resolves approach-avoidance conflict
abstract:
To survive, animals must balance opportunity and risk, yet how internal motivational state biases this trade-off remains poorly understood. Here, we show that hunger gates avoidance of a noxious stimulus in
                    Drosophila
                    to enable food approach under conflict. Using a behavioral assay in which flies must cross an electric shock barrier to reach food, we find that starvation promotes shock tolerance only when food-related olfactory cues are present. This state- and context-dependent behavioral shift is mediated by a defined neuromodulatory circuit. Leucokinin neurons encode hunger and convey this information to PV5K1 lateral horn output neurons, which integrate internal state signals with food odor cues and suppress shock-responsive FB2B neurons in the ventral fan-shaped body. Accordingly, electric shock-evoked activity in FB2B neurons is suppressed in starved flies exposed to food cues. These findings identify a circuit mechanism by which motivational state gates aversive processing to bias action selection towards goal-directed behavior.

title: Structure and dynamics of the cellular belt driving bacterial gliding motility
abstract:
Various bacteria move on solid surfaces through a process known as gliding motility. Gliding bacteria of the phylum
                    Bacteroidota
                    are major ecological players in a wide variety of niches, as commensals or as pathogens. They use the type IX secretion system (T9SS) to transport adhesins to the cell surface, which then travel in a helical pattern to propel the cell. Here, we purified the filament that drives adhesin helical movement and uncovered its structure by cryo–electron microscopy. Live imaging showed that this outer membrane–associated periplasmic belt, built from T9SS core components, is powered by T9SS molecular motors. This structure functions as a moving walkway that conveys outer membrane β barrel protein–adhesin complexes, therefore coupling motor activity to directional surface translation. This study reveals a unique machinery coupling protein secretion with rapid directed movement of membrane-embedded protein complexes.

title: Membrane-confined self-assembly enables localized bioorthogonal prodrug activation and selective cancer therapy
abstract:
Bioorthogonal prodrug activation offers a promising approach for site-specific drug release, significantly reducing the systemic toxicity associated with conventional chemotherapy. However, challenges remain in precisely controlling prodrug activation at the target site while maintaining optimal selectivity, reactivity, and potency. Here, we report a dual-targeting peptide, TzFFY
                    p
                    HH, that integrates on-membrane enzyme-instructed self-assembly (EISA) with bioorthogonal chemistry to enable selective chemotherapy. Exploiting the overexpression of alkaline phosphatase (ALP) and programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) on cancer cells, TzFFY
                    p
                    HH selectively anchors and self-assembles on the cancer cell membrane, enriching tetrazine (Tz) handles that act as bioorthogonal reactors to activate a
                    trans
                    -cyclooctene (TCO)-caged prodrug (TCO-Dox) for precise drug release. Upon topical administration, TzFFY
                    p
                    HH forms a hydrogel at subcutaneous tumor sites, enabling in situ prodrug activation for effective tumor inhibition. Notably, this localized chemotherapy elicits a potent antitumor immune response, which, when combined with anti-programmed death-1 antibody (αPD-1), synergistically potentiates therapeutic outcomes. By coupling supramolecular self-assembly with bioorthogonal reactivity on the cell membrane, this work establishes a chemically programmable platform for spatiotemporally controlled prodrug activation and provides a general strategy for integrating localized chemotherapy with immunotherapy.

title: Beyond metabolites: A wearable biointerface integrating antibody and aptamer probes for the real-time tracking of proteins in vivo
abstract: Continuous monitoring of protein biomarkers could transform the management of acute and chronic diseases. Despite tremendous potential, wearable health monitors have remained largely limited to metabolites and small molecules. A key challenge is the limited availability of biointerfaces that reversibly track low-abundance proteins in vivo without user intervention. Here, we present the Differential Aptalyzer, a minimally invasive hydrogel microneedle platform for continuous monitoring of proteins in skin interstitial fluid. The platform combines high-affinity antibodies for selective target capture with aptamers for reversible electrochemical signal transduction. When integrated into a differential electrochemical chip and pulse-assisted sensor regeneration, this approach enables continuous monitoring of proteins in a wearable format. Using cardiac troponin I (cTnI) as a clinically relevant model analyte, Differential Aptalyzer offers a broad dynamic range (0.003 to 0.640 nanograms per milliliter) and strong specificity against interfering proteins. This platform reliably tracks both rising and falling exogenous cTnI levels injected into healthy mice, as well as endogenously elevated cTnI in a double-knockout mouse model of coronary artery disease, demonstrating its capability in continuous protein monitoring and identifying coronary artery disease cohorts.

title: Cross-domain encoding models reveal shared and domain-specific neural representations across language and mathematics
abstract: Whether language and mathematics rely on shared or distinct neural representations remains unresolved in cognitive neuroscience. Here, we combined latent features from a large language model with functional magnetic resonance imaging encoding models to test cross-domain generalization in 32 participants performing sentence comprehension and calculation tasks. Cross-domain prediction identified cortical regions showing partially shared representations, most consistently in the left area 55b, while control analyses suggested that these effects could not be fully explained by low-level visual or task-general factors. Domain-specificity contrasts revealed stronger language-related prediction in the left superior temporal sulcus and angular gyrus and math-related prediction in the left precentral sulcus and bilateral intraparietal sulci. Model-weight analyses revealed distinct weight profiles associated with shared and domain-specific prediction patterns. Cross-domain regions also exhibited task-dependent functional coupling with language- and math-related networks. Together, these findings suggest that language and mathematics involve partially shared neural representations alongside domain-specific cortical organization, helping reconcile previous contrasting views on their neural basis.

title: TRIM28-mediated SUMOylation of ERG at K389 conveys PARP inhibitor resistance by inhibiting 53BP1 expression in CRPC
Tracking local chemomechanics in graphite–silicon composite electrodes
abstract: Operando 4D imaging reveals how local ionic pathways govern activity in graphite–silicon battery electrodes.

title: In Situ STEM Imaging of Colloidal Crystals Based on Programmable Atom Equivalents
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract It is challenging to image the assembly of colloidal crystals composed of programmable atom equivalents (PAEs) using electron microscopy (EM). PAEs typically consist of nanoparticle cores densely functionalized with radially oriented DNA shells, which assemble in the liquid phase via DNA bonds. EM requires high-vacuum conditions, and electron beams can damage soft materials like nucleic acids. Here, we present a liquid-phase scanning transmission electron microscopy (LPSTEM) method for imaging PAEs composed of ∼5 nm gold nanoparticle cores in solution, enabling the direct investigation of their DNA-directed assembly processes. This system is particularly well-suited for in situ studies of soft-matter dynamics because the gold nanoparticle cores provide strong electron contrast. Using a nanofluidic liquid cell, the nucleation and growth of PAE assemblies, governed via the principles of colloidal crystal engineering with DNA, were directly observed. Imaging conditions were established to resolve colloidal assemblies in liquid while also characterizing electron-beam-induced damage under both conventional STEM and STEM-in-SEM conditions. Quantitative image analysis reveals changes in local coordination during crystal growth and subsequent beam-induced dissociation. Complementary ex situ simulations corroborate that radiolytic species generated in the buffer are major contributors to beam-induced damage. Together, these results establish a versatile and accessible platform for probing the in situ dynamics of PAE assembly in liquids, with broad applicability to the study of other soft nanomaterials and composites relevant to sensing, actuation, energy storage, catalysis, and medicine.

title: Hierarchical interfacial anchoring for durable perovskite solar cells
abstract:
Although inverted perovskite solar cells now deliver certified efficiencies approaching their single-junction limits, their practical deployment remains constrained by the thermo-mechanical fragility of buried interfaces under realistic temperature fluctuations. Here, we identify thermo-mechanically driven, stress-accumulation-dominated adhesion failure at self-assembled monolayer-based buried interfaces as a critical failure mode in inverted perovskite solar cells. To address this issue, we propose an interfacial robustness design strategy based on a homometallic halide pretreatment, which constructs a chemically compatible and highly anchorable interfacial environment on transparent conductive oxides to guide the ordered assembly of SAMs. This interfacial treatment increases the density of surface hydroxyl species and enables hierarchical multipoint interfacial anchoring dominated by metal-oxygen coordination, with Cl
                    −
                    induced hydrogen-bonding interactions acting cooperatively, thereby enhancing anchoring robustness and improving tolerance to thermo-mechanical stress accumulation. With this interfacial strategy, the devices achieve a power conversion efficiency of 27.3% (26.9% certified) and retain 94% of their initial efficiency after 400 temperature cycles between −40 and 85°C (ISOS-T-3). These results demonstrate that rational regulation of buried interfacial anchoring architectures can simultaneously enhance device efficiency and long-term operational reliability, offering a viable pathway toward high-efficiency and durable perovskite photovoltaics.

title: Expert operating skills learning-based intelligent shared control method for a CT-guided percutaneous biopsy robot
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Accurate and minimally invasive percutaneous biopsy is critical for early lung cancer diagnosis, yet conventional manual procedures suffer from repeated radiation exposure, high reliance on doctor expertise, and risk of tissue injury. This study presents a 5 degree-of-freedom robotic system combined with an intelligent shared control framework guided by expert skills learning. Expert skills were modeled using a variational autoencoder–hidden Markov model to segment latent procedural phases, and dynamic motion primitives reconstructed representative expert trajectories. These learned skills were integrated into a phase-adaptive shared controller, enabling online modulation of impedance and trajectory parameters. Both phantom and in vivo porcine experiments validated the system’s feasibility, safety, and accuracy, with animal experiment studies confirming minimal tissue trauma and stable physiological responses. Compared with manual, leader–follower, and admittance control methods, the intelligent shared control substantially reduced force fluctuations and trajectory deviations.

title: Large language models' complicit responses to illicit instructions across socio-legal contexts
source: Scientific community and society : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Large language models may facilitate unlawful activities, yet this risk remains underexplored in studies assessing illicit-content recognition or narrow categories of illicit scenarios. We define complicit facilitation as model guidance that assists users with illicit instructions. To assess it, we develop a legally-informed, automated pipeline grounded in real-world cases and legal frameworks, and introduce EVIL, a benchmark covering 269 illicit scenarios and 50 illicit intents across Chinese and United States legal contexts. Evaluations indicate that complicit facilitation is widespread across models, with legal warnings and lawful alternatives often omitted. Risks vary across socio-legal contexts and are elevated for crimes against societal interests, non-violent offenses, and intents involving subjective motives or deceptive justifications. Models provide more complicit assistance when instructions describe users as older adults, racial minorities, non-religious individuals, or workers in lower-prestige occupations. Existing open-source safety benchmarks and alignment datasets offer limited coverage and mitigation of these risks.

title: A spectral framework for revealing the hidden low-dimensional structure in stochastic reaction networks
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Stochastic reaction networks govern noise-driven dynamics in systems ranging from gene regulation to cellular signalling and population processes. Yet their high dimensionality and sensitivity to initial states obscure transient mechanisms and limit reliable inference from experimental data. Here, we show that stochastic reaction networks in biological systems often exhibit dominant low-dimensional spectral structure that shapes their dynamics. We develop a spectral framework based on the stochastic Koopman operator that identifies these dominant dynamical modes directly from simulated trajectories, yielding reduced representations with computable error bounds. This reduction enables accurate analytical descriptions of the time evolution of moments, parameter sensitivities, and cross-spectral densities, while achieving order-of-magnitude computational gains relative to standard simulation-based methods. Applied to synthetic gene circuits, our framework reveals the spectral organisation of stochastic oscillators, enables systematic comparison of competing intracellular controllers, and facilitates inference of initial-state distributions from single-cell snapshot population data collected over time. Together, these results establish a principled spectral description of stochastic reaction dynamics and provide a foundation for analysing and inferring high-dimensional noise-driven biological systems.

title: Viscoelasticity of synthetic antigen presenting cells reprograms T cell metabolism for TCR-T cell manufacturing and therapy
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Adoptive T cell receptor (TCR)–based immunotherapy offers a powerful strategy to target solid tumors. However, how the physical properties of the antigen-presenting interface regulate T cell metabolic programming remains poorly defined. Here we develop synthetic viscoelastic activating cells (SynVAC), artificial antigen-presenting cells whose stress-relaxation kinetics are chemically tuned independently of stiffness and of peptide–MHC (pMHC) and co-stimulatory ligand density. SynVAC-pMHC provides a defined, scalable platform that outperforms monocyte-derived dendritic cells to enrich antigen-specific CD8+ T cells. Fast-relaxing SynVAC-pMHC amplifies TCR signaling and mTOR activity, drives metabolic changes, and programs antigen-specific T cells toward an energetically favorable state with improved memory-like features after expansion. TCR-T cells expanded using fast-relaxing SynVAC-pMHC exhibit superior persistence and durable antitumor activity in melanoma and ovarian cancer models. These results establish cell-mimetic viscoelasticity as a key biophysical cue governing T cell metabolism and differentiation and offer a fully synthetic strategy for manufacturing potent TCR-T cells.

title: Fully stretchable moisture-electric generators with peak milliamp-scale output via conformationally adaptive ionic hydrogels for wearables
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Moisture-electric generators (MEGs) that harvest ambient or physiological moisture offer a promising route to self-powered wearable and deformable electronics. However, their practical applications are hindered by insufficient moisture-responsive output and unstable performance under strain. Here, we report a fully stretchable MEG with peak milliamp-scale output for self-powered epidermal sensing, enabled by an in situ formed, conformationally adaptive hygroscopic ionic hydrogel adhesively integrated between two stretchable asymmetric-porosity styrene–ethylene–butylene–styrene (SEBS) composite electrodes. The hydrogel encodes charge-selective pathways that drive quasi-two-dimensional, oppositely directed counter-ion migration, enabling rapid ion separation and high ionic conductivity (8.1 S m−1). Its reversible helix–coil transitions preserve ion transport under strain by dissipating strain energy across multiple scales. Coupled with SEBS composite electrodes that facilitate continuous moisture delivery and reliable electrical contact during stretching, the device achieves a peak current density of 1.1 mA cm−2 upon moisture activation, while remaining fully stretchable up to 400% strain and stable at 200% strain over 1000 cycles with minimal output degradation. We show its use as a self-powered, deep-learning-assisted skin-hydration sensing platform, achieving 98% classification accuracy during extended on-body operation with smartphone feedback. This approach to designing deformation-tolerant MEGs will enable next-generation self-powered, skin-conformal healthcare electronics.

title: Highly elastic ceramic fibers with a high tensile fracture strain
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Ceramics are prized for high strength, but their inherent brittleness has long been a fundamental bottleneck. Here, we overcome this limitation by reporting macroscopically elastic SiO2 fibers that achieve a high tensile fracture strain of 13.59% while maintaining high strength of 1.22 GPa. This is enabled via a metal-coordination-mediated topology reconstruction strategy. title: Controlling intertwined electronic orders in FeSe with exfoliation
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Controlling intertwined electronic orders in two-dimensional superconductors offers an effective route to answering fundamental questions and engineering new quantum devices. However, tuning the balance between competing orders typically requires complex chemistry, strain, or interface engineering. Here, we show that a pristine alternative is the dimensional reduction of the unconventional superconductor FeSe. Exfoliation suppresses the bulk electronic nematic response and switches the superconducting symmetry from bulk s-wave to d-wave-dominant. Transport, electron microscopy, and Raman spectroscopy establish the substantial weakening of nematic order in thin flakes. To probe superconductivity, we perform angle-dependent Andreev reflection spectroscopy on pristine crystal edges. As the junction’s orientation is rotated, the spectra evolve from zero-energy bound states to coherence peaks. The injection angle, field, and temperature dependence, along with theoretical modeling, confirm that exfoliation switches the superconducting symmetry. Our results suggest a versatile superconducting platform for engineering quantum orders and provide insights into the underlying pairing mechanisms.

title: Efficient n–i–p all-perovskite tandem solar cells enabled by interconnection layer engineering
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: All-perovskite tandem solar cells promise ultrahigh efficiencies, yet monolithic devices have been realized predominantly in the p–i–n architecture because n–i–p integration imposes stringent materials constraints. The preformed wide-bandgap top subcell and its hole-selective contact must withstand bottom-subcell fabrication temperatures, limiting material choices. Here we address this challenge using a 2.0 eV Cs-based all-inorganic wide-bandgap subcell and an additive-free P3HT hole-selective contact whose molecular organization is reconfigured by MeO-2PACz. This interfacial modification enhances P3HT ordering and promotes efficient hole extraction, alleviating a transport bottleneck in monolithic n–i–p tandems. Coupled with PCBM modification of the ALD-SnO₂ electron-selective contact in the 1.55 eV bottom subcell, this architecture enables balanced carrier coupling across the interconnection layer, suppresses charge accumulation and voltage loss, and delivers efficiencies of 25.3% and 24.7% for 0.096 cm² and 1.045 cm² devices, respectively, with a stabilized power output of 24.4%. Additionally, combining the n–i–p double-junction device with a p–i–n narrow-bandgap subcell (1.25 eV) yields a four-terminal triple-junction device with 28% efficiency. To our knowledge, this is the first report of an n–i–p double-junction device exceeding 25% efficiency and an n–i–p-based four-terminal triple-junction device reaching 28%, advancing perovskite tandem technology.

title: Opposite migrations of Pacific and Atlantic tropical cyclones during the Medieval Warm Period
source: Earth and environmental sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Whether the recent poleward migration of tropical cyclones (TCs) reflects anthropogenic warming or natural variability remains unresolved. Here, we use paleoclimate evidence to reconstruct TC migration across the western North Pacific (WNP) and North Atlantic (NA) during the natural-forcing-dominated Medieval Warm Period (MWP, ~1000–1300 CE). We integrate a paleo-TC record from the WNP generated in this study with existing records to produce a basin-scale reconstruction of TC migration across the two major TC basins. We show that TC migration during the MWP was strongly basin dependent, with a poleward shift in the WNP but an equatorward shift in the NA, driven by differences in sea surface temperature forcing between the two basins. This contrasting behavior indicates that internal variability can drive opposing migration responses across basins under quasi‑equilibrium conditions. In contrast, recent decades show a synchronous poleward shift in both basins. We suggest that the modern basin-wide coherence reflects increasingly dominant anthropogenic forcing that overwhelms natural, regionally specific feedbacks. Our results provide a new benchmark for attributing observed TC migration and constraining future projections of TC risk.

title: High-κ bismuth molybdate single-crystalline dielectric for high-temperature two-dimensional transistors
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Two-dimensional (2D) semiconductors represent promising alternatives to traditional silicon for next-generation electronic devices. However, there are still significant challenges in high-temperature 2D electronic devices integrated by existing high-κ dielectrics. Here, we report a BiOCl-assisted chemical vapor deposition method to synthesize high-quality bismuth molybdate (Bi2MoO6) single-crystalline nanosheets with controllable thickness and good thermal stability. High-κ (54.2) nature is identified within as-grown Bi2MoO6 nanosheets, with wide bandgap (∼3.85 eV) and large breakdown field strength (∼3.9 MV/cm) at room temperature. As results, Bi2MoO6 top-gate MoS2 transistor exhibits a negligible hysteresis and an average subthreshold swing less than 100 mV dec−1 within 3 orders of magnitude of current range, as well as excellent operational stability. Moreover, the transistor maintains a high on/off current ratio of > 104 and a hysteresis of less than 10 mV/(MV cm−1) at the high temperature up to 500 K, meeting the requirements of high-temperature electronic devices. The inverter with Bi2MoO6 gate dielectric is also achieved, yielding a high gain of 86.1 at supply voltage of 5 V. This work enriches the high-κ gate dielectric family and provides considerable application potential in high-temperature electronic devices.

title: Hyperelastic microfibers as bioinspired proprioceptive artificial muscles
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Skeletal muscles combine forceful contraction with built-in sensing of their own length and movement, known as proprioception. Reproducing this combination in soft artificial muscles remains difficult, because added sensors often reduce actuation performance, complicate fabrication or limit miniaturization. In natural muscle, specialized sensory fibers are embedded alongside, and mechanically coupled to, the force-generating fibers. Inspired by this arrangement, we pair a hyperelastic, highly stretchable fluid channel with a stiffer, off-center optical core inside a single thin fiber. When liquid is pumped in, the channel wall undergoes a shape bifurcation: a localized bulge forms and propagates along the fiber. Because the core resists stretching, the bulge bends the fiber into a contracting coil, while the core also reports the fiber’s shape through the light it transmits. Here we show that such fibers, produced continuously by a scalable drawing process, act as artificial muscles that sense their own contraction and stretching, supporting self-monitoring movement in soft robots.

title: Nanofriction strengthened mechanically adaptive electrolytes for safe lithium metal batteries
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The expanding application of lithium metal batteries in emerging fields such as unmanned aerial vehicles and humanoid robots exposes them to heightened risks of mechanical abuse, which has become a critical factor contributing to safety failures. To address this predicament, we design a mechanically intelligent responsive multifunctional electrolyte using a “nano-friction-strengthening” strategy to dynamically reinforce its mechanical robustness. The high-polarity carbonate solvents spontaneously infiltrate the hydroxyl-rich poly(hydroxyethyl methacrylate-diethyl allyphosphonate) shell and induce a hydrogen-bond-driven, self-regulated swelling response that enables uniform nanoparticle dispersion. Under impact, the intimate interfacial contact between core-shell nanoparticles instantaneously activates a dense network of dynamic hydrogen bonds within the swollen shell, boosting interparticle friction and adhesion. This molecularly orchestrated nano-friction-strengthening effect endows the electrolyte with impact hardening, driving a 160-fold surge in viscosity and delivering highly effective mechanical protection. Consequently, the electrolyte attenuates impact forces by 73.1%, enabling single Li‖LiFePO4 pouch cells to endure impact without short-circuiting. Beyond mechanical reinforcement, the phosphate-ester groups in nanoparticles suppress exothermic chain reactions, ensuring safe operation during nail-penetration and ballistic tests in ampere-hour-scale Li‖LiFePO4 cells.

title: Twist-engineered arbitrary polarization detection for intelligent polarimetric sensing
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Twist-photonics offers a powerful route to engineer light-matter interactions beyond conventional planar architectures. Although twist-photonic platforms, including twist-stacked metasurfaces, van der Waals (vdW) materials and photonic crystals have successfully engineered chiral optical responses, anomalous dispersion and high-Q localized modes, most platforms remain passive. Their translation into on-chip optoelectronic sensing is hindered by an intrinsic trade-off: photosensitive absorbers can quench twist-engineered resonances, whereas passive twist-photonic modes often couple inefficiently to active photocarrier-generation regions. Here, we report an emerging twist-photonic paradigm that integrates anisotropic metasurfaces with anisotropic black phosphorus (BP). Coupled to a vectorial cavity, this twisted stack produces quasi-pure circular-polarization photoresponses and enables arbitrary polarization selectivity across the full Poincaré sphere at multiple wavelengths. Then, we establish an ultra-compact on-chip full-Stokes polarimeter using only two metasurface-BP twisted stacks, achieving high-accuracy full-Stokes reconstruction with a root-mean-square error below 1.3%, and the highest responsivity among reported vdW material-based full-Stokes polarimeters. We further implement an in-sensor kernel matrix that directly maps polarization states into synaptic weights for polarization-programmable multimodal convolutional image processing, reducing electrical switching energy by 1 to 3 orders of magnitude and reconfiguration latency by 2 to 4 orders of magnitude, as the array scales from the 10k-pixel to megapixel level.

title: Wafer-scale thin-film PZT photonic integrated circuits enabling multi-terabit optical transmission
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Meeting the escalating demand for high-capacity optical communication requires electro-optic (EO) photonic integrated circuits (PICs) that combine terabit-scale capacity, energy efficiency and scalable manufacturing. Here we establish thin-film lead zirconate titanate (PZT) as a wafer-scale photonic integration platform on 8-inch SiO2/Si substrates. Uniform, high-quality PZT thin films are prepared using a scalable chemical solution deposition–magnetron sputtering process, followed by a deep ultraviolet (DUV) stepper-based wafer-scale manufacturing process. Low propagation loss and low in-plane optical anisotropy provide the precise phase control and layout flexibility required for large-scale integration, supporting high-performance arrayed waveguide gratings (AWGs). Ferroelectric-domain engineering activates the strong Pockels response, enabling Mach–Zehnder modulators (MZMs) with a half-wave voltage–length product (VπL) of 1.19 V·cm, a broadband EO response extending to 70 GHz and data rates up to 224 Gbps. We further demonstrate a monolithically integrated 16-channel wavelength-division multiplexing transmitter supporting 3.2-Tbps-class optical interconnects. These results establish PZT as a practical wafer-scale platform for multi-terabit photonic systems.

title: Pathway-dependent chiral toroid self-assembly and topological transformations based on large π-conjugated dipeptides
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Rational introduction of large π-conjugated moieties to peptides is crucial for their assembly, luminescence, chiral expression, and functional applications. In this work, a series of dipeptides functionalized with large conjugated benzoperylene imide segments are designed and synthesized, demonstrating programmable chiroptical and self-assembly behaviors. Water as poor solvent is identified as a critical factor governing the self-assembly of these dipeptides, by modulating the balance of intermolecular interactions to produce diverse morphologies such as nanoparticles, helical fibers, toroids and supercoiled structures. The assembly pathway progresses through multiple stages governed by diffusion-limited kinetics, interfacial energy minimization, and chiral internal stress. By varying the concentration, aging time, and temperature, it is possible to achieve diverse chiral morphological transitions, thereby enabling the preparation of toroids with both high phase purity and pronounced chiroptical activity. Furthermore, enantiomeric excess transforms toroids into helical rods, with racemic mixtures undergoing spontaneous resolution. Structural evolution and pronounced chiroptical activity, including strong circularly polarized luminescence, are confirmed by spectroscopic and diffraction analyses. This work offers new insights into both the mechanistic understanding of supramolecular chirality and an engineering framework for designing π conjugated dipeptide-based functional materials with tailored chiroptical properties.

title: Optical observation of ultrafast carrier separation in InGaN photocatalyst nanostructures
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Understanding carrier dynamics in semiconductor nanostructures is essential for optimizing their photocatalytic performance. We present direct optical evidence of ultrafast carrier separation in InGaN nanostructures used for water splitting. Two types of InGaN-based photocatalysts are studied: deepnano structures, which are a p-type InGaN micro-network, and nanowires incorporating an InGaN/GaN layered heterostructure. Here, we show that rapid lateral carrier separation in these nanostructures produces observable signatures in ultrafast spectroscopy. Using combined time-resolved photoluminescence and time-resolved differential reflectance spectroscopy, we observe photoluminescence exhibiting fast decay while differential reflection remains stable. This indicates rapid carrier separation. Studies of temperature and power-dependent photoluminescence confirm that carrier separation dominates over recombination-driven decay, and Mg doping studies reveal that stronger band bending enhances the carrier separation. The physical interpretation of the observations is supported by a numerical model including drift, diffusion, and thermal relaxation. The results provide critical insights into charge carrier dynamics in InGaN nanostructures, highlighting their potential for efficient photocatalysis.

title: Chemical upcycling of mixed polyolefins via rapid C–H nitration
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Non-degradative C–H functionalization provides a promising route to upgrade polyolefins into functional materials by installing polar groups onto the carbon backbones, but few methods are universally applicable to the diverse and mixed polyolefins commonly encountered in waste streams. Herein, we report a rapid, selective, and broadly applicable C–H nitration strategy for the direct upcycling of mixed polyolefins. Driven by the low steric hindrance and radical nature of NO2, diverse substrates are nitrated with high selectivity (87–97%), reaching functionalization degrees of up to 2.4 mol% in just 5 min while substantially maintaining their molecular weights. The functionalized polymers not only exhibit enhanced tensile and adhesion properties, but can also be formulated into a dynamic covalent polymer network that displays 23-fold higher toughness than the original polyolefin mixture. This work establishes a rapid and general C–H nitration as a scalable and waste-compatible strategy to upcycle mixed polyolefins beyond depolymerization.

title: Wafer-scale transferable hexagonal boron nitride membranes via interfacial engineering for multilevel storage
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Two-dimensional materials hold immense potential for memristive devices, offering a pathway to overcome the von Neumann bottleneck. Specifically, hexagonal boron nitride (h-BN) is highly promising for low-voltage, multilevel memristors due to its robust physicochemical properties. However, synthesizing wafer-scale, transferable, and thickness-controllable h-BN (tens of nanometers thick) remains challenging, impeding its device integration. Herein, we demonstrate an interfacial modulation strategy via controlled sapphire substrate nitridation to grow high-quality, crack-free h-BN membranes. Introducing an interfacial B–O buffer layer improves the crystalline quality of epitaxial h-BN and facilitates its rapid, damage-free wet transfer onto target substrates. The fabricated memristors with these transferred membranes exhibit a low set voltage of 1.06 V, an ultrahigh ON/OFF ratio of 1.57×109, an ultrafast switching speed of 30 ns, robust multilevel switching and long-term stability. Our study presents a scalable approach for advancing next-generation in-memory computing architectures.

title: Laser ablation rapid evaporative ionisation mass spectrometry imaging with few-micrometer sampling pixels
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Achieving sub-cellular resolution in ambient, matrix-free mass spectrometry imaging (MSI) remains challenging because reducing the sampling area often compromises ion yield and image fidelity. Here, we demonstrate an infrared laser–driven ambient MSI platform that mitigates these limitations through low-fluence, picosecond pulsed, high-repetition-rate laser ablation with a custom 2.94 μm light source with near-diffraction limited beam quality. This approach produces well-confined ablation features with diameters of 5 μm to 10 μm. Coupling the laser ablation plume to a rapid evaporative ionisation mass spectrometry (LA-REIMS) interface and a commercial time-of-flight mass analyser provides multiplexed ion maps of metabolites, phospholipids, and other small molecules in a single acquisition. This configuration enables routine 3 μm-pixel size imaging of fresh-frozen tissue sections, as well as imaging of formalin-fixed, paraffin embedded biopsy samples, all without additional preparation steps. Oversampled images preserve sub-cellular morphology and yield molecular distributions that correlate with fluorescence and histological features. Together, these results define a robust operational regime for high-fidelity, matrix-free MSI in the few-μm pixel range, where high infrared beam quality and stable, low-fluence, high repetition rate picosecond laser sampling underpin gentle ablation and efficient ion formation via REIMS, enabling sub-cellular molecular mapping in a clinically compatible, fully ambient format.

title: Damping and accumulation characteristics of flow driven by fishbone instability
abstract: The persistence of fishbone-driven flows across successive bursts is critical to their potential role in regulating turbulence and improving core confinement, yet the damping characteristics of such flows have not been experimentally characterized. Here we report the first direct measurement of the damping rate of fishbone-driven flows using Doppler reflectometry on the EAST tokamak. The experimentally obtained damping rate exceeds prior theoretical predictions, and this discrepancy can be reconciled by incorporating the effective charge number into the calculation of the damping rate. Furthermore, we observe that flow accumulation occurs when the time interval between successive fishbone bursts is sufficiently short, and we estimate the critical inter-burst interval threshold for accumulation to be approximately 1 ms under the present discharge conditions. These results establish an essential experimental foundation for understanding the temporal persistence of fishbone-driven flows and their implications for transport barrier dynamics.

title: Linking human sources to antibiotic resistance genes in global surface waters
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is a global public health threat driven by antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs). Yet global human ARG generation, environmental discharges and surface-water abundances remain poorly characterized, and their linkages remain unclear, particularly at gene-specific absolute abundances, given differences in antibiotic and pathogen associations among ARGs. Here, we compiled 464 absolute abundance measurement data of five key ARGs (qnrS, ermB, tetA, tetM, and sul1) and intI1 in wastewater treatment plant (WWTP) influent covering 30 countries, and combined these data with machine learning, a WWTP removal framework and a spatially explicit dilution model to estimate these metrics. Per capita generation was highest in Africa, whereas total generation and discharges were greatest in Asia; surface-water hotspots clustered in water-scarce regions, highlighting hydrological constraints alongside discharge intensity. Raising WWTP coverage in below-average countries to the global mean and high-income standards could increase global removal from 12–29% to 53–60% and 72–76%, respectively. These findings quantitatively link human ARG sources to surface-water abundances, providing a foundation for surveillance and intervention to curb ARG dissemination.

title: A framework-driven pathway to dehydration embrittlement in gypsum fault gouge
source: Earth and environmental sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Mineral dehydration can alter the mechanics and hydraulics of fault zones and affects even plate boundaries, yet direct observations of how mineral replacement reorganises the architecture of a shearing fault gouge remain limited. Here, we combine a direct shear experiment with time-resolved synchrotron-based microtomography (4DSμCT) and digital volume correlation (DVC) to track shear deformation during the transformation of gypsum to its hemihydrate.
