The dehydration reaction progressively reorganises the load-bearing grain framework during shear, producing a transition from distributed granular deformation of gypsum gouge to localised brittle faulting of hemihydrate. By direct correlation between evolving microstructures and macroscopic mechanical and hydraulic behaviour, our results show that dehydration can induce a rheological transition, driving strengthening, embrittlement, and shear localisation even under drained conditions. Framework reorganisation therefore provides a direct pathway by which dehydration reactions may promote instability in fault gouges, complementing models that attribute dehydration embrittlement primarily to transient pore-pressure increases.

title: Intravenous phage therapy for difficult-to-treat infections: a systematic review and meta-analysis of individual patient data
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Intravenous phage therapy enables systemic bacteriophage delivery in difficult-to-treat infections, but raises distinct pharmacokinetic, immunological and safety considerations, while evidence remains fragmented. Here in this systematic review we analysed 60 studies from nine high-income countries, predominantly case reports, case series and uncontrolled trials reporting intravenous phage therapy with or without local administration and mostly alongside antibiotics. We extracted and synthesised individual patient data both descriptively and through a meta-analysis using mixed-effects models, which estimated probabilities of reporting clinical improvement and microbiological eradication of 65.8% (n = 122) and 55.3% (n = 106), respectively, while the probability of reporting adverse reactions was 9.2% (n = 168), with reactions predominantly mild and self-limited. In exploratory analyses, combined intravenous and local administration was associated with more frequent reporting of clinical improvement than intravenous administration alone, raising questions regarding potential limitations of the intravenous route. However, the uncontrolled and heterogeneous nature of current evidence warrants cautious interpretation and underscores the need for rigorous research.

title: var2csa transcription implicates variant surface antigen switching in cerebral malaria pathogenesis
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Previous PCR-based gene expression studies linked severe malaria, including cerebral malaria (CM), to Plasmodium falciparum erythrocyte membrane protein-1 (PfEMP1) variants that bind endothelial protein C receptor (EPCR). Using RNA sequencing and de novo transcriptome assembly in a matched CM case-control study of Malian children, we quantify var gene transcripts encoding PfEMP1s in 13 matched pairs of CM cases and uncomplicated malaria controls and in 25 CM cases and 55 uncomplicated malaria controls. Contrary to earlier findings, PfEMP1s that bind EPCR alone are not associated with CM. Transcription of conserved gene var2csa is implicated in var gene switching in vitro. Here, its transcription is significantly associated with CM across study sites, suggesting that switching may contribute to CM pathogenesis. Importantly, this association is observed at the transcript level, but potentially not translation. We use a protein microarray to show a lack of antibody responses to the VAR2CSA antigen in cerebral malaria, supporting an association between CM and var2csa transcription rather than antigenic presence. CM is also associated with distinct var transcriptional profiles and dual ICAM-1/EPCR-binding PfEMP1 variants. These findings underscore the complexity of PfEMP1-mediated pathogenesis and highlight the need for deeper investigation of transcriptional and regulatory mechanisms underlying severe malaria.

title: velotest: statistical assessment of RNA velocity embeddings reveals quality differences for reliable trajectory visualizations
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Contemporary single-cell RNA-sequencing studies typically use RNA velocity analyses to investigate cellular dynamics. Commonly, RNA velocities are assessed with two-dimensional projections. Although it is well established that nonlinear embeddings of gene expression data cannot comprehensively preserve the structure of the original high-dimensional data across scales, there is no tool that systematically assesses and quantifies the faithfulness of velocity embeddings. This situation potentially leads to misleading velocity visualizations and putative cell state transitions. To this end, we introduce velotest, a cell-level statistical test that quantifies the faithfulness of a velocity embedding with respect to its high-dimensional counterpart. Applying velotest across multiple datasets and embedding methods, we find strong differences in the embedding qualities between embedding methods, datasets, and regions in individual datasets. velotest thus provides an essential validation step and enables researchers to select a suitable visualization of high-dimensional velocities, ensuring that hypotheses drawn from velocity projections are grounded in accurately represented dynamics.

title: Local niche-derived immunosuppressive CXCR2+ cells impair antiviral immunity
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Symptom severity after viral infection varies among individuals, yet its mechanism remains poorly understood. We categorize mice into recovering and non-recovering groups based on body weight after infection with the same titer of vesicular stomatitis virus (VSV). We reveal that in the olfactory bulb (OB) where VSV initially expands, non-recovering mice exhibit an anti-inflammatory environment, suggesting its detrimental effect. Importantly, CXCR2+ cells resembling immunosuppressive myeloid-derived suppressor cells (MDSCs) are more abundant in the OB of non-recovering mice than in that of recovering mice after VSV infection. Depleting CXCR2+ MDSC-like cells from the brain increases inflammatory responses and the animal’s survival after infection. Furthermore, site-specific labeling indicates that a significant fraction of these cells in the OB originate from the skull-bone marrow (skull-BM) as well as circulation. This study reveals the lethal effects of CXCR2+ MDSC-like cells on local immune responses to viral infection, highlighting their therapeutic potential for antiviral defense.

title: ER-associated biogenesis of PINK1 preprotein for neuronal mitophagy
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Given the large size of neurons, local maintenance of mitochondria is crucial to counteract insults to this organelle in axons and dendrites. The Parkinson-related mitochondrial kinase PINK1 plays a central role in mitochondrial quality control, which in neurons requires the transport of Pink1 mRNA by mitochondrial hitch-hiking. However, how and where PINK1 is locally translated and processed has remained unclear. Using live-cell imaging, we trace local PINK1 translation sites and preprotein dynamics, revealing a concerted interplay between mitochondria and the ER, with endolysosomes frequently localized adjacent to the site of translation. Upon metabolically regulated untethering from mitochondria, Pink1 mRNA relocates to ribosomes in proximity to the ER and endolysosomes for translation of the PINK1 preprotein. The ER chaperone DNAJB6 shields the PINK1 preprotein in transit to mitochondria, following the post-translational ER-SURF pathway. Consequently, loss of DNAJB6 leads to persistent ER/endolysosome-associated PINK1 precursor stores and failure of mitophagy upon mitochondrial damage. Our findings reveal that neuronal PINK1 protein translation switches between mitochondrially anchored co-translational and ER-associated post-translational import states, with functional implications for mitochondrial quality control.

title: Cholesterol dysregulation contributes to hematopoietic failure in parn-mutant zebrafish with implications for dyskeratosis congenita
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Germline mutations in PARN cause dyskeratosis congenita (DC), an inherited bone marrow failure syndrome characterized by multilineage cytopenia and progression to myeloid disease. The mechanisms underlying this malignant transformation have not been fully elucidated. Here we show, using a loss-of-function CRISPR-Cas9 zebrafish parn mutant, hematopoietic stem and progenitor (HSPC) expansion and reduced mature hematopoietic cells across various lineages. Cholesterol biosynthesis was transcriptionally activated; a finding recapitulated in patient-derived iPSCs with PARN mutations. Inhibiting cholesterol biosynthesis rescued HSPC expansion and anemia in parn mutants. Concurrent myeloid differentiation therapy or Wnt inhibition reduced HSPCs to varying degrees. We further demonstrate a role for activated Erk signaling in impairing erythrocyte differentiation and show robust rescue with trametinib treatment. Overall, our findings uncover unrecognized roles for Parn in regulating cholesterol metabolism and Erk signaling and provide preclinical evidence for targeting these pathways to restore hematopoiesis in DC.

title: A protein repeat interruption rule governs Nebulin stability and explains in-frame NEB mutations
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Nemaline myopathy is a rare congenital muscle disease associated with thin filament disruption that is currently without treatment. Biallelic mutations in Nebulin are the most common cause of nemaline myopathy. Nebulin encodes a giant protein with a primary function of establishing thin filament length. Nebulin protein has a large central region composed of a series of thin filament binding super repeats. Many Nebulin mutations are small in-frame deletions within individual super repeats. Why these deletions cause disease remains unclear. To study this, we generated a series of zebrafish lines, including ones carrying in-frame partial super repeat deletions and ones harboring complete/intact super repeat deletions. Partial super repeat deletions destabilize and reduce Nebulin protein, resulting in severe phenotypes and early death. Conversely, complete super repeat deletions preserve Nebulin stability and expression, and induce no overt phenotypes. Our work provides mechanistic insights and informs future therapeutic approaches for Nebulin-related Nemaline myopathy.

title: A genome-wide imaging screen reveals epigenetic and mechanistic partitioning of lamina-associated chromatin
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The nuclear periphery is a near-universal site of heterochromatin organization, where lamina-associated domains (LADs) play a crucial role in transcriptional repression and genome stability. Yet the molecular mechanisms that tether LADs in human cells have remained elusive. Here, we overcome this barrier by performing the first genome-wide, imaging-based siRNA screen of LAD positioning, identifying more than 100 genes required for perinuclear localization. We isolate a striking enrichment of RNA-binding proteins, with hnRNPK emerging as a factor required for the positioning of nearly two-thirds of LADs in the human genome. Its loss drives large-scale LAD detachment from the nuclear periphery without altering heterochromatin states or lamina components, but induces transcriptional dysregulation within these domains. Strikingly, hnRNPK-sensitive LADs are uniquely enriched for H3K27me3, distinguishing them from H3K9me3-enriched insensitive LADs. Together, these findings demonstrate that LADs comprise epigenetically distinct subclasses governed by distinct regulatory pathways and establish a framework for systematically mapping genetic control of nuclear architecture.

title: Orbital spectroscopy links dust source composition to atmospheric acidity and nitrate
source: Earth and environmental sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Mineral dust affects atmospheric chemistry, air quality, and climate, yet its impacts remain uncertain because its mineral composition is poorly constrained. Here we combine NASA EMIT orbital imaging spectroscopy with a satellite-constrained global chemistry model to quantify how source-resolved calcite variability alters aerosol chemistry and optical properties. EMIT-derived calcite improves agreement with airborne observations and reveals contrasts in dust alkalinity. Compared with globally averaged calcite, source-resolved calcite shifts regional annual mean aerosol pH by -0.6 to +0.5 units, with local changes exceeding 1 pH unit across substantial areas of the most affected dust-influenced regions, reaching -4 to +3 units in limited areas. These acidity changes reorganize secondary inorganic aerosol formation, nitrate partitioning, and extreme nitrate events, particularly where dust interacts with anthropogenic pollution. In contrast, calcite-driven secondary-aerosol radiative effects are small relative to those caused by spatial variations in iron-oxide absorption. These results show that calcite variability strongly modulates heterogeneous chemistry, whereas iron oxides dominate radiative impacts.

title: Double-membrane-spanning RNA export pores are a conserved feature in nidovirus replication organelles
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Upon infection, arteriviruses, coronaviruses, and other nidoviruses transform endoplasmic reticulum membranes into viral replication organelles. These include large numbers of double-membrane vesicles (DMVs) whose interior is considered the primary site of viral RNA synthesis. Early studies characterized nidovirus DMVs as sealed compartments, leaving it unclear how newly synthesized viral RNA could be exported to the cytosol. The discovery of DMV-spanning pore complexes in coronavirus-infected cells provided a plausible solution for this topological challenge. However, their structural organization, functional features, and evolutionary conservation across the nidovirus order, have remained unclear. Here, we investigate the macromolecular architecture of DMVs induced by two prototypic arteriviruses using cellular cryo-electron tomography. Despite the substantial evolutionary distance separating arteriviruses and coronaviruses, we observe DMV-spanning pore complexes with striking structural similarities to those previously described in coronaviruses. These pores may facilitate both export and encapsidation of viral RNA. In the absence of viral RNA synthesis, ectopic expression of the arterivirus transmembrane nonstructural proteins nsp2 and nsp3 suffices to induce the formation of pore-containing DMVs. Together, our findings reveal the conservation of key structural features of DMV pores across two distantly related nidovirus families and support a central role for these pores in nidovirus replication.

title: A renewable autologous biomaterial for reprogramming cellular metabolism
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Autologous blood-derived products are attractive for tissue repair because they are biocompatible, renewable and readily accessible, but their liquid form limits local retention and provides little structural support. Here we show that autologous serum can be transformed into an injectable hydrogel microsphere biomaterial using gas-shearing microfluidics combined with ionic and fibrin-based enzymatic crosslinking. Reconstruction of the fibrin network improves structural support, interfacial lubrication and local retention of serum-derived factors. Compared with citrate-anticoagulated PRP, anticoagulant-free autologous serum better preserves chondrocyte metabolic adaptation under hypoxic inflammatory conditions. Multi-omics analyses further indicate enhanced chondrocyte proliferation, migration and matrix maintenance, together with modulation of hypoxia-responsive metabolic pathways. In osteoarthritis models, the microspheres promote cartilage repair and reduce disease progression. These findings establish a renewable autologous serum biomaterial platform that integrates biochemical and mechanical functions and may support personalized regenerative therapies.

title: Environmental toxicant-induced epigenetic and transcriptional reprogramming of transposable elements
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Transposable elements (TEs) are mobile DNA sequences that constitute a significant portion of mammalian genomes and are generally epigenetically silenced, yet can regulate gene expression and chromatin architecture. Their roles under environmental exposure remain unclear. Here, we integrated 351 multi-omic datasets from adult mouse liver following early-life exposure to arsenic, lead, bisphenol A, tributyltin, di-2-ethylhexyl phthalate, tetrachlorodibenzo-p-dioxin, and particulate matter less than 2.5 micrometers. Early-life toxicant exposure altered chromatin accessibility and expression of TEs in later life, revealing exposure-specific and sex-dependent responses. Most differentially accessible TEs located in non-coding regions. Genes associated with Long Interspersed Nuclear Elements (LINEs) were enriched in metabolic pathways, while long terminal repeat elements, particularly the ORR1E subfamily, were associated with immune-related genes. We also identified 164 TE-gene chimeric transcripts with TE-derived transcription start sites, highlighting TE-contributed transcriptional plasticity. Our findings depict a landscape of TE response to early-life toxicant exposures in mouse liver.

title: VHSeek: biology foundation model-based virus representations revealing virus host associations
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Virus-host association prediction is fundamental to virus-related disease control and phage therapy, yet many existing tools require candidate-host genome sequences, which may be unavailable for some eukaryotic hosts or impractical to search at the scale of large virome studies. We present VHSeek, a supervised virus-host association predictor that integrates DNA- and protein-derived viral representations. VHSeek combines nucleotide representations from AIDO.DNA and protein representations from ESM2 to learn virus-host association patterns, and then transfers predictions through known host taxonomies from lower to higher ranks. During inference, VHSeek uses viral sequence data and known host taxonomies, without host sequence data. Compared with iPHoP, the state-of-the-art baseline evaluated in this study, VHSeek improves genus-level maximum F1 score (Fmax), Top-1 accuracy, and area under the precision–recall curve (AUPR) by 12%, 19%, and 27%, respectively. Confidence thresholding enables abstention and reduces false discoveries. On the processed IMG/VR v4.1 metagenomic collection, VHSeek expands effective host coverage from 36.5% to 64.5% using a validation-calibrated confidence threshold. VHSeek prioritizes candidate viruses and reservoir hosts with potential human health impacts, including multi-host hypotheses in which one virus may be associated with humans and additional hosts (e.g., Saboya virus with Homo sapiens and Culicidae) not currently captured in the dataset.

title: Wnk1 drives CD4+ T cell lineage fate determination and bone marrow homing in a mouse model of retinal autoimmune disease
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Dysfunctional CD4 + T helper (Th) cell differentiation and migration, along with bone marrow (BM) myeloid hematopoietic responses, contribute to the progression of inflammatory and autoimmune diseases, yet the regulatory mechanisms remain unclear. Here, we perform single-cell transcriptomics of BM, cervical draining lymph nodes, and retinas in a mouse model of experimental autoimmune uveitis to comprehensively profile T-cell immune dynamics. We find that Wnk1 upregulation promotes expansion, differentiation, and migration of pro-inflammatory Th1 and Th17 cells by activating the c-Myc/glycolysis pathway. Genetic or pharmacological inhibition of Wnk1 reduces ocular inflammation, T-cell chemotaxis, and trafficking to BM and retina, accompanied by reduced BM-derived neutrophils and monocytes and fewer myeloid cells in draining lymph nodes and retina. In Vogt-Koyanagi-Harada patients, Wnk1 is elevated in CD4 + T cells, and its inhibition impairs their proliferation and effector functions. Collectively, our data implicate Wnk1 as a key regulator of CD4 + T-cell behavior and inter-organ immune communication.

title: SMC5/6 safeguards chromatin compartments and TAD boundaries for genome stability
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: SMC5/6, a member of the Structural Maintenance of Chromosomes family, coordinates 3D genome organization, chromatin states, and transcriptional regulation, yet its role in higher-order chromatin architecture remains poorly defined. Here, we investigate the impact of conditional SMC5 depletion in human B lymphoblastoid cells. Hi-C analyses reveal global rewiring of chromatin interactions, with increased long-range and reduced short-range contacts, leading to altered large-scale chromosome organization. SMC5 loss induces changes in 3D genome compartmentalization affecting ~2% of the genome and is accompanied by transcriptional upregulation of inflammatory and cancer-associated gene programs. SMC5 depletion also promotes double-strand break accumulation, preferentially in active compartments and following gene expression levels. However, regions undergoing architectural reorganization display comparatively fewer breaks, indicating that chromatin changes are not driven by DNA damage. Together, our findings establish SMC5/6 as a key regulator of chromatin compartmentalization and TAD boundary integrity, linking 3D genome organization to transcriptional control and genome stability.

title: Combinatorial mutagenesis of N-terminal sequences reveals expanded stability determinants of the Escherichia coli N-degron pathway
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Although penultimate residues near the N-terminus are known to influence protein stability, their exact contributions in prokaryotes are not well understood. Here, we utilize combinatorial mutagenesis, cell sorting, and next generation sequencing to perform the deepest sequence coverage screen of the Escherichia coli N-degron pathway of proteolysis. Our results reinforce the known influence of canonically destabilizing P1 F/L/Y/W/R/K while revealing unexpected effects from P2 residue identities that influence protein stability comparably to P1 identity, such as for P2 Pro (stabilizing), Gly (stabilizing), or Gln (destabilizing). For low stability sequences without P1 F/L/Y/W/R/K, we identify motifs rich in P1 Cys paired with bulky and negatively charged P2-P5 residues. Furthermore, additive stability effects were observed for motifs rich in bulky (destabilizing), acidic (stabilizing), and flexible Gly/Ser (stabilizing) residues. We train a machine learning model to predict the stability of N-terminal sequences, including motifs that break expected stability rules. We find that these data-driven predictions of P2 identity contributions quantitatively correlate with binding energies predicted from computational docking of peptides to N-recognin ClpS. Our work expands the stability determinants of the N-degron pathway with unprecedented granularity, serving as a resource for N-degron identification, understanding, and design.

title: Soybean Pb encodes a WD40 protein regulating pubescence tip morphology and seed size during domestication
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The classical soybean Pb locus controls pubescence tip morphology, with sharp (Pb/-) and blunt (pb/pb) types. It associates with insect resistance and experiences strong negative selection during domestication, yet the causal gene remains unknown, leaving unclear whether Pb directly confers insect resistance and the selective mechanism. Here, we report the cloning of Pb, which encodes a seven-WD40-repeat protein. A 4.88-kb deletion in the pb allele causes premature translation termination. Transgenic Pb soybeans with sharp pubescence tips show unchanged antibiosis and antixenosis against leaf-chewing insects compared with blunt-tip wild-type plants, demonstrating pubescence tip morphology alone does not confer insect resistance. The Pb gene reduces seed size, likely explaining its near disappearance in modern cultivars. Pb promotes assembly and activity of the GmLEC1a/GmNF-YC2/GmbZIP67 complex to regulate seed development. These findings resolve long-standing questions about the Pb locus and advance our understanding of soybean domestication.

title: Disaccharide production in marine cold seeps links dissolved organic carbon to anaerobic oxidation of methane
source: Earth and environmental sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Anaerobic oxidation of methane (AOM) has been proposed as a source of dissolved organic carbon (DOC) at marine cold seeps, but the underlying molecular mechanism for its production remains unknown. Here we demonstrate a previously unrecognized link between AOM and porewater DOC by analyzing disaccharides in sediment and porewaters from a methane-charged cold seep in Astoria Canyon (Oregon, USA). In the AOM zone, sediments contain up to 17.7 mg L−1 trehalose with δ13C values as low as −78‰, and porewaters contain up to 1 mg L−1 sucrose with δ13C values as low as −66‰, representing 4.6% of DOC. Stable isotope probing experiments reveal AOM-dependent biosynthesis of trehalose and sucrose, and both disaccharides turn over faster than diagnostic lipids, suggesting that these compounds serve as biomarkers for active AOM. Accordingly, disaccharides mediate a relationship that may sustain microbial food webs and influence carbon cycling in methane-rich marine sediments.

title: σ-complex stabilization shapes enzymatic C-glycosylation and restricts the scope of natural C-glycosides
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: C-glycosides are valuable compounds containing hydrolytically stable C-C bonds, yet their scarcity in nature and synthetic complexity limit their availability. Enzymes offer a sustainable route to C-glycosides, but few are known to display C-glycosylation activity and their mechanism remains unclear. Here, we study the intricacies of the maize C-glycosyltransferase ZmUGT708A6 using X-ray crystallography, biochemical assays, and atomistic simulations. Structural and dynamical analyses reveal two flexible gates that control substrate access and reactive conformations. Combined Quantum Mechanics/Molecular Mechanics simulations and mutational data support a stepwise SEAr mechanism for C-glycosylation of neutral phloretin, mediated by the catalytic His-Asp dyad and involving a high-energy σ-complex that stabilizes through a water-mediated proton transfer. Complementary pH- and substrate-activity experiments, together with Quantum Mechanics calculations, indicate that substrate hydroxylation patterns, protonation states, and σ-complex energetics restrict the scope of C-glycosides. Our results provide a coherent mechanistic framework that reconciles experimental observations across diverse conditions and advances our understanding of enzymatic C-glycosylation.

title: Phonon-assisted endothermic triplet sensitization enables record NIR-II-to-visible-light photon upconversion
abstract:
Near-infrared-to-visible triplet−triplet annihilation photon upconversion (TTA-UC) enables harvesting low-energy photons; however, extending nanocrystal-sensitized TTA-UC into the second near-infrared window (NIR-II) remains challenging because triplet sensitization is thermodynamically disfavored under sub-triplet excitation. Here, we demonstrate that lead-free AgBiS
                    2
                    nanocrystals facilitate phonon-assisted endothermic triplet sensitization, enabling efficient NIR-II-to-visible upconversion. Under the sub-bandgap single-photon excitation, AgBiS
                    2
                    nanocrystals exhibit anti-Stokes photoluminescence, suggesting strong exciton−phonon coupling mediated by surface states. When coupled with 5-tetracene carboxylic acid transmitters and rubrene annihilators, AgBiS
                    2
                    achieves 980 nm-to-visible upconversion with a record quantum yield of 6.22% (normalized to 100%) and an anti-Stokes shift of 0.95 eV. Time-resolved photoluminescence and ultrafast transient absorption spectroscopy support a surface-state-mediated uphill energy-transfer pathway coupled to low-frequency vibrational modes. Our work establishes phonon-assisted triplet sensitization as a strategy to overcome the NIR-II red wall for lead-free photon upconversion.

title: A fully electromagnetic hybrid PIC-fluid model for predictive fusion neutron yield in dense plasma focus
abstract: A fully electromagnetic hybrid ion-PIC/electron-fluid framework is developed for the implosion-to-pinch phase of dense plasma focus (DPF) discharges. Ions are advanced kinetically, electrons form a charge-neutralizing fluid under the quasi-neutral approximation, and the full Maxwell equations are solved in both plasma and vacuum. The generalized Ohm law includes resistive, electron pressure-gradient, and Hall terms. Applied to a non-hollow 180 kA geometry initialized from a pre-ionized end-of-rundown state, the framework reproduces the axial rundown, radial compression, and pinch stages. The sheath front trajectory agrees with fully kinetic benchmarks within 10%, and a pinch-radius comparison captures the radial collapse. A beam-target neutron diagnostic applied to the simulated ion distribution gives a yield of , at the same scale as the fully kinetic reference. The ion spectrum develops a non-Maxwellian suprathermal tail to about 0.25 MeV. The yield remains sensitive to the electron-temperature closure and anode geometry. The framework captures relevant macroscopic observables and ion-kinetic diagnostics at a computational cost roughly – times lower than comparable fully kinetic electromagnetic PIC simulations.

title: Bifunctional Pt/CeO2 Nanozyme-Mediated Metabolic Regulation Promotes NAD+ Regeneration and ROS Clearance to Ameliorate Age-Related Osteoporosis
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Age-related osteoporosis is characterized by progressive loss of bone mass and deterioration of trabecular microarchitecture, driven by chronic inflammation, redox imbalance, mitochondrial dysfunction, and osteoblast senescence that uncouples bone formation from resorption. During aging, declining nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD+) availability further exacerbates mitochondrial dysfunction and stress responses, suggesting that restoring NAD+ redox homeostasis could be a viable therapeutic strategy. Here, we reported a bifunctional nanozyme-mediated metabolic regulation strategy to promote NAD+ regeneration and scavenge reactive oxygen species (ROS) for the treatment of age-related osteoporosis. The bifunctional nanozyme (Pt/CeO2) was constructed by in situ growth of platinum nanoparticles on cerium oxide nanorods and was designed for ROS scavenging and NAD+ regeneration via NADH (reduced nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide) oxidation. In senescent osteoblasts, Pt/CeO2 reduced ROS, restored mitochondrial integrity, and alleviated senescence, thereby promoting osteogenic differentiation. In vivo results confirmed that systemic administration of Pt/CeO2 preserved trabecular architecture and increased bone mineral density in naturally aged mice. These findings demonstrated that coupling ROS scavenging with the restoration of NAD+ redox homeostasis via Pt/CeO2 nanozyme provided a promising therapeutic strategy to counteract osteoblast senescence and slow the progression of age-related osteoporosis.

title: Taming Metal–Electrolyte Interface via Two-Dimensional Organic Metal Chalcogenide Colloids for Anode-Free Sodium Metal Batteries
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Anode-free metal batteries are promising candidates for next-generation energy storage technologies, yet their application is severely limited by dendrite growth and rapid capacity decay induced by an unstable metal–electrolyte interface. Herein, we propose a “colloid electrolyte” strategy employing coordination polymer nanosheets as electrolyte additives for constructing anode-free sodium metal batteries (AFSMBs). Unlike conventional molecular additives or inert particle suspensions, these colloidal nanosheets provide spatially organized and continuously available interfacial reaction domains, thereby spatially regulating electrolyte component distribution and interfacial reactions. These nanosheets, composed of AgS layers uniformly decorated with fluorinated groups, undergo in situ decomposition at the metal–electrolyte interface. This process generates gradient distributions of Ag nanoparticles and NaF/Na2S species, which guide the spontaneous formation of a functionally graded solid electrolyte interphase (SEI). This hierarchical SEI enables dendrite-free Na deposition and imparts sustained interfacial protection during cycling. Consequently, high-cathode-loading AFSMBs achieve an ultralong lifespan (>1600 cycles), representing a 10-fold improvement over counterpart cells without the colloidal additive. Notably, 0.5-Ah-level anode-free pouch cells exhibit stable cycling for 500 cycles at 2 C. This work establishes coordination polymer colloids as a new class of electrolyte additives for advanced alkali metal batteries.

title: Aryl Palladium Acetates as Highly Active Species in Intermolecular Heck Reactions of Hindered Olefins
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Despite decades of development since the early 1970s, the intermolecular Heck reaction of hindered tri- and tetrasubstituted olefins with aryl halides has remained a challenge. Traditional approaches relied on rate-acceleration by directing groups or high reactivity of cationic arylpalladium species generated from triflates and diazonium salts. Herein, we report the first general and efficient Heck coupling between trisubstituted alkenes (and selected tetrasubstituted olefins) with aryl iodides and bromides. Our protocol employs simple PdCl2 or Pd(OAc)2 as precatalyst and needs no directing groups. It features an exceptionally broad substrate scope, accommodating diverse (hetero)aryl halides and both acyclic and cyclic olefins, and the reaction proceeds efficiently on a gram scale with remarkably low palladium loadings. The practical value of this method is highlighted by its application in concise synthesis of several pharmaceutically relevant motifs. Mechanistically, HRMS and DFT calculations revealed that phosphine-free complexes of arylpalladium acetates─either monomer [(Ar)Pd(OAc)] or its paddlewheel dimer with bridging acetates─serve as the key active species. These species exhibit minimal steric hindrance, a high partial positive charge, and high electrophilicity at the palladium center, synergistically facilitating the binding and rapid insertion of hindered alkenes.

title: Phototunable Solid–Liquid Interfacial Energy via Ion–Electron Coupling
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The solid–liquid interfacial energy governs wetting, adhesion, and friction, yet is commonly regarded as a static property defined by surface chemistry and liquid composition. Here we show that light can reversibly modulate the interfacial energy at chemically invariant semiconductor–electrolyte interfaces by tuning the electrostatic coupling between electronic carriers in the solid and ions in the liquid. Using dark dynamic tensiometry, we directly quantify photoinduced changes in advancing and receding contact angles, revealing pronounced and reversible wettability modulation that is absent on insulating or metallic substrates. Systematic control experiments indicate that, in simple salt electrolytes, the response arises primarily from electrostatic coupling between photomodulated carriers and mobile ions in the electric double layer, rather than from detectable photochemical surface modification or changes in bulk liquid properties. In situ atomic force microscopy and ionovoltaic measurements provide microscopic and quantitative evidence that light attenuates or enhances electrostatic double-layer forces and ion–electron coupling, and reveal a sign reversal in the photoresponse between PFOTS-modified and bare Si interfaces. The opposing responses of PFOTS-modified and bare interfaces persist on p-type Si, showing that the effect is not confined to n-type substrates. Furthermore, we demonstrate that this phototunable coupling extends to reversible control of kinetic friction, enabling active modulation of droplet sliding dynamics. These results also identify imaging light as a potential source of bias in contact-angle measurements at photoactive semiconductor–electrolyte interfaces. These findings establish ion–electron coupling as a tunable thermodynamic lever linking semiconductor physics to macroscopic interfacial energy, opening opportunities for optically controlled wetting, friction, and interfacial transport.

title: Concerted Ligand-to-Metal Charge Transfer Absorption and Localized Photoluminescence in an Fe(III) Photosensitizer
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract There is tremendous interest in the electronic structure of [FeIII(phtmeimb)2]+, the first iron complex to show room temperature photoluminescence (PL) with an excited-state lifetime sufficient for dynamic quenching in fluid solution. Two types of excited states are generated by light absorption, termed the Franck–Condon (FC) state and the thermally equilibrated excited state (THEXI) that is photoluminescent. Herein we report solvatochromic and electroabsorption studies to probe the electronic structure of these two states. The doublet ligand-to-metal-charge-transfer absorption was found to be mostly solvent independent while a notable solvatochromism in the PL spectra indicated the presence of an excited-state dipole in polar solvents (μ⃗ = 16 ± 10 D), best formulated as [FeII(phtmeimb•+)(phtmeimb)]+*. However, standard and higher-order electroabsorption spectra revealed concerted and equal charge transfer from the two tridentate ligands to the metal, giving rise to a significant polarizability change (Δα) without the generation of a dipole moment (Δμ⃗ = 0) best formulated as [FeII(phtmeimb+1/2)2]+*. The strong interligand coupling necessary for such concerted charge transfer is proposed to be mediated by a t2g orbital of the Fe(III) center. Taken together, these findings provide new insights into this famed photoluminescent open-shell iron complex relevant to the design of improved iron photosensitizers.

title: Spatiotemporally Decoupled Cascade Photocatalysis on Dual S-Scheme Heterostructure with Interfacial Polarization Fields and Proton Shuttle Channels
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Transient surface reaction dynamics govern artificial-photosynthesis-enabled multistep tandem biomass oxidation but are hindered by spatially intermingled reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation and temporally entangled elementary-step sequences. A spatial-engineering strategy for fabricating ZnS/Sv-chalcogenide/MoSe2 (Sv = sulfur vacancies, chalcogenide = ZnIn2S4, Zn0.5Cd0.5S, CdIn2S4) dual S-scheme heterostructure, with chalcogenide as the shared mediator between the ZnS/chalcogenide and chalcogenide/MoSe2 S-junctions, is developed by anchoring MoSe2 nanoparticles onto chalcogenide nanosheets epitaxially grown from ZnS hollow dodecahedral cages. These ternary-component nanoreactors integrate dual interfacial features, the interfacial localized polarization field and the interfacial proton shuttle channel, to orchestrate dynamic intelligent catalysis. Specifically, the interfacial localized polarization field drives spatially decoupled ROS generation (•OH, •O2–, •OOH) via the asymmetric charge distributions, enabling zone-specific ROS to undertake differentiated oxidation tasks. Interfacial proton shuttle channel drives temporally decoupled elementary-step sequences via the interfacial dynamic hydrogen-bonding networks, thereby liberating pH-dependent proton transfer through directed radical protonation (•O2– → •OOH). This synergy provides a proof of concept for neutral 5-hydroxymethylfurfural-to-2,5-furandicarboxylic acid (HMF-to-FDCA) conversion and demonstrates a fundamental research-to-practical-application capability. This work proposes a generalizable catalyst design paradigm integrating interfacial localized polarization fields and interfacial proton shuttle channels, offering innovative insights for guiding spatiotemporally decoupled multistep cascade catalysis.

title: Symmetry-Breaking Charge Localization Controls Radiationless Decay in a Multibranched Charge-Transfer State
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Symmetry breaking in multibranched charge-transfer (CT) excited states is generally viewed as a mechanism for excited-state localization, yet how such localization controls the subsequent fate of the excitation remains poorly understood. Here, we show that environmental stabilization of a symmetry-broken CT state can fundamentally reshape radiationless decay in a bent donor–acceptor–donor chromophore. Increasing solvent stabilization drives rapid reorganization toward a lower-energy CT configuration, collapsing the singlet lifetime from 1.98 ns in toluene to 9.2 ps in acetonitrile while increasing the effective nonradiative rate (knr) from 2.14 × 108 to >1.11 × 1011 s–1. Femtosecond transient absorption establishes that formation of the stabilized CT configuration precedes terminal population loss, while triplet accumulation observed in nonpolar media disappears as singlet depletion becomes ultrafast. Controlled toluene–acetonitrile mixtures further reveal that the nonradiative rate does not obey a single invariant energy-gap dependence: distinct energy-gap-law regimes emerge as the CT state is progressively stabilized, followed by a strongly reorganized regime in which knr continues to accelerate despite little additional change in the energy gap. Independently, the changing relationship between emission spectral variance and Stokes shift shows that the nuclear reorganization of the relaxed CT ensemble also changes with stabilization. Together, these results support a solvent-dependent symmetry-breaking landscape in which progressive charge localization reshapes both the excited-state energy and the nuclear coordinates governing access to the ground state. Symmetry breaking therefore acts not simply as an electronic localization process, but as an environmental kinetic switch, converting a long-lived, emissive and triplet-forming CT state into a rapidly quenched excited state.

title: Accessing Alkyl Linkers for Macrocyclic Peptide Synthesis via Nickel-Mediated Doubly DeAminative Macrocyclization
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The rise of macrocyclic peptides as a therapeutic modality has exposed gaps in the synthetic chemistry toolbox available for drug discovery teams to rapidly explore diverse linkers for structural optimization. In contrast to the thioether linkers common in peptide leads identified from mRNA display, all-carbon linkers are desirable for imparting solubility and stability, but existing approaches suffer from limited amino acid diversity, incompatibility with solid-phase peptide synthesis (SPPS), stereochemical loss, multistep requirements, or restricted linker placement. We report a Doubly DeAminative Macrocyclization (D2AM) to install alkyl linkers via C(sp3)–C(sp3) bond formation. This method uses pyridinium monomers derived from commercial amino acids that are stable to SPPS for the seamless synthesis of complex macrocyclic and polycyclic peptides with conservation of stereochemistry. This deaminative method is anticipated to accelerate optimization of peptide macrocycle structure in drug discovery.

title: Discerning between Excimer and Singlet Fission Sites Using Modulated Magnetic Field Photoluminescence
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Magnetic field effects play a key role in the characterization of organic electronic materials. In particular, the microscopic processes underlying singlet fission and triplet–triplet annihilation have been clarified in recent years through the observation and subsequent theoretical explanation of magnetic field effects in these processes. Here, we study magnetic field effects on the luminescence of 5,12-bis((triisopropylsilyl)ethynyl)tetracene, a well-studied material in which both singlet fission and triplet–triplet annihilation occur. By performing highly sensitive modulated-field magneto-photoluminescence experiments we observe magnetic field effect lineshapes with rich detail, allowing a precise characterization of triplet exciton dynamics. By additionally filtering these magnetic field effects by luminescence wavelength, we can identify the excimer state by its unique magnetic field signature. Finally, we show that a theoretical explanation of these field effects requires a model that explicitly accounts for quantum coherences, which highlights the importance of detailed spin dynamics modeling in understanding magnetic field effects, even at room temperature.

title: Electrothermal Mapping: A Methodology for Decoupling Redox, Protonation, and Denaturation Dynamics of Cytochrome c
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Differential scanning calorimetry, fluorometry, circular dichroism, and electrospray ionization mass spectrometry are routinely used to study thermal and chemical denaturation of proteins. However, these powerful methods monitor protein unfolding in bulk aqueous solutions but overlook interfacial environments, such as lipid membranes and confined crevices, where electrostatic and hydrophobic forces reshape protein conformational landscapes and dictate their function. Herein, we introduce an electrothermal methodology that uniquely probes protein conformational changes in a potential-modulated biomimetic environment. Electrochemistry at the Interface between Two Immiscible Electrolyte Solutions (ITIES) captures nonredox fingerprints of cytochrome c under heat stress, offering a unique perspective on protein behavior without relying on electron transfer reactions and revealing interfacial activity not evident in bulk solutions by conventional methods. Electrothermal mapping presents the protein thermal stability as a current–potential–temperature landscape, enabling direct comparison of the protein’s native and non-native conformational states driven by electrostatic and hydrophobic interactions. Ultimately, our work establishes a new paradigm for predicting protein behavior under heat stress at membrane-like interfaces, with far-reaching implications for biotechnology and medicine, including drug development, enzyme engineering, and protein expression, where protein stability and crevice accessibility are critical.

title: Cathode Surface Reconfiguration via Solvent Chemistry for Durable All-Solid-State Lithium Batteries
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Electrode surfaces and interfaces critically dominate the performance of all-solid-state lithium batteries. However, established additive-oriented strategies physically isolate the cathode from the electrolyte without improving the restricted Li+ transport pathways of the cathode surface. Here, we propose a solvation-mediated chemical etching mechanism governing cathode surface reconfiguration, driven by competition between solvent coordination and lattice stabilization. The solvent coordination, coupled with electron and proton transfer, weakens transition-metal–oxygen covalency and destabilizes lattice-bound surface species, shifting the interfacial energy landscape toward solvation-favored states. This triggers selective transition-metal dissolution and oxygen modulation, ultimately reorganizing confined surface regions into continuous Li+ transport networks. Using micron-sized single-crystalline Li- and Mn-rich cathodes as a model, we demonstrate the formation of a Mn- and O-deficient interfacial layer equipped with a three-dimensional Li+ diffusion network. This functional layer accelerates Li+ diffusion and anionic redox kinetics while suppressing transition metal migration and oxygen release. Consequently, charge-transfer resistance drops drastically (from 585 to 67 Ω) and Li+ diffusion increases 90-fold at 4.8 V, enabling 80.3% capacity retention after 2800 cycles at 2C. This solvent-driven reconfiguration provides a scalable framework for stabilizing diverse cathodes in next-generation advanced batteries.

title: Extraframework Cations Promoted Ultratrace Acetylene Capture by Coordinatively Unsaturated Nickel Sites in FAU Zeolites
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Removal of ultratrace alkynes to produce polymer- and electronic-grade olefins is an important but extremely challenging task. Here, we report a dual-cation strategy in FAU-type zeolites that enables the unprecedented capture of acetylene at concentrations of parts per million (ppm). The optimized Ni–Ba–Y adsorbent delivers high dynamic uptakes of 0.37–0.82 mmol·g–1 at acetylene concentrations of 500–10,000 ppm, with acetylene/ethylene selectivity exceeding 100 under industrial relevant conditions. Neutron powder diffraction (NPD) and theoretical calculations reveal that Ba2+ at Site I modulate the coordinatively unsaturated Ni2+ centers at Site II, enhancing π-back-donation to adsorbed acetylene. Process simulations demonstrate that adsorptive separation using Ni–Ba–Y achieves over 200-fold higher space-time productivity (STP) of ethylene and reduces energy consumption by over 44% compared with conventional catalytic hydrogenation processes. This dual-cation strategy will promote the design of zeolite adsorbents for challenging industrial separations.

title: Interband connectivity and climate shaped Neanderthal extinction and Homo sapiens ’ dispersal
abstract:
To what extent Neanderthal extinction was triggered by climate change or the arrival of
                    Homo sapiens
                    , and by which mechanisms, remains unresolved. Here, on the basis of climate-driven changes in habitat favorability for primary and secondary consumers and in net primary productivity, we estimate carrying capacity, herbivore biomass, and intraguild predation pressure during the time Neanderthals and
                    H. sapiens
                    lived in Europe. These spatially explicit estimates were incorporated into an agent-based model simulating human demographic dynamics under various scenarios. Results indicate that carrying capacity changes cannot explain Neanderthal extinction at a continental scale, though they are essential to understanding spatiotemporal distribution patterns of both human species. Conversely, the arrival of
                    H. sapiens
                    remarkably increased Neanderthal extinction likelihood. Because of the successive demographic expansions and contractions, group connectivity emerges as the key factor shaping population stability in both species. These findings support that Neanderthal disappearance and
                    H. sapiens
                    dispersals were interconnected demographic processes.

title: Radical Molecular-Junction Covalent Organic Framework for Asymmetric Iodide Conversion: 100,000 Cycles in Zn-Iodine Batteries
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Aqueous Zinc–iodine batteries are promising for large-scale energy storage owing to their eco-friendliness and safety. However, conventional two-electron cathode hosts suffer from poor cycling life due to polyiodide shuttling and sluggish one-step I–/I2 redox kinetics, which limits their practical usage. Herein, we designed a molecular-junction covalent organic framework (COF) denoted as TNCOF, integrating the tetrathiafulvalene (TTF) donor and the naphthalene diimide (NDI) acceptor. Typically, TTF forms a robust radical-cationic TTF•+ structure by anchoring to iodine electrostatically. TTF•+ and electron-withdrawing NDI within the T•+NCOF molecular junction provide a driving force through an intense local electrostatic potential for the asymmetric iodine conversion (AIC) pathway (I–/I3–/I2 vs. I2/I–), markedly boosting reaction kinetics and suppressing polyiodide shuttling. The optimized T•+NCOF cathode delivers a specific capacity of 228.7 mAh g–1 at 1 A g–1 and achieves an ultralong cycling stability exceeding 100,000 cycles, which is one of the highest records in this field. In situ measurements, Peak Force Tunneling atomic force microscopy (AFM) results, and calculations confirm the robust adsorption capability of T•+NCOF and demonstrate the accelerated I3– conversion kinetics. This work establishes that a radical-cationic molecular-junction COF enables robust I3– anchoring and a unique AIC pathway, offering a novel strategy to overcome inherent stability challenges in Zinc-halogen batteries.

title: Transition-Metal-Mediated Discharge Intermediates Set Anionic-Redox Potentials and Voltage Hysteresis in Li-Rich Cathodes
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Voltage hysteresis arising from anionic redox reactions remains a central bottleneck for lithium-rich cathodes. While ligand-to-metal charge transfer (LMCT) has been invoked to describe the charging pathway, its proposed reverse counterpart, metal-to-ligand charge transfer (MLCT), remains experimentally unresolved during discharge. Here, using cation-disordered rock-salt Li2Ni0.33Ta0.66O3 (LNTO) as a model system, we combine electrochemical relaxation analysis with synchrotron-based spectroscopy to identify, for the first time, a metastable reduction intermediate characterized by Ni(2-δ)+/(O–O)n− during discharge, thereby providing direct experimental validation for the MLCT framework. The discovery of this metastable intermediate demonstrates that discharge proceeds through a two-step electrochemical–chemical pathway, wherein the spontaneous relaxation evolution of the metastable intermediate drives free-energy dissipation and voltage hysteresis. Guided by this picture, Ru substitution was introduced to modulate the cation–anion electronic structure, enabling Ru 4d–O 2p hybridization to generate persistent low-energy hole states that lower the energy of the metastable discharge intermediate and shift O–O dimer reduction to higher potentials. We further show that the discharge intermediate serves as the energetic link through which transition-metal electronic structure governs the effective anionic-redox potential. This work provides a discharge-side thermodynamic framework for understanding and mitigating voltage hysteresis in Li-rich anionic-redox cathodes.

title: In vivo screening reveals new regulators of natural killer cell development and functional response to acute cytomegalovirus infection
abstract: Natural killer (NK) cells are critical innate immune effectors in antiviral and antitumor responses. However, the factors governing NK cell development and function remain incompletely understood. To address this, we adopted an in vivo screening approach, generating a panel of mice deficient in genes differentially expressed across NK cell maturation stages or following viral infection. We performed a combinational screen comprising baseline immunophenotyping and mouse cytomegalovirus (MCMV) challenge. We identified regulators of NK cell development, including transcriptional regulators and proteins with putative trafficking functions. MCMV challenge studies additionally identified proteins that affected antiviral immunity independently of NK cell phenotypes, including a previously undescribed regulator of NK cell degranulation, synaptotagmin-like protein 3. Identified genes exhibited a trend toward reduced tolerance to loss of function in large-scale human sequencing studies and evidence for reduced NK cell numbers in a cohort of patients with immunodeficiency. Together, these findings provide a resource of NK-expressed genes important for NK cell maturation and function, with relevance to human health.

title: Reconciling the medical relevance of mitochondrial transplantation in vivo
abstract: Mitochondria transplantation is a proposed therapeutic approach to improve the function of diseased or injured tissue. It has garnered attention and sparked debate.

title: USP8 inhibition suppresses prostate tumorigenesis via promoting RICTOR degradation to inhibit mTORC2 signaling
abstract:
RICTOR plays an essential role in regulating mechanistic target of rapamycin complex 2 (mTORC2) kinase activity, but it remains largely elusive how RICTOR is aberrantly activated in human prostate cancer (PrCa). Here, we identify RICTOR as a substrate of Cullin 3–based ubiquitin ligase adaptor SPOP, an important tumor suppressor in PrCa. SPOP deficiency or cancer-derived
                    SPOP
                    mutations disrupt SPOP-mediated degradation of RICTOR, thereby promoting PrCa progression. Furthermore, we identify USP8 as its upstream deubiquitinase, and inhibition of USP8 specifically suppresses RICTOR/mTORC2 activity without affecting mTORC1. As such, the USP8 inhibitor induces RICTOR degradation concomitant with marked tumor suppression in vivo. Hence, these findings reveal an SPOP-USP8-RICTOR regulatory circuit that underlies PrCa tumorigenesis and provides a rationale for targeting RICTOR via USP8 inhibition as a therapeutic strategy for patients with PrCa.

title: Nanoparticle-enabled gene delivery for pediatric brain tumors
abstract: Pediatric brain tumors are the leading cause of disease-related death in children, yet effective treatment remains a major clinical challenge. These aggressive tumors have limited therapeutic options capable of crossing the blood-brain barrier (BBB) and frequently recur due to genetic or epigenetic alterations and treatment resistance. Gene therapy offers a promising strategy to address these limitations by modifying gene expression, correcting mutations, or introducing functional genes. Nanoparticle (NP) delivery systems facilitate this approach by protecting genetic cargo and enabling BBB penetration and tumor-specific uptake. This review summarizes current genetic engineering strategies and NP-based delivery systems for pediatric brain tumors, including their design principles and delivery mechanisms, highlights key therapeutic approaches under preclinical and clinical investigations, and discusses the major challenges and future directions in NP-mediated gene therapy for pediatric neuro-oncology. By critically evaluating these developments, we aim to underscore the transformative potential of NP-mediated gene therapies in reshaping treatment paradigms and improving outcomes and quality of life for children.

title: Supramolecular Regulation of the Enzymatic Dephosphorylation of Twin Phosphotyrosine Peptides
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract We report the design, preparation, and study of a supramolecular pseudopeptidic cage that selectively binds twin phosphotyrosine (pTyr–pTyr) peptides and modulates their enzymatic dephosphorylation in water. The receptor combines an expanded aromatic cavity specifically designed to encapsulate a twin Tyr-Tyr motif with peripheral Lys-derived ammonium groups that engage phosphate residues through electrostatic interactions. In addition to studying the cage’s binding properties through different experimental and computational techniques, we investigated the ability of the receptor to modulate the kinetics of the irreversible phosphate hydrolysis catalyzed by alkaline phosphatase (ALP). When different substrates are connected through irreversible catalytic reactions, forming a nascent network, the presence of a supramolecular protecting host, able to selectively bind these substrates, modifies the system outcome in a way that cannot be predicted from the mere comparison of individual binding constants. This leads to unexpected, emerging behaviors, altering the relative intermediate concentrations through time and therefore regulating the network response. We demonstrate the biochemical potential of this cage by protecting the twin pTyr–pTyr motif within the activation loop of JAK2 kinase from dephosphorylation by λ-protein phosphatase. Altogether, our results establish supramolecular substrate protection as an effective strategy to regulate multistep enzymatic reaction networks.

title: Core-edge integration of negative triangularity plasmas in TCV
abstract: This study demonstrates the core-edge integration of negative triangularity (NT) plasmas with reactor-relevant operation on TCV. Neutral beam injection (NBI)-heated scenarios are developed, achieving stationary, high-performance plasmas, with up to 1.7 and above 1, at a relatively high density (Greenwald fraction of approximately 0.4). Featuring a hybrid shape that combines a negative upper-triangularity and a positive lower-triangularity, the NT L-mode achieves central ion and electron temperatures that are higher than those of its positive triangularity counterpart. Before any extrinsic impurity seeding, the divertor is already cold. This is evidenced by the retreat of the C III front from the outer target, which corresponds to a low outer-target electron temperature ( ), as well as by a significant fraction of radiated power, partly attributable to the high operational density. With divertor seeding, an X-point Radiator is formed, further cooling the divertor, with only a slight reduction in plasma performance.

title: CMOS surprises
abstract: Unexpected effects are still being discovered in complementary metal–oxide–semiconductor (CMOS) circuits, and the results could have implications for the advance of quantum computing.

title: Conformal growth of hexagonal boron nitride on three-dimensional nanoporous metals for electronic modulation in electrocatalysis
abstract: Growing atomically thin coatings over complex porous metals is challenging. Wang et al. develop a low-pressure chemical vapor deposition method for the conformal growth of few-layer hexagonal boron nitride on 3D bicontinuous nanoporous NiFe frameworks. Interfacial coupling via electronic modulation breaks the activity-stability trade-off in OER catalysis, illustrating how two-dimensional coatings can add electronic functionality to three-dimensional nanoporous catalysts.

title: Boron Nitride-Enhanced Thermally Conductive, Color-Developer-Free Thermochromic Polyurethane Composite Phase Change Material
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Traditional thermochromic phase-change materials (TC-PCMs) face several limitations, including the use of potentially toxic color developers, low heat storage/release efficiency, and the compositional complexity of conventional color-developing systems. In this study, we synthesized a negative photochromic spiropyran (SPOH) that undergoes heat-driven ring-opening isomerization, thereby enabling a direct color change. SPOH was employed as the thermochromic unit, lauric acid (LA) as the phase-change energy storage component, and amino-functionalized boron nitride (BN-NH2) as a thermally conductive filler. Through the reaction of polyethylene glycol (PEG2K) with hexamethylene diisocyanate (HDI) and its trimer (THDI), a cross-linked polyurethane network (TC-CPCMs) was constructed to encapsulate SPOH, LA, and BN-NH2. The TC-CPCMs exhibited high thermal energy storage performance, with an enthalpy efficiency (φ) of 82.1%. The introduction of BN-NH2 increased the thermal conductivity to 0.9196 W/(m·K), representing a 252% enhancement compared with that of BN-free TC-CPCMs, while maintaining stable and reversible thermochromic properties, thereby enabling the functional integration of thermal energy storage and temperature indication. In applications involving wastewater waste heat recovery and the thermal management of electronic devices, TC-CPCMs demonstrated significant performance improvements while enabling visual monitoring of the energy storage process through color changes.

title: Laser Fabrication of Vibrating Microcavities on Silicon: Formation Dynamics and Frequency Tunability
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Laser processing of silicon has long since become a standard method for wafer dicing, surface texturing, recrystallization after ion implantation, as well as surface amorphization, to name a few examples. Here, we introduce a different concept: the fabrication of vibrating microcavities in a commercial platform, Si wafers covered by a thick SiO2 layer, acting as a membrane. We demonstrate that by exposing our material system to single ultrashort laser pulses above the evaporation threshold of Si, a controlled delamination of the cover layer without fracture can be achieved, leading to the formation of a microcavity accompanied by a surface bulging up to 1.5 μm. The formation dynamics of the microcavities have been investigated by time-resolved optical probe techniques. Ultrafast pump–probe microscopy resolves the initial stages of substrate melting and the onset of layer expansion followed by relaxation. Real-time reflectivity measurements with nanosecond resolution resolve the long-lived, highly complex oscillation process of the membrane, extending over tens of μs. The formed cavities can be re-excited at low fluence without damage or degradation, featuring vibrations at single frequencies with high Q factors. The frequencies can be tuned continuously from 8 MHz up to 19 MHz by adjusting the fabrication fluence. A simple classical model is found to well describe the behavior of the membranes. Our results pave the way for applications in micro- and nano-optics and acoustics, in great part due to the commercial availability of the Si–SiO2 platform and the simplicity of the fabrication method. An extension to the field of microelectromechanical system (MEMS) of this technology is proposed.

title: MOF-on-MOF Heterojunction for Aerobic Photocatalytic Uranium Extraction from Seawater
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The photocatalytic uranium reduction provides an alternative strategy for seawater uranium extraction, yet it remains challenging due to the high carbonate content and aerobic conditions. In this work, a MOF-on-MOF (MOM) heterostructure was constructed by growing NH2-MIL-125(Ti) (M125) onto MIL-101(Cr) (M101) via a hydrothermal method. The composite integrates the excellent U(VI) adsorption capacity of M101 with the superior photoelectric properties and oxygen activation ability of M125. In air atmosphere, MOM achieved over 95% U(VI) removal from carbonate-containing solution within 2 h under light irradiation, which is significantly higher than that of M101 and M125. 90.1% of uranium was recovered from uranium-spiked seawater, and 87.8% of uranium was extracted from real seawater using MOM. In situ irradiated XPS and KPFM confirmed electron transfer from M101 to M125 in the MOM heterojunction. MOM facilitates the generation of superoxide radicals (·O2–), which play a key role in reducing U(VI) to insoluble U(IV). This work presents a synergistic MOF-on-MOF design strategy for efficient photocatalytic uranium extraction under aerobic conditions.

title: Prodrug-Based Self-Assembly Enables Dual-Triggered Release of Triazole Fungicide with Improved Environmental Safety
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Stimuli-responsive prodrug-based controlled-release systems enable precise spatiotemporal regulation of the site-specific activation and release of active ingredients, thereby enhancing overall efficacy while minimizing off-target effects in pesticide application. In this study, cyproconazole (CPZ) was covalently conjugated with cinnamic acid (CAA) via a hydrolyzable ester bond to yield a prodrug (CCP), which spontaneously self-assembled into uniform nanoparticles (CCP NPs) without the addition of any auxiliary adjuvants. Benefiting from its small hydrodynamic diameter (277 nm), narrow size distribution (PDI = 0.139), and high surface charge (–33.2 mV), the resulting CCP NPs exhibited significantly improved foliar retention and spreading capacity on plant leaf surfaces. Compared with commercial CPZ suspension concentrate (CPZ SC), CCP NPs reduced soil leaching by 71.81% and 57.48% in yellowish-brown soil from Beijing and red soil from Yunnan Province, respectively. Furthermore, CCP NPs displayed pH- and esterase-dual-triggered release behavior and provided long-term antifungal activity against plant pathogens with a control efficacy of 74.86%, outperforming CPZ SC (50.36%) after 14 days of foliar application. Comprehensive biosafety evaluations revealed that CCP NPs had no adverse effects on plant growth and exhibited approximately 5-fold lower acute toxicity to earthworms. Overall, this CAA-based prodrug nano assembly provides an effective strategy that simultaneously enhances efficacy and curbs environmental mobility, thereby supporting the development of sustainable crop protection products.

title: Simultaneous Microplastic Remediation and Hydrogen Generation in a Scalable Photocatalytic System Based on Graphdiyne-Tuned CdS/CuS S-Scheme Heterostructures
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Heterojunction catalysts have been demonstrated to promote the oxidative degradation of plastics in conjunction with the production of clean hydrogen. However, their practical application is still hampered by inherent drawbacks, including inadequate charge separation and sluggish surface reaction kinetics. Herein, we report an S-scheme heterojunction photocatalyst CdS/CuS-graphdiyne (NCSCG), consisting of N-doped CdS (NCS), CuS, and graphdiyne (GDY) that can produce 1081 μmol of hydrogen within 5 h, which is nearly 5 times that of single NCS. Under the same conditions, NCSCG selectively photoreformed microplastic polylactic acid (PLA) into pyruvic acid (PA) and hydrogen, achieving a hydrogen production of 1029 μmol. In a square-meter-level photocatalytic device, it can generate 379,000 μmol of hydrogen. Mechanistic investigations reveal that N doping modulates the d-band center of CdS and facilitates photogenerated electrons from GDY to NCS, whereas CuS supplies extra electrons to NCS, thus effectively suppressing photogenerated charge recombination. By virtue of this synergistic effect, both the surface reaction kinetics and the hydrogen production performance of the photocatalytic system are effectively improved. This study shows that coupling d-band center modulation with an S-scheme heterojunction significantly enhances photocatalytic performance, offering a practical pathway to scalable photocatalytic hydrogen production and PLA waste valorization.

title: Quantitative Steric Hindrance to Determine Pressure-Induced Emission Harvesting
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Pressure engineering enables distinctive pressure-induced emission (PIE) and piezochromism in halide perovskites, yet structural reversibility generally prevents ambient condition retention of high-pressure metastable states (HPMS), limiting their practical optoelectronic applications. This perspective compares PIE retention behavior across all-inorganic, aliphatic-cation, and aromatic-cation hybrid halide perovskites. Insufficient steric hindrance yields fully reversible responses in inorganic and aliphatic systems, whereas rigid aromatic cations elevate phase-transition barriers and kinetically trap HPMS after decompression. The steric-effect index (SEI, critical threshold 2.3) quantitatively distinguishes reversible systems from those capable of HPMS retention, establishing a link between cation molecular geometry and PIE persistence. We highlight outstanding quantitative structure–property challenges and outline future research directions, including machine-learning-guided screening, advanced high-pressure characterization, and new strategies for metastable-state stabilization. Extending PIE to phosphorescent and chiral luminescence further expands opportunities for applications in optical anticounterfeiting, information storage, sensing, and display technologies.

title: Blue-Hazard Free WOLEDs with High Efficiency and Color-Rendering Index by Exciton Confinement and Energy Transfer Sensitization from Bluish-Green Emitter to Ultrathin Light-Emitting Layer
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract White organic light-emitting diodes (WOLEDs) demonstrate tremendous potential as next-generation light sources. However, the simultaneous achievement of ideal white emission and high efficiency remains a significant challenge. This work proposes a solution by inserting low-mobility light-emitting layers (EMLs) on both sides of the high-mobility EML and introducing ultrathin red phosphorescent EMLs to regulate exciton distribution and energy transfer processes. The obtained WOLEDs achieve the maximum power efficiency and external quantum efficiency up to 77.1 lm W–1 and 32.2%, respectively, which maintain 52.8 lm W–1 and 29.5% at 1000 cd m–2. Concurrently, the devices exhibit color rendering index exceeding 80 within a luminance range from 1000 to 80000 cd m–2, accompanied by complete elimination of harmful blue emission. Time-resolved photoluminescence spectroscopy reveals that the red emission of WOLEDs based on ultrathin red EMLs mainly originates from energy transfer through the quasi-equatorial conformer of bluish-green emitter DMAC-TRZ. This work elucidates the concealed photophysical mechanisms in WOLEDs based on ultrathin EMLs while presenting a promising strategy for energy-efficient and blue-hazard free lighting technologies.

title: Growth-Spiral Control of Defect Topology and Local Vertical Piezoresponse in Bi4Ti3O12 Thin Films
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Aurivillius phase materials are layered ferroelectrics with high thermal stability (>600 °C) and fatigue resistance, yet their polarization is predominantly in-plane, limiting integration into vertical device architectures relevant to future memory, data storage, and neuromorphic computing concepts. Achieving robust vertical polarization in these systems remains fundamentally challenging because of crystallographic symmetry constraints. Although defects can locally reorient polarization, deterministic control of defect topology through growth-mode engineering remains largely unexplored in layered ferroelectrics. Here, we demonstrate that precise control of nominal precursor loading and oxygen partial pressure during direct liquid injection chemical vapor deposition enables a transition in epitaxial Bi4Ti3O12 thin films from two-dimensional growth to dislocation-mediated, chiral spiral growth. This work introduces growth spirals as a controllable route to engineer defect topology and grain morphology, rather than relying on post-growth or stochastic defect formation. Atomic-resolution microscopy and piezoresponse force microscopy reveal that chiral spiral-mediated morphologies exhibit a 135% higher local vertical piezoresponse amplitude and a reduced local vertical switching bias from ±20 to ±5 V compared with two-dimensional films. High-angle annular dark field scanning transmission electron microscopy (HAADF-STEM) displacement mapping and density functional theory indicate that out-of-phase boundary defect-associated local structural distortions modify local symmetry, bonding, and strain in a manner consistent with an enhanced out-of-plane polarization component and local vertical electromechanical response. These results establish spiral-driven defect topology as a growth-controlled pathway for tuning the local vertical piezoresponse in layered ferroelectrics and suggest a broadly applicable design principle for future low-power vertical ferroelectric oxide devices.

title: Can a liquid “harden” a “soft” solid? Solvent-induced rigidification in luminescent porous polymers
abstract: Liquids typically soften solids, but whether this holds when liquids are confined within the nanopores of crosslinked networks remains unclear. Here, common solvents entering a flexible luminescent porous polymer restrict intramolecular motion of the AIEgen units, suppressing nonradiative decay and enhancing quantum yield 1.8-fold. This reversible, optically readable rigidification offers a design principle for responsive porous materials.

title: Self-Powered Actuation of Commercial UV Sensors via Single-Electrode Triboelectric Nanogenerators Using Self-Exposed MXene Nanosheets in Porous Dielectrics
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Triboelectric nanogenerators (TENGs) have emerged as pivotal sustainable energy harvesters. However, single-electrode configurations, despite their structural simplicity and seamless circuit integration, suffer from inherently low output performance compared to double-electrode systems, primarily due to the absence of a top electrode and reduced potential difference across the dielectric layer. To overcome this limitation, we report a high-output, single-electrode TENG platform featuring a porous dielectric layer with self-exposed MXene nanosheets. By monolithically integrating this layer onto a flexible electrode via a water steaming process, we simultaneously achieve structural and interfacial modifications that promote charge accumulation and electrostatic induction. Specifically, the porous structure increases the effective contact area, while the migration and self-exposure of hydrophilic MXene nanosheets at the water–polydimethylsiloxane interfaces during droplet-templating modify the surface electrostatic properties, enhancing the triboelectric performance of the device. The resulting device delivers a remarkable peak power density of 5870 mW/m2 under hand tapping. Crucially, this superior output achieves a 24–28% faster charging rate than MXene-embedded counterparts.
