The practical utility of our platform is validated through the successful actuation of a commercial UV index sensor system. Operated entirely without external power, the seamless integration of this TENG with standard electronic components demonstrates a fully independent, self-sustainable power solution for practical environmental monitoring. This study provides a robust strategy to enhance energy-harvesting performance of single-electrode TENGs, thereby enabling diverse self-powered applications in next generation electronics.

title: Electron-Donation and Hydrophilicity Synergy in Side-Chain Engineered COFs: Enhanced Photocatalytic U(VI) Reduction
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The photocatalytic U(VI) reduction is vital for radioactive wastewater treatment, yet covalent organic frameworks (COFs) face limitations in charge carrier separation and transport, with insufficient studies on functional group effects. Herein, three donor–acceptor COFs (TfBD, TfBD-CH3, and TfBD-OH) were synthesized to investigate electron-donating group modifications. Enhanced light absorption, narrowed bandgaps, increased photocurrent density, and reduced impedance were confirmed. Consequently, the reduction efficiency of U(VI) increased from 73% for TfBD to 77% for TfBD-CH3 and 91% for TfBD-OH, with stronger electron-donating ability leading to superior performance. TfBD-OH exhibited comparable removal efficiency in uranium-spiked seawater due to its synergistic effect of hydrophilicity and electron-donating groups. DFT calculations showed that TfBD-OH had the lowest adsorption energy for U(VI), while photogenerated H2O2 promoted U(VI) removal via formation of (UO2)O2·2H2O precipitates. This study demonstrates a viable strategy for side-chain-modified COFs in photocatalytic uranium enrichment.

title: The emerging geopolitics of sustainable aviation fuel: Policy architectures, book-and-claim and european strategic dependencies
abstract: Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF) is becoming a strategic component of aviation decarbonization, but its expansion depends on technological, economic, institutional, and resource conditions. This study compares the combinations of policy instruments, structural production characteristics, and market-governance arrangements observed in the European Union, the United States, the United Kingdom, Japan, Singapore, and Brazil, and considers the potential strategic vulnerabilities these configurations suggest, particularly for the European Union. The comparative qualitative policy analysis draws on peer-reviewed literature, legislation, regulatory documents, and institutional sources, organized through a single four-part framework: policy-instrument mix; structural production conditions; market and governance conditions; and potential strategic vulnerabilities. The cases display different configurations. The European Union and the United Kingdom emphasize mandatory demand; the United States relies more heavily on producer incentives; Japan and Singapore emphasize coordination and supply security; and Brazil combines established biofuel capabilities with a developing SAF framework. These observations do not identify causal effects or rank the configurations. Instead, they indicate possible exposure to feedstock, production, finance, policy-continuity, import, and certification constraints. Book-and-Claim is examined as a governance arrangement that separates environmental attributes from physical fuel flows; its practical contribution depends on credible certification, verification, registry governance, and interoperability. For the European Union, the comparison suggests that regulatory leadership may coexist with external supply and institutional dependencies. The concept of resilient interdependence is therefore proposed as a policy lens rather than a measured outcome.

title: Local Delivery of Astragalus Polysaccharide via Alginate Hydrogels to Inhibit Postoperative Osteosarcoma Recurrence and Metastasis
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The recurrence and metastasis of osteosarcoma after surgery and chemotherapy treatments are still a clinical challenge. Astragalus polysaccharide (APS) possesses notable antitumor activity but rather low bioavailability after intravenous or oral administration. Herein, a porous composite hydrogel combined with alginate (ALG) was prepared for the efficient local delivery of APS, which demonstrated a biphasic release profile with an initial burst release in the first several hours and a sustained release in the long term. The APS/ALG-Ca2+ gel exhibited antitumor activity, specifically enhancing the inhibition of cell proliferation with an inhibition rate of 97.85 ± 0.29% within 48 h, demonstrating cytotoxicity approximately equivalent to a 5-fold dose of APS solution. The promotion of apoptosis was also shown by the increased expression of cleaved caspase-3 by ∼11-fold in vivo. Concurrently, its inhibitory effect on cell migration was validated through a Transwell assay in vitro and metastatic foci in livers and lungs in vivo (with significantly decreased expression of platelet-derived growth factor D (PDGFD) and receptor beta (PDGFRB)). Furthermore, in mouse models, it demonstrated sustained suppression of osteosarcoma recurrence following B-cell maturation in the spleen. Our findings suggested that the APS/ALG-Ca2+ gel could be a feasible local adjuvant strategy of postsurgical osteosarcoma for further preclinical evaluation.

title: Machine-learning-driven identification of cooperative descriptors for polysulfide conversion on spinel oxides
abstract:
Spinel oxides have emerged as promising catalysts for polysulfide conversion, yet a comprehensive design strategy that elucidates the underlying structure–property relationship across diverse spinel oxides remains elusive. The complex multistep conversion processes make single descriptors insufficient to capture the full catalytic behavior, whereas identifying cooperative descriptors introduces additional complexity that challenges manual analysis. Here, we employ a machine-learning–assisted approach to uncover universal cooperative descriptors and accelerate the discovery of high-performance spinel catalysts. We reveal that the intrinsic polysulfide conversion efficiency of spinel oxides is cooperatively governed by two structural features. Further screening of promising catalysts is conducted using the extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost) algorithm, achieving rapid and accurate prediction of these features on spinel oxides. The model identifies Fe
                    2
                    CoO
                    4
                    and Fe
                    2
                    NiO
                    4
                    as superior catalysts, which are experimentally validated to exhibit excellent performance. This work provides deep mechanistic insights and a powerful data-driven framework for the rational design of spinel catalysts, with potential extension to other applications.

title: Edge computing and interoperability in energy consumption prediction for smart grids
abstract: The design and implementation of a deterministic point forecasting algorithm adapted for resource-constrained devices are presented herein, enabling efficient electricity load/production prediction with a 100-minute horizon. The algorithm is integrated with an elastic energy management system to facilitate real-time dynamic decision-making. Validation of the proposed method was conducted within an Edge Computing architecture simulating a smart-meter environment, specifically designed to minimize latency. Quantitative validation confirms high predictive accuracy: under diagnostic open-loop conditions, the network achieves a Mean Absolute Error of 0.4008 kW and an open-loop Mean Absolute Scaled Error of 0.9665 ($< 1.0$). Crucially, under extended 100-minute recursive closed-loop telemetry outage conditions, the proposed Residual Harmonic architecture delivers a data supplementation MAE of 4.2354 kW, representing a validated 18.08% improvement over the Persistence baseline. With an average inference latency of 8.44 ms on commodity edge hardware, the solution is demonstrated to be effective for Distribution System Operator processes requiring timely and reliable data supplementation.

title: Globally antiaromatic anthracene–porphyrin nanobelts
abstract:
Abstract
                  
                    Conjugated molecular belts attract increasing attention because of the unusual electronic and magnetic behaviour arising from their radially oriented
                    p
                    orbitals. A π-conjugated molecular belt is expected to behave like a quantum ring, showing global aromatic or antiaromatic ring currents, but in most hydrocarbon benzenoid belts, localized Clar sextets preclude the emergence of global ring currents. Here we report the synthesis of anthracene-bridged porphyrin nanobelts that sustain global antiaromatic ring currents in the neutral state. Macrocyclization was achieved by nickel(0)-mediated Yamamoto coupling. Scholl oxidation with DDQ/TfOH, promoted by electron-donating methoxy substituents, yielded the strained triple-stranded nanobelts. These hybrid nanobelts show global antiaromaticity, with Hückel circuits of 72, 96 or 120 π electrons, as revealed by
                    1
                    H NMR spectroscopy and corroborated by computational analysis. This work establishes a platform for synthesizing other heterocyclic nanobelts, in cases where the corresponding hydrocarbon nanobelt is not yet synthetically accessible.

title: Four-dimensional X-ray nano-holotomography reveals multiscale chemomechanics in composite graphite–silicon battery electrodes
abstract: Linking electrode microstructure to electrochemical performance is essential for optimizing Li-ion batteries. However, this requires mechanistic four-dimensional observations at the ultimate spatiotemporal scales, which remain elusive. Here we demonstrate the use of interrupted-operando synchrotron X-ray nano-holotomography combined with digital volume correlation to track chemomechanical dynamics at both particle (local) and electrode (averaged) scales. Quantitative scale-bridging image analysis is applied to composite graphite-silicon electrodes during their electrochemical formation cycle. Our findings reveal that local ionic diffusion properties, graphite particle morphology and position in the electrode, distance to silicon clusters, surface contact with the liquid electrolyte solution, and mechanical deformations all directly affect local electrochemical activity and irreversibility, although these parameters are not equally important. In particular, we identify fast ionic diffusion channels that play a key role and counterbalance intrinsic depth-dependent reaction heterogeneities arising from ionic and electronic diffusion limitations. The various structural factors that determine the electrochemical performance of composite graphite-silicon electrodes in Li-ion batteries beyond ensemble properties are classified using a scale of influence, providing a practical framework for the optimization of materials and electrode manufacturing.

title: The microbial world of male reproduction
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
abstract: The last decade has brought renewed interest to microbial influences on host biology, yet the roles of microbes in host reproductive biology are underappreciated and often defined by a profound maternal bias. This perspective synthesizes emerging evidence across the tree of life to highlight the paternal microbiome as an overlooked driver of fitness, reproductive output, and intergenerational health, impacting epigenetic sculpting of the sperm and embryo, sexual transmission of microbes, and male gamete functions. These contributions indicate that mating can involve interactions between holobionts rather than simply the union of the maternal and paternal genomes. Thus, uniting male reproduction with the growing generalizations of microbial symbiosis guides several conceptual, theoretical, and empirical avenues for research in the life sciences.

title: A genome-wide senescence synthetic lethality screen identifies PARP16 as a senolytic target
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
abstract: Accumulation of senescent cells is increasingly viewed as a significant contributor to aging and age-related diseases. To date, the elimination of senescent cells through small molecule senolytic agents has largely relied on a limited number of repurposed agents, often leveraged from previous oncological applications. Here, we describe a CRISPR-based, genome-wide, synthetic lethal screen for senescent cells. From this screen, we identify a number of genes whose deletion appears to be well tolerated in normal proliferating cells, but whose deletion is lethal in the context of senescence. We further characterize one promising candidate gene encoding the ER-resident protein PARP16. Knockdown of PARP16 does not affect the viability of mouse or human cells but results in the death of a wide range of senescent cells. Furthermore, two distinct small molecule PARP16 inhibitors have little effect of normal cell growth but result in the selective death of senescent cells in culture and in freshly isolated human donor lung tissue explants. Together, these results demonstrate a rational strategy to identify novel senolytic therapies that could have potential applications for a wide range of age-related conditions.

title: Harness design matters for AI capabilities in mathematics
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
abstract: To assess the ability of current AI systems to correctly solve research-level mathematics problems, we tested four AI systems on a set of ten problems in a broad range of mathematical fields; these problems arose naturally in the research process of the contributors. This document includes our methodology, and the results of our testing, including the assessment of human reviewers and a report of costs. We provide links to supplementary documents including the human solutions, the AI-generated solutions, and the referee reports and logs for the AI-generated solutions.

title: Antireflective bilayer metasurfaces with complete wavefront control
abstract: Antireflection coatings are widely used in optical systems to increase transmission and suppress unwanted reflections by matching the optical impedance across a uniform interface. Applying the same idea to metasurfaces is fundamentally more challenging because their wavefront control relies on arrays of geometrically distinct meta-atoms, presenting as a spatially varying optical impedance. Here we show that vertical integration can overcome this limitation by allowing bilayer meta-atoms to act simultaneously as phase shifters and impedance-matching stacks. By treating meta-atoms as multilayer thin films, we derive a design rule that links the effective refractive indices of two independently patterned layers and identifies antireflective bilayer libraries with full 0-2π transmission phase coverage. We demonstrate the approach with a free-standing TiO2/TiO2 metalens operating at 1,310 nm, which suppresses reflection below that of bare glass while maintaining diffraction-limited focusing. These results establish bilayer metasurfaces as a platform for jointly engineering optical impedance and wavefront response at the meta-atom level.

title: Windblown dunes are born in sand at the brink of transport
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
abstract: Windblown dunes are found everywhere in the Solar System where a supply of loose sediment is mobilized by gas flows, from the sluggish winds of Venus to speed-of-sound sublimation flows on comets. Their abundance is nontrivial because dunes only form where grains hop ballistically (“saltate”). This implies that winds across the Solar System reach “goldilocks” speeds that are just right to initiate and maintain saltation of whatever sediment is available despite vast variations in material and fluid properties, and gravity. Based on select observations, it was proposed that dune fields may be characterized by a near-threshold transport state where dune-forming winds minimally exceed the saltation threshold on Earth. Here, we demonstrate that this is indeed the case globally. Next, we show that, unlike riverbeds—which evolve to a similar state through adjustments of channel geometry—dune fields are born in it due to the rapid decrease in wind frequency with increasing wind speed. These results imply that grain sizes in windblown dunes provide a robust record of formative winds, such that corresponding wind speeds can be estimated from aeolian sandstones and dune deposits across planets. The near-threshold state of windblown dunes thus opens a promising line of investigation for paleoenvironmental and paleoclimate reconstructions on Earth and beyond.

title: A zero-one law for one-shot system identification
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
abstract: Can a model be identified from one experiment? We study analytic systems that are linearly parameterized by a combination of prescribed dictionary terms, such as partial differential operators and dynamical systems. For a single input-response pair, recovery is possible exactly when the evaluated dictionary terms are linearly independent. We prove a sharp zero-one law: either no input uniquely determines the coefficients, or almost every random input sampled from a nondegenerate Gaussian measure does. This dichotomy reduces one-shot system identification to a question about degenerate inputs and provides an a posteriori certificate in the noiseless setting. Numerical examples recover dynamical systems, nonlinear partial differential equations, and structured matrix families from single trajectory data, while also detecting when an extra probe is necessary.

title: Improving compatibility in mixed-matrix membranes
abstract: Mixed-matrix membranes promise to combine the processability of polymers with the transport advantages of porous fillers, yet poor compatibility between the two limits their performance. New research shows that tailoring interfaces between polymers and covalent organic frameworks enables high filler loadings, producing improved membranes for carbon capture.

title: Environmental and material implications of global climate mitigation pathways
abstract:
Abstract
                  Reaching the goals of the Paris Agreement requires a rapid transformation of global energy systems. Yet, energy supply and use exert multiple pressures on ecosystems, human health and natural resources, raising questions about the broader environmental consequences of alternative decarbonization pathways and the resources they require. Here we analyse 24 climate mitigation pathways from three integrated assessment models using a life-cycle perspective. This enables a system-wide comparison of environmental impacts and resource requirements of global final energy provision from 2020 to 2100. We find that deep decarbonization delivers substantial cobenefits for human health and ecosystem quality, but does not systematically reduce pressures on land, water or mineral resource extraction. For metals central to electrification, climate change mitigation ambition primarily reshapes the timing of extraction rather than cumulative volumes. Pathways achieving similar climate targets can impose markedly different environmental and resource pressures, shaping the feasibility and desirability of alternative transitions.

title: High-loading all-solid-state lithium–sulfur batteries enabled by tailored sulfur–sulfide and sulfur–carbon interfaces
abstract: High energy density promised by solid-state batteries requires overcoming fundamental limitations in carrier transport. Although tortuous carrier pathways in high-loading cathodes are often viewed as the dominant bottleneck, we show that interfacial ion and electron transport is an even more critical lever for enhancing energy density in sulfide-based all-solid-state lithium-sulfur batteries. By enabling partial lithiation at the sulfur-sulfide interface and eliminating the electron-impeding oxidation layer at the sulfur-carbon interface, we achieve high-loading all-solid-state lithium-sulfur battery cathodes with areal capacities near 15 mAh cm-2 and sulfur utilization above 90% with a moderate stack pressure of 15-25 MPa. These metrics correspond to projected pouch-cell-level energy densities surpassing 500 Wh kg-1. Fast cycling at 1C retains 82.1% capacity over 500 cycles with Coulombic efficiencies up to 99.9%, and stable cycling is also achieved with a lithium metal anode at 10 MPa instead of the more common Li-In alloy. This work highlights the power of interfacial control within composite cathodes, and demonstrates another approach for designing high-energy-density all-solid-state lithium-sulfur batteries for next-generation energy storage.

title: Rethinking Creep in Solid-State Batteries: From a Chemo-mechanical Liability to a Design Parameter
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Creep is an inherent time-dependent mechanical response in alkali-metal-based solid-state batteries (SSBs) subjected to sustained stack pressure. Although creep can significantly influence battery performance, its role has often been interpreted narrowly as either a beneficial mechanism for maintaining interfacial contact or a detrimental contributor to cell degradation. In this perspective, we establish a unified conceptual framework by linking sustained loading in the classical definition of creep to stack pressure in SSBs, thereby explaining why creep is intrinsic to their operation. We further argue that creep should be regarded as a chemo-mechanical phenomenon with inherently dual roles, whose competing effects govern the dynamic evolution of electrode–electrolyte interfaces during electrochemical cycling. Finally, we discuss how timescale-based design principles and time-resolved in situ and operando characterization can deepen understanding and guide the rational optimization of creep under practical battery operating conditions, thereby informing the design of durable next-generation alkali-metal SSBs.

title: O6-type layered oxides for sustainable high-energy battery cathodes
abstract: Cobalt-free cathodes are vital for green energy but suffer from structural instability. Here the authors report a unique O6-type framework that stabilizes oxygen redox for exceptional cycling durability.

abstract: Plant fungal pathogens in crops can lead to substantial economic losses and pose a severe threat to food security. title: Harnessing lattice distortion for point-defect self-healing in multi-principal element alloys
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
abstract: Multi-principal element alloys are promising structural materials for nuclear, aerospace, and fusion applications, yet their accelerated discovery is limited by the prohibitive cost of evaluating point-defect transport and self-healing behavior across vast compositional spaces. Here, we establish local lattice distortion (LLD), an intrinsic feature of chemically complex alloys, as a predictive and universal descriptor for vacancy–interstitial diffusivity convergence. We develop and validate a high-fidelity machine-learning interatomic potential based on the moment tensor potential formalism for body-centered-cubic Zr–Ti–Nb alloys, enabling accurate large-scale simulations of defect energetics and migration. Molecular dynamics simulations reveal a robust inverse correlation between LLD and the activation energy disparity between vacancies and interstitials. This relationship is further validated in face-centered-cubic V–Co–Ni and Ni–Pd systems, demonstrating transferability across distinct chemistries and crystal structures. LLD-induced narrowing of vacancy–interstitial mobility differences promotes Frenkel pair recombination and defect self-healing. Mechanistically, vacancy diffusion is governed by the energy barrier associated with bond-length compression at the saddle state, together with statistical sampling of low-barrier jumps mediated by oversized atoms. These findings establish lattice distortion as a powerful, physically grounded design lever that links nanoscale disorder to point-defect self-healing, offering a practical pathway for the accelerated discovery of next-generation structural materials for extreme environments.

title: Concurrent atmospheric phenomena amplify precipitation extremes under anthropogenic climate change
abstract: Extreme precipitation events are increasing in many regions. Here the authors discuss how the increasing concurrence of atmospheric phenomena could contribute to these trends under anthropogenic warming.

title: Climate and glacier geometry dominate global glacier–lake interactions
abstract: The contribution of glacial lakes to glacier mass loss is unclear. This work maps global glacial lakes in 2000 and 2020 to quantify changes in number, volume and area, showing that they explain 11 ± 7% of lake-terminating glacier loss, with climate forcing and glacier geometry the dominant factors.

title: Knowledge gaps and scientific progress
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
abstract: Knowledge production is often viewed as an endogenous process in which discovery arises through the recombination of existing theories, findings, and concepts. Yet not all recombinations are equally valuable, and identifying those that may prove most generative remains challenging. We propose that a crucial form of recombination occurs when linking concepts creates knowledge gaps—empty regions in the conceptual landscape that may focus scientific attention on unexplored connections. Using computational topology, we develop a method to identify knowledge gaps in science at scale. In this framework, gaps form when new connections complete cycles in evolving networks of scientific concepts. We apply the method to 34,363,623 papers in Microsoft Academic Graph spanning 1900 to 2020. The main analyses use samples ranging from 8,643,571 to 31,983,201 papers. Compared with papers that introduce novel concept pairs without opening gaps, gap-opening papers have greater long-term citation impact, are more disruptive of prior work, and exhibit greater delayed recognition. Gap-opening papers receive fewer citations within five years of publication but more over twenty years, consistent with scientific communities needing time to recognize and develop newly opened research territories. Evidence for the generative capacity of gap-opening papers—as indicated by high citation impact and disruption—replicates in five additional databases (OpenAlex, the PubMed Knowledge Graph, Dimensions, American Physical Society journals, and United States patents) and across eight concept vocabularies, including several derived directly from text. Together, these results point to a distinctive generative role for gap opening in scientific discovery.

title: Mitigating the Optical-Electrical Trade-Off in Sb2S3 Solar Cells with a Buried Li-Modified ZnO Interlayer
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Thinning CdS electron-selective layers reduces parasitic blue-light absorption in Sb2S3 solar cells but can compromise charge collection and absorber growth. Here, we address this optical-electrical trade-off through crystal-structure-guided buried interface engineering. Exploiting the shared wurtzite structure of ZnO and CdS, we introduce a ZnO interlayer to regulate CdS formation. Reducing CdS thickness from 70 to 30 nm enhances Sb2S3 absorptance at 400–500 nm but decreases internal quantum efficiency (IQE) and increases nonradiative voltage loss, offsetting the optical gain. Undoped sol-gel ZnO improves CdS uniformity and partially restores the cathode contact response without improving long-range structural order. Li modification produces a more ordered ZnO/CdS stack, lowers the ZnO work function, and improves Sb2S3 texture and morphology. Consequently, IQE reaches 94%, with a champion power conversion efficiency of 8.10%. These findings establish a crystallography-guided strategy for integrating optical, electrical, and structural optimization.

title: Influence of Local Curvature and Structural Chirality on Magnetic Spin Textures in Fe Thin‐Film Möbius Bands
abstract: ABSTRACT The Möbius band is a fascinating three‐dimensional (3D) architecture that exhibits a geometric chirality where left‐ and right‐handed twists cannot be interchanged via continuous rotation, along with a varying extrinsic curvature. Here, we demonstrate that spin textures in arrays of Fe magnetic Möbius structures are fundamentally governed by their geometric chirality and extrinsic curvature. Magnetic full‐field soft x‐ray transmission microscopy reveals that the unique geometry drives domain fragmentation into nontrivial arrangements in regions of maximal curvature, along with the formation of nontrivial vortex domains. Magnetometry and first‐order reversal curve measurements reveal a complex magnetization reversal process, as the lateral and vertical portions of the Möbius structures respond differently to in‐plane and out‐of‐plane applied fields. Micromagnetic simulations confirm a vortex state with geometry‐driven preferred circulation direction. The resulting spin textures propagate either clockwise or counterclockwise along the Möbius structures, depending on the direction of an in‐plane magnetic field applied along the primary bend of the structure. These geometric‐chirality‐driven effects are manifested in the experimentally captured evolution of the remanent magnetization. Our results demonstrate a new platform where curvature and real space topology of 3D nanostructures may be used as degrees of freedom to tailor spin textures.

title: Synergistic Integration of Materials and Design Strategies for Next‐Generation Stretchable Displays
abstract: ABSTRACT Stretchable displays rely on sophisticated integration enabled by materials engineering, structural strategies, and micro‐nano integration, encompassing stretchable substrates, conducting and semiconducting components. This review provides a focused discussion of recent technological advances. We highlight key innovations in stretchable electrodes, interconnects, emissive materials, transistor arrays, circuit layouts, and deformable substrates for their roles in improving electrical uniformity, mechanical resilience, and display performance. Additionally, we summarize the latest strategies for achieving stretchability, either by using intrinsically elastic electronic materials or by structurally engineering rigid components. We introduce emerging applications with substantial potential, including epidermal human‐machine interfaces, conformal biomedical monitoring and visualization, soft robotics with distributed optical feedback, and skin‐integrated augmented reality (AR)/virtual reality (VR) systems, to illustrate the transformative opportunities ahead for stretchable display technologies.

title: Electronic Spin States in Oxygen Reduction: From Identification Divergence to Mechanism Clarification
abstract: ABSTRACT The oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) is a cornerstone process in clean‐energy technologies including fuel cells, metal–air batteries, and electrochemical hydrogen peroxide synthesis. Emerging evidence has established the electronic spin states of transition‐metal active centers as a critical descriptor that governs ORR activity and selectivity, yet present studies of the same metal center have reported divergent electronic spin states and ORR pathway selectivity. This review attempts to perform a comprehensive discussion about this divergence. The fundamentals of spin states are first introduced within the frameworks of crystal field theory and molecular orbital theory and the principal characterization techniques for spin states identification. Subsequently, the contradictory correlations between spin states and ORR selectivity reported in different catalytic systems are critically analyzed in terms of d ‐orbital occupancy and reaction kinetics. Furthermore, rationally regulating spin states strategies are elucidated to optimize ORR performance. Finally, key challenges and future research directions are outlined, emphasizing the need for in situ characterization, advanced theoretical modeling, and unambiguous identification of active sites. This review will furnish theoretical guidance for subsequent investigations of spin effects, and provide insights into extending spin state engineering to other small‐molecule electrocatalytic reactions.

title: Strong and Thermally Conductive Graphene‐Bamboo Nanocomposites by Topological Fiber‐Network Engineering Towards Intelligent Energy‐Efficient Floors
abstract: ABSTRACT Smart floor‐heating systems that integrate occupancy sensing with localized thermal regulation offer a promising route toward low‐carbon buildings, yet existing flooring materials cannot simultaneously provide robust mechanical properties and rapid heat delivery. Here, a topological fiber‐network engineering and thermorheology‐assisted assembly strategy is reported that enables continuous thermal‐transport and load‐bearing networks to coexist within a single material. Long bamboo fibers form a topologically entangled framework that simultaneously serves as a mechanically robust scaffold and a three‐dimensional template for graphene nanoplatelet assembly, while thermorheological phenol‐formaldehyde (PF) resin facilitates their rearrangement into ordered face‐to‐face configurations under low pressure. The resulting graphene–bamboo composites (GBC) exhibit metal‐level thermal conductivities of 12.8–116.7 W m − 1 K − 1 together with outstanding flexural strengths of 75–155 MPa, outperforming conventional flooring materials. When integrated into a pressure‐sensing smart floor‐heating system, the composites enable rapid thermal homogenization and occupant‐responsive localized heating. Whole‐building simulations indicate that nationwide adoption of the composite in pressure‐sensing smart floor‐heating systems in China could reduce annual heating‐electricity consumption by up to ∼208 TWh, corresponding to a ∼37% reduction compared with conventional wood flooring. This work establishes the integration of topological fiber‐network engineering with thermorheology‐assisted assembly as a general strategy for overcoming the thermal–mechanical trade‐off in structural biomass composites and advancing energy‐efficient building materials.

title: Trace‐Metal‐Assisted Flash Synthesis for Fast‐Charging Graphite Anodes
abstract: ABSTRACT Graphite has remained the dominant anode material in lithium–ion batteries (LIBs), powering portable electronics and electric vehicles (EVs). However, sluggish Li + diffusion kinetics in natural and synthetic graphite can severely limit charging rates. Overcoming this bottleneck requires the rational design of graphite architectures that enable rapid Li + transport in LIBs. Here, we disclose a trace‐metal‐assisted flash (TMF) process for the millisecond synthesis of catalytic flashed graphite (CFGr) with exceptionally fast‐charging capabilities. The TMF process induces in situ formation of trace nickel nanoclusters that catalyze ultrafast graphitization of amorphous carbon into highly ordered graphite within I D / I G of 0.09, with calculations yielding an interlayer bonding energy ( E b ) of −2.297 eV, while diffraction reveals an interlayer spacing (d 002 ) of 3.4 Å. These features enhance structural stability and Li + accessibility. Consequently, optimized CFGr achieves a high reversible capacity of 347.4 mAh g −1 at 0.25 C and retains 158.8 mAh g −1 at 15 C with 80% capacity retention after 1000 cycles, outperforming the rate and cyclability of both commercial graphite and graphite prepared by flash Joule heating. The TMF route can replace conventional energy‐intensive graphitization, reducing energy use and emissions by over 80% and lowering the production cost of premium fast‐charging synthetic graphite by ∼80% to only US$0.84 kg −1 . These findings establish a promising pathway to advance fast‐charging graphite anodes into next‐generation LIBs.

title: Bioinspired Molecular‐Scale Tape Interface Towards Ultrahigh‐Pixel‐Density Flexible Quantum Dot Light‐Emitting Devices
abstract: ABSTRACT Flexible, high‐density integrated optoelectronics underpin emerging wearable information systems and human–machine interfaces. However, as pixel size decreases to a few micrometers, emission uniformity and performance of flexible light emitting diodes (LED) degrade severely due to microscale electrical and optical nonuniformity of electrodes especially after bending, hindering their potential applications. Inspired by fish scales, we propose a molecular‐scale tape interface as a transparent electrode for ultrahigh‐pixel‐density flexible LEDs. An atomically thin MXene layer, assembled via liquid–air interfacial assembly, conformally adheres to indium tin oxide through reversible hydrogen bonding and van der Waals coupling, enabling stress redistribution, crack bridging, and potential homogenization. This electrode enables flexible quantum‐dot LEDs with uniform micro‐area current and emission up to 25 400 ppi and a record external quantum efficiency (EQE) of 23.4%, maintaining performance after 3000 bending cycles. This biomimetic transparent‐electrode interfacial strategy unites mechanical flexibility with ultrahigh pixel density, advancing high‐density integrated optoelectronic architectures.

title: Molecular Engineering of Redox Mediator for Accelerated Multi‐Electron Transfer Reactions in Lithium Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Lithium–sulfur and lithium–oxygen batteries are highly attractive due to their ultrahigh theoretical energy densities, while their performance is severely constrained by sluggish multiphase reaction rates and limited reaction stability at the cathodes. The conventional solid‐phase catalysts suffer from small interfacial contact area and activity loss of active sites, while the mobile redox mediators (RMs) present a new paradigm for accelerating multi‐electron transfer pathways through a solution‐mediated electron transfer pathway. This review first discusses the critical rate‐limiting factors governing reaction rate at the cathode, and then systematically examines the latest advances in the molecular engineering of RMs for cathode catalysis from the viewpoint of redox potential, solubility, molecular size, and chemical stability. Following these points, we comprehensively analyze, from both thermodynamic and kinetic perspectives, how the molecular engineering of RMs affects the redox potential, solubility, stability, and so on. These characteristics strongly dictate the specific capacity and lifespan, elucidating key structure–activity relationships. Finally, we propose systemic strategies expanding beyond isolated liquid‐phase catalysis toward solid–liquid synergistic design and functionalized electrolyte/separator engineering.

title: Advances and Perspectives of Cobalt‐Free Li‐Rich Mn‐Based Layered Oxide Cathodes
abstract: ABSTRACT Lithium‐rich manganese‐based oxides (LRMOs) are prioritized for next‐generation batteries due to their high theoretical specific capacity and energy density. In particular, the cobalt‐free LRMOs offer additional competitive advantages due to their lowered production cost and reduced resource dependence. However, the cobalt‐free LRMOs still suffer from persistent structural stability challenges, exhibiting low initial Coulombic efficiency, rapid capacity and voltage decay, and inferior rate capability. To advance cobalt‐free LRMO development, massive research efforts focused on effective regulation strategies have emerged recently. It is therefore imperative to timely summarize these recent works to systematically evaluate the attained achievements, recognize the unresolved issues, and formulate the key optimization approaches in the next stage; however, such related reviews for cobalt‐free LRMOs remain limited. Herein, we carefully examine the fundamental advances in cobalt‐free LRMOs and give a comprehensive review work. Initially, the microstructure of cobalt‐free LRMOs is dissected, and the corresponding electrochemical mechanism is elucidated. In addition, the faced challenges are described and analyzed in detail. More importantly, the currently proposed modification strategies are primarily discussed from the microstructure regulation, element doping and surface coating views. Finally, the significant perspectives are highlighted.

title: Re‐Evaluating the Role of Water in Hexacyanoferrate Cathodes for Sodium and Potassium Ion Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Hexacyanoferrates (HCFs) are among the most promising cathode materials for sodium‐ion and potassium‐ion batteries owing to their open three‐dimensional framework, high operating voltage, and fast alkali‐ion transport. As an unavoidable constituent of hexacyanoferrates (HCFs), water is intimately associated with crystal growth, vacancy formation, local coordination, and framework stability. Water has long been regarded primarily as a detrimental impurity in cathodes because it blocks ion transport, accelerates electrolyte decomposition, and promotes structural degradation. However, recent studies indicate that interstitial and coordinated water exhibit distinct binding strengths, mobilities, and electrochemical reactivities, rendering their roles far more complex than can be described by total water content alone. In this Review, we re‐evaluate the role of water in HCF cathodes by redefining it from a structural impurity to a functional component. We discuss how water governs crystal structure, electronic structure, ion transport, interfacial reactions, and electrochemical performance. We further summarize advanced characterization techniques, particularly neutron methods, for probing the dynamic behavior of water molecules, and highlight regulation strategies. This work establishes a unified framework linking water with crystal, electronic structure, and electrochemical behavior, providing guidance for the rational design of high‐performance HCF cathodes.

title: Light-guided photophosphorylation nanorobot rescues injured cardiomyocytes via in situ bioenergetic restoration
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Myocardial injury is a leading cause of death worldwide and is accompanied by profound mitochondrial bioenergetic dysfunction in impaired cardiomyocytes. Restoring cellular bioenergetic homeostasis could be a promising strategy to promote cardiac repair; however, current clinical adenosine triphosphate (ATP) injection therapies yield limited efficacy due to the inability to achieve in situ, targeted delivery. Here, we develop a photoactivated phosphorylation nanorobot engineered to rescue impaired metabolism via targeted, in situ ATP synthesis within cardiomyocytes. These Janus photophosphorylation nanorobots are fabricated through mechanical extrusion–assisted phase separation, enabling the asymmetric integration of chromatophore-coupled F o F l -ATPases. Under structured near-infrared irradiation, the nanorobots exhibit synergistic F o F l -ATPase rotation, which simultaneously drives active propulsion and high-yield ATP catalysis. Following targeted internalization and efficient lysosomal escape, the nanorobots achieve deep penetration into injured myocardial tissue. Intracellularly, the localized elevation of ATP rebalances the NAD + /NADH ratio, suppresses pathological mitochondrial permeability transition pore (mPTP) opening, and mitigates calcium ion overload—collectively restoring mitochondrial integrity and promoting functional myocardial recovery. This self-propelled, bioenergy-restoring nanoplatform represents a rationally designed strategy for targeted therapy of energy-deficient cardiomyopathies.

title: Asymmetric interactions and feast-famine cycles drive chaos in microbial populations
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Predicting the dynamics of ecological systems is a central challenge in biology. One factor that may limit predictability is ecological chaos. Theory has long suggested that even simple interactions can produce chaos, yet empirical demonstrations in living systems remain scarce. In a two-strain system of Escherichia coli , increasing the duration between resource replenishment reveals transitions from competitive exclusion to chaos, driven by asymmetric ecological interactions and periodic environmental forcing. Guided by these observations, we developed a dynamical systems framework grounded in empirical data that recapitulate the observed dynamics and predicts intermediate ecological states and transitions. Experimental validation of these predictions by implementing the corresponding conditions successfully reproduces the full range of predicted dynamical regimes. Because feast-famine cycles and asymmetric interactions are widespread in nature, our findings provide a model for uncovering the ecological and evolutionary significance of chaos, opening avenues to use resource fluctuation and interaction strength to quantify, monitor, and manipulate complex ecosystem behavior previously interpreted as stochasticity.

title: Immune infiltrate predicts response to αPD1/αCTLA4 but not αPD1 and distinguishes programs of primary resistance in metastatic melanoma
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: While immune-checkpoint blockade (ICB) has revolutionized treatment of metastatic melanoma, the identification of robust biomarkers to predict the relative efficacy of single versus combination ICB has been challenging. We performed a meta-analysis of eight cohorts of patients treated with anti–PD-1 ( n = 290), anti–CTLA-4 ( n = 175), and combination anti–PD-1/anti–CTLA-4 ( n = 51) with pretreatment tumor sequencing and clinical annotations. Surprisingly, the increased response rate to combination anti–PD-1/anti–CTLA-4 compared to anti–PD-1 monotherapy was observed only in highly immune infiltrated tumors, and not in immune-low tumors. Stratifying tumors by high or low frequency of immune cells also distinguished context-dependent programs of primary resistance to single and combination ICB. Notably, hypoxia-related pathways were enriched in nonresponders to anti–PD-1 ICB in immune-high, but not immune-low, tumors. Using an independent cohort of patients with scRNA-seq data, we observed that correlates of hypoxia were associated with increased stromal tumor receptor-ligand interactions. As proof of concept, selective inhibition of HIF-2α, a component of the hypoxia pathway and highly expressed in endothelial cells and fibroblasts, in combination with anti–PD-1, controlled tumor growth in mouse models of highly immune-infiltrated tumors but not poorly immune-infiltrated tumors. Our work demonstrates how stratification by tumor immune characteristics and clinical features can lead to the rational discovery of novel therapeutic targets.

title: Dynamic nuclear pores dictate the emergence of lamina-associated domains and UV protection during embryogenesis
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Lamina-associated domains (LADs) are large heterochromatin domains tethered to the nuclear periphery. LADs organize genome architecture, replication, repair, and transcription, but their formation during development is not well understood. Here, we use DamID and single-cell imaging to analyze embryonic LAD biogenesis in Caenorhabditis elegans . In early embryos, abundant nuclear pore components prevent heterochromatin formation at the lamina, and DNA positioned there is transcriptionally active. Over time, pore components decline, enabling LADs to form; auxin-mediated pore depletion induces precocious LADs. Nuclear basket component npp-21 /Translocated Promoter Region is not required, distinguishing embryonic LAD biogenesis from LADs in differentiated cells. Functionally, LADs confer protection against UVB radiation: Older embryos concentrate DNA damage at the nuclear periphery and survive UVB, whereas early embryos accumulate damage throughout nuclei and die, unless shielded by their mothers in utero. Within the embryo, damage is concentrated in upper, ultraviolet-facing cells, while underlying cells are shielded, suggesting that the Bodyguard effect operates at the organismal level. These findings identify embryonic dissipation of nuclear pores as a key step in embryonic LAD biogenesis, enabling older embryos to withstand environmental challenges.

title: The importance of organics in hydrothermal environments: A synchrotron laboratory study
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: The icy moon Enceladus has hydrothermal plumes that are of astrobiologic interest as they could provide conditions to sustain life or allow for its origin. To understand the geology of hydrothermal environments on icy moons, a carbonaceous asteroid simulant similar to the material Enceladus may have accreted from was subjected to conditions analogous to that of its seafloor. The sample environment used allowed high-resolution in situ synchrotron x-ray diffraction data to be collected during the experiment. Mineral reactions were observed as they occurred. Multiple mineral reactions had a large dependence on organic matter. Organics catalyzed the breakdown of aluminosilicates and dissolved pyrite. Melanophlogite and pyrrhotite were also formed as a result of organics being present. This study reveals that organics can have a large impact on mineral reactions and likely play an important role in the geology of hydrothermal vents on icy moons, which have an abundance of organics.

title: Geophysics-informed hydrologic modeling reveals contrasting regolith and bedrock responses of headwater catchments to warming
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Predicting how warming reshapes headwater streamflow requires distinguishing shallow and deep subsurface contributions, which remain difficult to constrain in catchment-scale models. We use seismic P-wave velocity to partition the critical zone into regolith and fractured bedrock domains within a three-dimensional physically based model and develop a particle-based attribution method to quantify their streamflow contributions and source-water ages across realizations spanning diverse hydraulic configurations. Across these realizations, warming produces contrasting subsurface hydrologic responses: Regolith-sourced streamflow generally becomes slightly younger, whereas fractured bedrock-sourced streamflow generally ages. This contrast arises because warming increases evapotranspiration and alters snow accumulation and melt timing, reducing effective recharge and lowering fractured-bedrock saturation. Declining recharge slows water transit and shifts fractured-bedrock-sourced water toward longer flow paths. Our results suggest that warming may reduce fractured-bedrock water renewal, with implications for the buffering role of bedrock water storage and for prolonged retention of legacy contaminants.

title: Mycobacterium tuberculosis CpsA interferes with the TBK1-p62 axis to inhibit xenophagy
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb) survives in macrophages by interfering with host lysosomal trafficking. Previously, we demonstrated that the Mtb protein, CpsA, is critical for bacterial survival in macrophages and infection in mice and that it can inhibit a noncanonical autophagy pathway. We also found that CpsA can interact with NDP52 and TAX1BP1, selective autophagy receptors that recognize cytosolic bacteria and target them for degradation, raising the possibility that CpsA also disrupts canonical autophagy. Here, we show that CpsA binds NDP52 and TAX1BP1 in their SKICH domains, which normally recruit the autophagy initiation machinery and TBK1. We demonstrate that CpsA prevents phagosomal recruitment of FIP200, a component of the autophagy initiation machinery, and blocks TBK1-dependent phosphorylation of p62, leading to impaired xenophagy. Our findings provide mechanistic insight into how Mtb subverts host defenses, revealing that in addition to blocking noncanonical autophagy, CpsA inhibits the TBK1-p62 axis to block xenophagy.

title: A supergene converts queen-destined larvae into a novel caste in ants
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Novel morphological castes are a major source of phenotypic diversity in ants, but their genetic and developmental origins remain unresolved. Here we identify ergatoid , a 6.5-megabase dominant supergene that is necessary and sufficient to generate a novel caste in an undescribed species of moss ant, Leptothorax AF-erg . The resulting wingless (ergatoid) queens represent a distinct morphological population intermediate between workers and the ancestral winged queen caste. Morphometric and genotyping analyses show that ergatoid produces this caste by modifying queen-destined larvae rather than altering worker development or generating a new larval population. Transcriptomic and candidate gene analyses most strongly support altered ecdysone signaling and reduced insulin signaling as the developmental basis for this phenotype. These results show that a single large-effect genetic element can generate a novel caste by modifying a specific preexisting larval population, providing a molecular genetic explanation for how novel phenotypes can arise, more broadly, through modification of ancestral developmental plasticity.

title: Cyclin-dependent kinase-like 5 (CDKL5) binds talin and is anchored at the postsynaptic density by direct PDZ interactions
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Cyclin-dependent kinase-like 5 (CDKL5) is a serine/threonine kinase essential for brain development and function. Mutations in CDKL5 cause CDKL5 deficiency disorder (CDD), a severe early-onset epileptic encephalopathy associated with impaired synapse formation and function. However, how CDKL5 mutations disrupt synaptic function remains unclear. Here, we show that the major neuronal isoform of CDKL5 contains a C-terminal PDZ domain–binding motif that mediates direct binding to PSD-95 and SHANK PDZ domains and recruits CDKL5 to the postsynaptic density. Disrupting this motif mislocalized CDKL5, reduced dendritic spine density, and impaired spine maturation. We also show that the CDKL5 kinase domain binds the R8 rod domain of the mechanosensitive scaffold talin. Mutation of the talin-binding interface or reduced cellular contractility altered CDKL5 positioning relative to focal adhesions. These findings define how CDKL5 is targeted to synapses, suggest that talin mechanoswitching may position CDKL5 kinase activity, and highlight the importance of C-terminal anchoring for interpreting pathogenic truncations.

title: Psychedelics shift decision strategies and reconfigure orbitofrontal dynamics
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Psychedelics such as psilocybin and ketamine are attracting renewed attention as rapid-acting therapeutics, yet how they reshape cognitive computations remains poorly understood. To address this, we trained mice on a free-response perceptual decision-making task that disentangles bias-driven from sensory-guided strategies. Acute administration of psilocybin or ketamine slowed decision times while improving accuracy. Behavioral modeling combining drift diffusion and GLM-HMM approaches revealed that these effects were driven by increased decision thresholds and a shift toward sensory-engaged states. Whole-brain c-Fos mapping identified modulation of distributed task-related networks, including the orbitofrontal cortex (OFC). Calcium imaging showed that OFC population dynamics were reorganized under psychedelic conditions, with preserved task selectivity but altered temporal structure and shifted population correlations. Together, these findings indicate that psychedelics shift decision-making toward greater reliance on sensory evidence while reshaping cortical population dynamics, providing a system-level account of their effects on perceptual decisions.

title: Sequential anion chemistry enables dynamic interphase regulation in high-voltage LiCoO2
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Lithium-ion batteries using LiCoO 2 cathodes have powered portable electronics for decades, yet their operation above 4.5 volts remains severely constrained by the unstable evolution of the cathode-electrolyte interphase (CEI). Under high-voltage conditions, lattice oxygen release and continuous electrolyte oxidation progressively degrade interfacial integrity. Here, we report a diluent-mediated local solvation regulation strategy to decrease dissociative solvent molecules and induce dual anion selective redistribution around Li + , forming a sequential solvation motif that drives sequential anion interfacial chemistry. DFOB − preferentially decomposes to establish a robust initial CEI framework, while BF 4 − continuously drives interfacial reactions to dynamically repair CEI defects and quench reactive oxygen species generated from lattice oxygen release. This dynamic regulation mechanism effectively stabilizes LiCoO 2 under aggressive high-voltage cycling. Consequently, the LiCoO 2 cathode delivers stable performance for 500 cycles at 4.5 volts with 73.5% capacity retention even in a low-concentration ether-based electrolyte. Furthermore, graphite||LiCoO 2 pouch cell achieves an energy density of 265.8 watt-hours per kilogram and exhibits favorable low-temperature resilience, retaining 99.1% capacity after 700 cycles at −20°C. These findings provide critical mechanistic insights into how solvation structure–driven anion chemistry can govern interfacial stability and unlock high-voltage, extreme-condition lithium-ion batteries.

title: Monolithic tiered microlithography for stretchable multilayer electronics with high-density, soft, and ultrathin VIAs
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Stretchable multilayer electronics that sustain reliable electrical performance under mechanical deformation are critical for advanced skin-like devices. A remaining challenge is the development of high-density, soft, and ultrathin vertical interconnect accesses (VIAs) that enable reliable electrical interconnection in flexible and stretchable circuits, particularly at small feature sizes. Here, we present a three-dimensional (3D), tier-by-tier photolithography strategy using PEDOT-based conductors and polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS)–based insulators, each photocurable within 10 seconds, to directly pattern soft VIAs and planar interconnects across lithographically defined PDMS openings. Maskless, full-field exposure enables thousands of in-plane and through-plane electrical connections in a single step, bypassing conventional hole-by-hole fabrication and manual VIA-to-pad alignment. The multilayer stack ensures minimal thickness, matched mechanical compliance, and robust conduction and insulation, enabling soft VIAs to preserve cross-layer electrical performance. Integration of lithographically defined cutouts and perforations yields breathable, conformal bioelectronics with skin-friendliness and stable signal acquisition in wearable wireless ECG monitoring. This multilayer 3D electronics platform can be extended to biomolecular sensing in soft organs, where thin, integrated, and stretchable designs are essential.

title: An all-magnonic neuron with tunable fading memory
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Magnonics offers nanometer-scale wave propagation and strong nonlinearities, making it attractive for neuromorphic applications such as artificial neurons. Yet, magnonic elements with interconnections solely within the magnonic system remain challenging, preventing the realization of interconnected magnonic neurons to date. Here, we experimentally demonstrate an all-magnonic neuron that reacts to magnon inputs with thresholded, amplified magnon firing and subsequent self-reset, enabling all-magnonic operation and cascading. Our approach is based on micro-antenna excitation on an ultralow damping garnet with perpendicular magnetic anisotropy, where we exploit the positive magnon frequency shift to realize nonlinear activation. Using Brillouin light scattering spectroscopy, we uncover a transient neuron response with tunable fading memory: A 25% change in pump power results in a three-order-of-magnitude tuning in memory time, which we harness, demonstrating temporal integration of up to 50 magnon pulses. Last, we realize neuron triggering in a cascade of three neurons, highlighting its potential for connected magnonic circuits.

title: Anisotropic field suppression of charge order reveals orbital-selective Kondo hybridization in UTe2
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: UTe 2 is a rare correlated quantum material where unconventional density-wave orders, Kondo physics, spin-triplet pairing, and reentrant superconductivity coexist. Because superconductivity emerges from a strongly correlated normal state, identifying and controlling intertwined normal-state orders are essential for understanding the electronic landscape where superconductivity arises. Here, using scanning tunneling microscopy in a vector magnetic field, we uncover a staggered charge density wave (CDW) in high-quality UTe 2 crystals. This CDW exhibits a strong directional field response: It is completely quenched by a modest 1.7-tesla magnetic field along the quasi–one-dimensional uranium-chain direction while remaining robust against fields along other crystallographic axes. This anisotropy suggests an orbital-driven field-tuned quantum phase transition. Unexpectedly, the same field orientation concurrently suppresses the 5f Kondo resonance. Modeling indicates a switch in the dominant hybridization channel from Te 5 p- U 5 f to U 6 d- U 5 f coupling, suggesting an intimate interplay between CDW and the Kondo effect.

title: Denoised vibrometry reveals noncanonical filtering at the apex of the cochlea
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: How do mammals distinguish sounds with different pitch? Prevailing theory states that each position along the cochlear spiral responds best to one single stimulus frequency, forming a frequency-to-place (tonotopic) map that is preserved throughout the auditory pathways. Whether this holds in the low-frequency cochlear apex, a region important for vocal communication but technically challenging to study, is unknown. Using a differential noise-canceling technique, we recorded sound-evoked motion near the lower limit of hearing. Apical locations often had two best frequencies, contradicting the assumption of one-to-one frequency-to-place mapping. Spatially distant regions responded similarly, and brief sounds evoked synchronized motion across large distances, revealing an unusual energy propagation mode. Morphology and mathematical analyses corroborate these findings, showing that tonotopy breaks down at the apex of the cochlea. These results have important implications for cochlear implants, which currently assume tonotopic organization throughout the cochlea.

title: Interfacing ultrafast single-photon-level fields with an atomic ensemble
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Ultrafast photons—with pulse durations on the order of 100 femtoseconds—are typical of high-rate, high-purity, entangled photon-pair sources. Efficient, coherent mapping between these states and matter-based quantum systems is an important problem in quantum optics and could enable applications in quantum frequency conversion, bandwidth conversion, and local quantum information processing at gigahertz speeds. This coherent mapping is also the initial storage step in matter-based photonic quantum memory, which can enhance multiphoton rates and allow for synchronization in quantum repeaters. Here, we use a collisionally broadened neutral atomic barium ensemble to demonstrate a quantum-compatible light-matter interface with storage efficiency of 95.6 ± 0.3%, total internal efficiency of 31 ± 1%, and noise contributions of −4 photons per pulse. Using the simultaneous efficiency, bandwidth, and noise performance of this interface, we perform a full amplitude and phase reconstruction via spectral interferometry of single-photon-level fields retrieved from the interface.

title: LONP-1 deficiency causes dysregulated protein synthesis within mitochondria that is suppressed by mitoribosomal mutations
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Mitochondrial homeostasis is maintained by molecular chaperones and proteases located within the organelle. The mitochondrial matrix-localized protease LONP-1 degrades oxidatively damaged or misfolded proteins. Importantly, LONP-1 also regulates mitochondrial DNA replication. Here, we show that mutations in C. elegans that impair LONP-1 function cause dysregulation of mitochondrial DNA replication, mitochondrial RNA transcription and protein synthesis within the mitochondrial matrix. LONP-1 deficient worms had reduced levels of oxidative phosphorylation proteins despite increased mtDNA-encoded protein synthesis. Via a forward genetic screen, we identified three mutations that restored mitochondrial function and the rate of development in lonp-1 mutants to levels comparable to those in wildtype worms. Interestingly, all three suppressor mutations were found in genes encoding mitochondrial ribosome proteins. A point mutation in the mitochondrial ribosome protein MRPS-38 restored oxidative phosphorylation in lonp-1 mutant worms. Combined, our results suggest that LONP-1 regulates mitochondrial translation and that suppressor mutations within mrps-38 or mrps-15 can enhance oxidative phosphorylation complex assembly when LONP-1 function is diminished.

title: Flexible megahertz low-power complementary circuits based on nanoscale organic transistors
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: The stringent low-power requirements of wearable electronics systems can be met only by combining p-channel and n-channel transistors in a complementary circuit topology. For circuits based on organic thin-film transistors (TFTs), this calls for improvements in n-channel TFT performance. We report on flexible low-voltage nanoscale n-channel organic TFTs fabricated using a recently developed high-performance small-molecule semiconductor. The TFTs have on/off current ratios greater than 10 8 and subthreshold swings below 200 millivolts per decade. Nanoscale n-channel and p-channel organic TFTs were integrated into inverters that display small-signal gains up to 175, noise margins up to 80%, static power consumption as low as 10 −12 watts, and characteristic signal-delay time constants as short as 60 nanoseconds (at 3 volts). These are the best-performing flexible organic TFT–based complementary inverters reported to date.

title: Predictive model for nanoparticle incorporation into crystals reveals essential role of interfacial solution structure
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Control of interfacial phenomena remains limited by incomplete understanding of molecular-scale solution structure at solid-liquid interfaces. We address this challenge by developing and validating a comprehensive analytical model for nanoparticle incorporation during crystallization. Using atomic force microscopy (AFM) probes surface functionalized to be “particle proxies” combined with three-dimensional AFM and force spectroscopy, we measure nanoparticle-calcite crystal binding energies and kinetic barriers associated with interfacial hydration layers. These measurements, together with diffusivities, parameterize a predictive model that is corroborated using surface-functionalized fluorescent silica nanoparticles incorporated into calcite. We show that surface chemistry governs incorporation by reshaping the energy landscape, with amine groups particularly favoring incorporation. Applying this approach to nanoparticles with different topologies further supports our finding that kinetic barriers play a pivotal role in incorporation processes. This synthesis science framework links interfacial solution structure, particle dynamics, and crystallization kinetics, identifying kinetic barriers as a key design principle for engineering bioinspired nanocomposites beyond empirical approaches.

title: Resolving the black hole sphere of influence in a hyperluminous obscured quasar at redshift 4.6
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Supermassive black holes (SMBHs) imprint gravitational signatures on the matter within their sphere of influence (SoI). Nuclear gas dynamics can hence be used to accurately measure the mass of an SMBH, yet these measurements remain elusive in the early universe. We report the first dynamical measurement of an SMBH mass at z > 2, based on high–spatial resolution observations of the ionized-carbon 157.7-micrometer and carbon monoxide (12-11) 216.93-micrometer emission lines that resolve the SoI in an obscured quasar at z = 4.6. The radial profile of the velocity dispersion reveals a clear Keplerian rise, requiring the presence of an ∼6 × 10 9 –solar mass SMBH. We propose that heavily obscured quasars allow such tracers to survive in the inner regions and may be ideal targets for increasing dynamical SMBH mass estimates in the early universe.

title: Deep ultraviolet bound states in the continuum
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Light confinement is a key strategy for enhancing light-matter interaction, and photonic crystal (PhC) slabs have emerged as a promising resonant platform due to their high Q factors and design flexibility. However, realizing high- Q PhC slabs in the deep ultraviolet (DUV) regime has remained highly challenging due to the lack of suitable materials and limitations in fabrication. In this work, we propose an etchless fabrication strategy based on electron-beam lithography and atomic layer deposition. We demonstrate a shell-type PhC slab in which a low-index photoresist core is conformally encapsulated by a high-index zirconium dioxide shell. Through angle-resolved transmittance measurements, we experimentally observe symmetry-protected bound states in the continuum in the DUV regime and achieve the highest reported Q factor among resonant modes in this spectral range. Furthermore, by comparing conventional bulk-type and shell-type PhC slabs in far-field response, we show that the shell-type structure maintains comparable performance while offering fabrication advantages. These results provide a practical route for realizing high- Q PhC slabs in the DUV and open opportunities for DUV-based molecular sensing and enhanced light-matter interaction applications.

title: Targeting METTL3 protects against acetaminophen-induced liver injury through HAPTOGLOBIN/CD163 macrophage axis
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Acetaminophen (APAP) overdose is the most common cause of drug-induced liver injury (DILI), with limited treatment options. N 6 -methyladenosine (m 6 A) is the most abundant internal epitranscriptomic modification in eukaryotic RNAs and is involved in various physiological and pathological processes, serving as a potential therapeutic target for many diseases. However, little is known about the role of m 6 A in DILI. Here, we found that intrahepatic expression of Methyltransferase-like 3 (METTL3), the core catalytic subunit of RNA m 6 A methyltransferase complex, was elevated in patients with DILI and mouse DILI models. Hepatocyte-specific knockout of METTL3, achieved via either Alb-Cre ERT2 –driven recombination or adeno-associated virus (AAV)–mediated delivery of Cre, significantly protected from APAP-induced hepatotoxicity in both male and female mice. Mechanistically, hepatic METTL3 deficiency reduced m 6 A deposition on acute-phase protein haptoglobin ( Hp ) transcripts and promoted Hp transcription and translation in hepatocytes. Increased HP secreted by hepatocytes bound to its receptor CD163, expressed explicitly on macrophages, and induced highly phagocytic and anti-inflammatory polarization of macrophages, finally reducing APAP-induced hepatic injury. Moreover, two different METTL3 inhibitors, JNJ64619178 and STM2457, effectively alleviated APAP-induced liver injury. Our study thus demonstrated that hepatic inhibition of METTL3 protected against APAP-induced liver injury by promoting the cross-talk between hepatocytes and macrophages through HP/CD163, underscoring the potential of targeting METTL3 as a promising therapy for APAP overdose.

title: Solubility-driven morphological decoupling enables elastic electron-deficient semiconducting polymers for fully stretchable electronics
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: The development of fully stretchable electronics is limited by the scarcity of electron-deficient polymers that combine high electron mobility with mechanical elasticity. Here, we report a solubility-driven morphological decoupling strategy that mitigates this trade-off by incorporating ∼10% planar, insoluble PyF units into a semicrystalline PySe backbone. This approach yields a hierarchical morphology characterized by suppressed long-range crystallinity alongside robust local aggregation. Driven by strong fluorine (F)-sulfur (S) interactions, highly ordered face-on domains function as robust physical anchors, providing the polymer network with exceptional elasticity to reversibly dissipate stress and preserve charge percolation pathways. Consequently, the resulting terpolymer largely relieves the long-standing trade-off between charge transport and mechanical stretchability, delivering a near-unity initial electron mobility (∼1.0 square centimeter per volt per second) and retaining 0.5 square centimeters per volt per second even under 100% applied strain, representing the highest performance reported to date. To demonstrate the practical utility of this system, we fabricated stretchable ambipolar inverters and phototransistors that maintain high performance under severe deformation. Notably, the phototransistors sustain an exceptional responsivity of 15.8 amperes per watt and an external quantum efficiency exceeding 2900% at 100% strain. These results establish a powerful blueprint for intrinsically elastic semiconductors, enabling the realization of high-performance, fully deformable optoelectronic systems.

title: Roseburia intestinalis counteracts TBEP-exacerbated atherosclerosis
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Interactions between serum metabolites and vascular endothelial cells directly influence atherosclerotic lesions. It is essential to identify and understand the effects of the complex profile of serum metabolites on vascular pathology. In this study, we found that coronary lesion severity positively correlated with serum levels of the organophosphate ester tris (2-butoxyethyl) phosphate (TBEP), while TBEP levels inversely correlated with gut Roseburia intestinalis abundance. Western diet supplemented with TBEP substantially exacerbated atherosclerosis in apolipoprotein E −/− ( ApoE −/− ) mice. We found that TBEP enhanced AMP-activated protein kinase α (AMPKα) phosphorylation, reduced nuclear translocation of active sterol regulatory element–binding protein 1c (SREBP1c) fragments, suppressed Patatin-like phospholipase domain–containing protein 3 (PNPLA3) protein expression in endothelial cells, and increased lipid deposition. Oral R. intestinalis supplementation reduced fecal and serum TBEP levels and attenuated TBEP-driven atherosclerotic lesions. We highlight that TBEP aggravates endothelial lipid accumulation and atherosclerosis, suggesting that targeting gut microbiota may serve as a promising strategy against TBEP-exacerbated atherosclerosis.

title: Enzymatic degradation of a polyester-based thermoset composite resin by an engineered cutinase from Fusarium solani
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Thermoset composites have become indispensable high-performance materials across key industrial sectors. However, existing recycling methods have yet to deliver sustainable end-of-life solutions for these materials. Here, we report the engineering of a highly active and stable biocatalyst capable of depolymerizing polyester-based thermoset composites. First, a second-generation polyester resin was designed to enhance susceptibility to enzymatic attack. Cutinase from Fusarium solani was selected and subsequently engineered through a combination of directed evolution and computational design using two soluble surrogate motifs representative of the redesigned resin structure. The resulting variant, which incorporated 19 mutations, exhibited a 22-fold increase in activity and an 11°C improvement in melting temperature while achieving recombinant production titers at the gram-per-liter scale in yeast cultivated in fed-batch bioreactor. This engineered enzyme depolymerized the polyester resin with a total release of 6 mM (∼1.08 grams per liter) monomethyl phthalate. Together, to our knowledge, these findings constitute the first documented example of enzymatic degradation of a complex polyester resin from thermoset composite materials.

title: Structural basis of Anopheles mosquito salivary protein complexes implicated in malaria transmission
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Successful malaria transmission by Anopheles mosquitoes depends on Plasmodium development within the mosquito midgut and subsequent sporozoite invasion of its salivary glands. Salivary proteins, notably Saglin and likely salivary gland surface proteins (SGS4 and SGS5), were suggested to play roles in these processes, but the lack of their structures has hindered our understanding of the underlying molecular mechanisms. In this study, we carried out biochemical and mass spectrometry analyses of salivary gland extracts and demonstrate that Anopheles gambiae SGS4 and SGS5 bind Saglin and other SG1 (salivary gland 1) proteins. Cryo-EM structure of the Saglin-SGS4 complex reveals that Saglin homodimerizes through coiled-coil interactions and disulfide bonds and engages longitudinally with SGS4. Comparisons among SG1-SGS complexes show that SG1 proteins share a conserved architecture, and SGS proteins adapt conformationally to bind different SG1 partners of varying lengths. To our knowledge, our findings uncover the first native mosquito salivary protein complexes that likely facilitate malaria transmission and highlight potential vector targets for blocking malaria transmission.

title: Self-assembly of bacterial volumetric patterns directed by a synthetic reaction-diffusion circuit
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Reaction-diffusion (RD) has long been proposed as a mechanism underlying biological pattern formation. However, quantitative frameworks linking circuit design to spatial organization remain limited.
