Here, we engineered a synthetic gene circuit, MINPAC, that couples gene expression regulation (reaction) with bacterial colony expansion and quorum sensing (diffusion) to guide bacterial cells to self-organize into periodic volumetric patterns across multiple scales, from single cells to three-dimensional colonies. The patterns exhibit robustness against environmental variations and size-dependent complexity. Mathematical modeling supports a clock-and-wavefront mechanism, where oscillatory gene expression interacts with outward expanding diffusions to generate these periodic spatial structures. Topological analysis reveals that specific network architecture is essential for pattern formation. Guided by model predictions, we further show that pattern complexity can be systematically tuned by gene dosage, with lower expression levels favoring multiple rings through faster dynamics. This work establishes a framework uniting circuit engineering and mathematical analysis for programming multicellular self-organization through RD mechanisms, with potential applications in regenerative medicine and biomaterials.

title: Clearance of erythrocytes after subarachnoid hemorrhage: Cranial lymphatic and dural pathways
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: The clearance of toxic blood products from the brain after subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH) is critical for neurological recovery, yet the precise anatomical pathways and cellular mechanisms responsible for this process remain poorly defined. Using murine models of both arterial perforation and low-rate intracisternal injection, we have mapped a comprehensive, multifaceted network of red blood cell (RBC) distribution and clearance. We found that, while RBCs accessed peripheral lymphatic vessels via cranial nerves, an extensive distribution of extravasated erythrocytes could also be observed sequestered within nonendothelial, collagen-lined interstitial channels flanking the major dural venous sinuses. By day 2 post-SAH, regional macrophages actively cleared some trapped erythrocytes. These findings provide a detailed spatiotemporal framework of SAH blood clearance, revealing promising anatomical and cellular targets to accelerate stroke recovery.

title: Evolution of MEIS transcription factor activity during metazoan neural development—born to be wild
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Meis TALE-class proteins pattern vertebrate neural tissue, inducing hindbrain and neural crest in Xenopus laevis embryos. Meis orthologs have two conserved regions: (i) Meis-specific domain and (ii) Meis-specific TALE homeodomain. Meis homeodomain proteins are present in “ancient” metazoans-eucaryotes like cnidarians, placozoans, and protozoans. We asked: When during metazoan evolution did Meis proteins acquire functionality to induce neural pattern? Using structure-function analysis in Xenopus , we show that the Meis-specific and Meis homeodomains suffice to induce the spinal cord but not the hindbrain. Meis proteins share a functionally conserved carboxyl-terminal transcription activation domain inducing the hindbrain. Ancient Meis proteins from Trichoplax and chlorophyte algae have a conserved Meis homeodomain, but lack the Meis-specific domain. Unexpectedly, these ancestral proteins robustly induce hindbrain and neural crest in Xenopus , unlike metazoan proteins requiring the Meis-specific domain. Thus, in early eukaryotes, Meis prototypes were “born to be wild,” having the intrinsic capacity to induce vertebrate structures like hindbrain and neural crest, despite predating them.

title: SeqA-mediated sister loci cohesion regulates the efficiency and fidelity of DNA double-strand break repair across the E. coli genome
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: In Escherichia coli , SeqA-mediated cohesion at snap loci on the right replichore persists longer, but its role in DNA double-strand break (DSB) repair remains untested. Here, we show that site-specific DSBs at snap loci confer higher cell survival than nonsnap loci. With perturbations affecting sister cohesion [Δ seqA , topoisomerase IV overexpression (T4-OE)], this survival advantage was progressively reduced, with the combined Δ seqA T4-OE strain retaining only a transient advantage. The increased survival correlates with faster repair, reflected by rapid restoration of locus copy number and shorter-lived, thinner RecA–green fluorescent protein filaments. Consistent with more accurate repair, snap loci exhibited lower mutation accumulation under normal and antibiotic stress conditions. Comparative genome analysis of E. coli strains revealed higher GATC motif counts and higher sequence conservation. Together, these findings suggest that the chromosomal organization associated with prolonged sister cohesion at snap loci promotes efficient homologous recombination–mediated DSB repair and contributes to genome conservation.

title: Platelet glycoprotein Ib shapes the immune response during lung injury
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: The acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) is a life-threatening, inflammatory disease state of the lung. Self-propagating inflammation within the alveolar space and excessive infiltration of neutrophils into the pulmonary airspace are the main mechanisms underlying the dysfunction. A role of platelets in the pathogenesis of ARDS is suggested, but the underlying mechanisms remain largely unknown. We hypothesized that platelet glycoprotein (GP)Ib is an important contributor of platelet activation in this context. To highlight the contribution of the GPIb to the acute phase of experimental ALI in mice, we exposed mice genetically lacking functional GPIb ( GPIb-IL-4tg ) and wild-type (WT) mice injected with a function blocking anti-GPIb antibody to lipopolysaccharide (LPS) inhalation. GPIb-IL-4tg mice as well as anti-GPIb–treated mice displayed reduced neutrophil infiltration of the alveolar space in response to LPS. GPIb-IL-4tg mice as well as anti-GPIb–treated WT mice showed reduced interactions of platelets with neutrophils in comparison to controls, resulting in reduced platelet-neutrophil complexes and mitigated formation of neutrophil extracellular traps. Since these mechanisms are important for defense against external invasion of pathogens, we exposed GPIb-IL-4tg mice to Klebsiella pneumoniae and found reduced survival with increased bacterial load in these animals. Last, translational evaluation of biosamples of patients with ARDS showed that patients with low plasma levels of the shed GPIbα ectodomain (glycocalicin) exhibited higher mortality and worsened overall outcome. Together, our study shows that GPIb is a central mediator of neutrophil migration into the alveolar space and the defense mechanisms against the external invasion of pathogens.

title: Subclonal evolution can shape the transition toward a sarcomatoid phenotype in pleural mesothelioma
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: A better understanding of intratumor heterogeneity in pleural mesothelioma (PM) is crucial to implementing precision medicine for this deadly cancer. Using single-cell RNA sequencing approaches on tumor samples and derived primary cell lines, we defined four phenotypic cell types, related to overall survival in larger bulk cohorts: epithelioid, sarcomatoid, intermediate, and nondifferentiated. Some tumor samples showed intratumor phenotypic heterogeneity, associated with subclonal evolution, in which sarcomatoid cells can emerge from parental cells with an intermediate phenotype following the acquisition of copy number variations. Subclones were conserved in cell lines and retained their specific phenotypes, suggesting high phenotypic heritability. Spatial transcriptomics illustrated the link between phenotypic and subclonal evolution, showing that subclonal cells were colocalized and exhibited specific morphologies within the tumor tissue. Our study provides a comprehensive single-cell profiling of PM tumor cells and reveals a link between phenotypic evolution, clonal architecture, and tumor spatial organization.

title: SMAD4 loss drives cancer chromosomal instability through transcription-replication conflict–associated replication stress
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Cancer chromosomal instability (CIN) drives tumor evolution through generating structural and numerical chromosome aberrations. However, its molecular determinants remain poorly characterized. Here, we uncover a yet unrecognized role for the tumor suppressor SMAD4 as a key regulator of chromosomal stability. Mechanistically, loss of SMAD4 causes replication stress by promoting transcription-replication conflicts (TRCs) and induces subsequent mitotic errors, leading to the concomitant emergence of structural and numerical CIN. While the tumor suppressor function of SMAD4 has been predominantly attributed to transforming growth factor–β signaling, we find that its role in genome maintenance operates via bone morphogenetic protein (BMP) signaling and its transcriptional target gene ID3 . Consequently, inhibition of BMP signaling mimics the loss of SMAD4 , while reexpression of SMAD4 or ID3 in SMAD4 -deficient colorectal or pancreatic cancer cells suppresses TRCs, replication stress, and mitotic errors. Our findings reveal a TRC- and replication stress–driven mechanism by which loss of BMP-SMAD4 signaling causes cancer CIN.

title: DFT-assisted natural abundance 13C zero-field NMR via optical magnetometry
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Zero-field (ZF) nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopy probes nuclear J-couplings without homogeneous magnetic fields, enabling inexpensive and geometrically flexible detection, including through metal. However, its broader use for chemical analysis has been limited by sensitivity and the difficulty of predicting the dense ZF multiplets. Here we demonstrate natural-abundance (1.1%) carbon-13 ( 13 C) ZF spectroscopy on off-the-shelf liquids using a compact commercial rubidium-87 magnetometer without hyperpolarization or special preparation. Instrumental advances yield improved sensitivity, ≤250-millihertz linewidths, and >week-long stability, enabling isotopomer-resolved fingerprint spectra across a 13-molecule library, including rare (0.0121%) doubly 13 C-labeled species. In parallel, we demonstrate vibrationally corrected density functional theory (DFT) prediction of ZF spectra with good qualitative agreement. Comparing experiment with these calculations renders residual deviations as chemically informative, reporting on hydrogen bonding and ion pairing at high ionic strength. These results contribute toward DFT-assisted ZF NMR as a general platform for field constraint–free molecular identification and for extracting transient solution-state structure from responsive J-coupling observables.

title: PEG-free tunable poly(2-oxazoline) lipids modulate mRNA-LNP biodistribution and expression in vivo
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) have transformed drug delivery, enabling the stabilization and efficient intracellular delivery of nucleic acids. Current LNP platforms, including those used in clinical COVID-19 vaccines, rely on polyethylene glycol (PEG) to stabilize the nanoparticle. However, anti-PEG antibodies are ubiquitous in the population and are a major cause of anaphylaxis and reduced therapeutic efficacy by accelerating the blood clearance of PEGylated products. Here, we report the development of poly(2-oxazoline) (POx) lipids as alternatives. POx polymers are poorly immunogenic and mitigate accelerated blood clearance. Upon varying polymer hydrophilicity and molecular weight, we screened transfection efficiency in multiple cell lines and evaluated top candidates in vivo. Our findings demonstrate that POx-lipids incorporating short hydrophilic oxazoline chains enhance target transfection while mitigating liver expression. These POx-lipids boost expression in key extrahepatic tissues, including lymph nodes and spleen. This marks a notable advancement toward replacing PEG in LNP therapies and provides a clear path to optimizing POx-lipids for targeted vaccine and therapeutic applications.

title: Dissecting the molecular triggers of early and late long-term potentiation
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: The brain stores information by changing the strength of its synapses, a process that has at least two phases: Late long-term potentiation (L-LTP) is thought to result from the consolidation of early LTP (E-LTP), just as long-term memory requires the prior establishment of short-term memory. Recently, inhibitory avoidance experiments under CaMKII inhibition have challenged this notion, demonstrating long-term fear memory without measurable short-term memory. Here we use optogenetic activation and inhibition of CaMKII during induction of spike-timing-dependent potentiation (tLTP) to dissect the signaling pathways. While CaMKII activation in CA1 neurons was sufficient to induce E-LTP, growth of the postsynaptic density and spine neck expansion, we found that CaMKII-induced LTP does not give rise to L-LTP. Conversely, inhibition of CaMKII during tLTP induction prevented E-LTP, but FOS and L-LTP were still expressed, driven by CaMKK and PKMζ. Thus, both long-term memory and L-LTP form in the absence of CaMKII activation.

title: A membrane-guided strategy for optimizing proton exchange membrane fuel cells via spatially controlled acid distribution
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Efficient regulation of phosphoric acid (PA) distribution is vital for advancing high-temperature proton exchange membrane fuel cells. PA migration from the membrane into the catalyst layer (CL) enhances proton accessibility but compromises membrane conductivity, highlighting the need to balance acid distribution within the membrane electrode assembly. Here, we propose a membrane-guided strategy enabling systematic evaluation of PA distribution effects and identification of a favorable acid content range. By designing side chain–grafted polybenzimidazole (PBI) membranes with abundant acid-binding sites, we achieve tunable acid doping levels and regulate PA partitioning through acid-polymer interactions. To compare PA accumulation, we introduce the mass ratio of phosphorus to platinum in the CL (PA CL /Pt CL ) as a semiquantitative descriptor of CL acid content and use distribution of relaxation times analysis to decouple its influence on ohmic resistance, oxygen reduction kinetics, and oxygen transport. We identify a favorable PA CL /Pt CL range of approximately two to three under the present conditions, while the nearly twofold enhancement over OPBI highlights coordinated control of membrane transport and the CL acid state.

title: Disulfiram inhibits pyroptosis and apoptosis through multiple complementary mechanisms
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Gasdermins (GSDMs) execute pyroptosis by forming lytic pores in the plasma membrane that release IL-1 cytokines and promote cell swelling and membrane rupture. Their key roles in infection, inflammation and cancer make GSDMs attractive therapeutic targets. Here we systematically investigate how disulfiram, an approved drug for treating alcoholism, inhibits pyroptosis and identify multiple complementary mechanisms. First, disulfiram inhibits processing of procaspase-1 to caspase-1. Second, disulfiram inhibits caspases from processing human GSDMD to release the lytic N-terminal domain (GSDMD Nterm ). Third, disulfiram structurally modifies GSDMD Nterm . Fourth, disulfiram partitions into membranes, where it remains embedded, changes membrane properties and prevents GSDMD Nterm insertion. Similarly, disulfiram blocks intrinsic apoptosis by inhibiting procaspase-3 activation, caspase-3 cleavage of human GSDME, and GSDME Nterm pore formation. Furthermore, we show that two other GSDMD inhibitors, necrosulfonamide and dimethyl fumarate also inhibit GSDM-induced cell death through multiple complementary mechanisms. These multilevel inhibitory mechanisms deepen our understanding of strategies to target GSDM-mediated cell death pathways.

title: Dual-modality photoacoustic and optical coherence tomography imaging simultaneously tracks transplanted stem cells and their viability
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Monitoring transplanted cell viability in vivo, noninvasively remains a considerable challenge. By using multiwavelength photoacoustic microscopy powered by a reactive oxygen species (ROS)–responsive contrast agent, we can relatively and semiquantitatively assess and longitudinally monitor the viability of human-induced pluripotent stem cell–derived retinal pigment epithelium (hiPSC-RPE) cells in vivo. The contrast agent comprises colloidal chain-like gold nanoparticle (CGNP) clusters conjugated with IR775c, a heptamethine cyanine dye that undergoes selective oxidative quenching under elevated ROS conditions associated with cellular death (CGNP-IR775c). Dual-wavelength photoacoustic microscopy at 620 and 775 nanometers provides self-calibrated ratiometric measurements that enable relative viability assessment, distinguishing healthy from nonviable cell populations. In vitro studies demonstrated that CGNP-IR775c exhibited biocompatibility and showed dose-dependent ROS sensitivity across physiologically relevant H 2 O 2 concentrations. hiPSC-RPE cells labeled by CGNP-IR775c were subretinally transplanted into living rabbit eyes and longitudinally monitored for 2 weeks, showing that laser-induced oxidative stress produced measurable photoacoustic signal changes that were consistent with the viability status of the transplanted cells. The imaging technology developed here provides a practical solution for noninvasive, longitudinal, and semiquantitative assessment of the transplanted cell viability in vivo, and may contribute to ophthalmology cell-based therapy in both preclinical and clinical settings.

title: Neuromorphic self-aware wings for embodied-intelligent bionic flying microrobotics
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Flying insects achieve robust proprioception and agile flight control using distributed mechanoreceptors on their wings, but current bionic flying microrobots rely heavily on external sensors for state monitoring. Typical sensing solutions including offboard vision or surface-mounted devices inevitably sacrifice either flight autonomy or payload capacity. Inspired by insect wing mechanoreception, we introduce an embodied neuromorphic self-sensing paradigm that eliminates this tradeoff by enabling intrinsic, aerodynamics-maintenance proprioception in flapping-wing systems. Instead of treating the wing solely as a propulsive structure, we reengineer it into a self-contained sensory organ capable of autonomous motion monitoring and health state awareness. We develop an interface charge field mapping model that decouples complex local wing motions, enabling dynamic three-dimensional reconstruction of wing deformation. Building on this theoretical foundation, a conformal bionic mechanoreceptor is directly grown on the wing surface via layered sensitive units. By synergistically combining physics-driven kinematic feature extraction with machine learning, the system achieves real-time fault diagnosis and closed-loop aerodynamic-loss compensation. We do not add sensors to the wing, we make the wing itself the sensory organ. This embodied self-sensing paradigm establishes a new principle for structural intelligence in bionic robotics, offering a promising path toward autonomous, self-aware, and robust miniature flying systems.

title: Complex IV maturation coordinates postnatal mitochondrial and metabolic development
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: The perinatal heart undergoes a rapid metabolic transition from glycolysis to fatty acid oxidation that requires extensive mitochondrial remodeling, yet the molecular checkpoints that coordinate this process remain poorly defined. Using temporally resolved proteomics and complexome profiling of developing mouse hearts from late gestation through early postnatal life (E18.5 to P10), we identify a discrete developmental window in which respiratory chain architecture is remodeled to enable metabolic commitment. Complex IV (CIV) emerges as a central structural determinant of this transition, undergoing isoform-specific reassembly and transient suppression at birth before incorporation into mature respiratory supercomplexes. We identify the CIV subunit COX7C as a developmentally regulated determinant of CIV maturation, with its abundance increasing during maximal respirasome assembly and the switch to fatty acid oxidation. Loss of COX7C impairs terminal CIV maturation, prevents incorporation of heart-specific isoforms, and destabilizes the respirasome organization. Notably, this defect causes a selective secondary failure of complex I completion, demonstrating that respirasome formation is required for catalytic CI maturation in vivo. Consequently, cardiac-specific COX7C deficiency fails to complete the perinatal metabolic transition, leading to the collapse of fatty acid oxidation, activation of nucleotide and serine–glycine–one-carbon metabolism, attenuated activation of the mitochondrial integrated stress response, and a metabolically and structurally compromised state unlikely to support the increasing energetic demands of the postnatal heart. Together, these findings define a developmentally timed, CIV-dependent assembly step that couples respiratory chain assembly to postnatal cardiac metabolic fate and provide a temporal framework for mitochondrial maturation in the developing heart.

title: Regiospecific Sila‐Matteson Homologative Arylation of Biased ( N ‐Oxide) Azines
abstract: ABSTRACT The judicious selection of silicon—as a Lewis acid—able to generate penta‐ and hexavalent hypercoordinated ate complexes is herein presented as a strategy to realize conceptually novel homologative arylations. Chemically stable aryl‐ equipped C1‐silanes, conveniently activated with the same biased ( N‐ oxide) substrate in the presence of fluoride, furnish—upon fine‐tuning of consecutive [1,2]‐transposition events—benzyl‐like nucleophilic elements which are precisely transferred at the C2‐position of azines. These benzyl synthons originate from combining an aryl residue and the homologating methylene fragment. The regioselective logic is levered on the unique capability of silicon to undergo two controllable expansive‐contractive modifications of its coordinative sphere. Compared to single rearrangements accomplished with labile C1‐donors on boron manifolds—retained in the final products (Matteson‐like)—the silicon approach directly gathers heteroatom‐free azines, thus documenting high versatility for rapid and predictable functionalization.

title: Adaptive Active Site Programming via Electrolyte Engineering Toward Enhanced Catalytic Activity
abstract: ABSTRACT Precise control over active site coordination is essential for advancing electrocatalysis, yet remains challenging due to insufficient understanding of how operating environments, particularly electrolyte anions, reshape local structure, and coordination. Here, we combine grand canonical ensemble calculations with experimental validations to investigate five representative anions (F − , Cl − , Br − , NO 3 − , and H 2 PO 4 − ) across a range of pH and potential conditions. Using Fe─N─C single‐atom catalysts and oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) as a prototypical system, we reveal the adaptive evolution of active site coordination: Anions act as axial ligands that modulate the electronic structure of active sites and enable pH‐dependent regulation of catalytic activity. Specifically, NO 3 − serves as the most effective axial ligand for enhancing catalytic activity across the entire pH range. Electrochemical measurements show enhanced ORR activity, and spectroscopic characterizations directly reveal axial NO 3 coordination upon introducing NO 3 − , supporting the theoretical predictions. Based on these insights, we propose an adaptive framework for electrolyte‐guided active site programming, which enables the selection of proper anion ligand with optimal catalytic activity under specific working conditions. This work bridges mechanistic modeling and experimental design, precisely constructing the active center for enhanced electrocatalytic activity.

title: Buckled Silver Microflake Conductors With In Situ‐Generated Ag–O Coordination Enable 3D‐Printed Stretchable Cardiac Bioelectrodes
abstract: ABSTRACT Metallic pacemaker electrodes risk myocardial injury during implantation, while silver micro‐flakes (AgMFs), despite excellent conductivity, are too rigid for stretchable devices without proper composite/device engineering. Here, we present a synergistic strategy to fabricate fully stretchable, electrically stable, and crack‐resistant cardiac electrodes by integrating AgMF‐based ink with metal‐organic interfacial bonding, biaxial buckling, and wet‐adhesive hydrogels. In situ‐generated Ag–O coordination of silver nanoparticles (AgNPs) in the polymer matrix/conductor dissipates stress and suppresses crack propagation, effectively compensating for AgMF rigidity and enabling intact buckled microstructures. The resulting electrodes exhibit high conductivity (∼2.1 × 10 4 S cm −1 ) and stable resistance under 50% cyclic strain, exceeding cardiac motion requirements (15%–20%). The ink is 3D‐printable into mesh electrodes and can be integrated with wet‐adhesive hydrogels to form puncture‐free, stretchable metallic cardiac bioelectrodes with excellent biosafety, offering a promising route toward leadless pacemakers and long‐term wireless cardiac monitoring. A multiscale synergistic strategy integrating metal‐organic interfacial bonding with stretch‐release‐induced buckled architectures enables silver microflake conductors with simultaneously high conductivity and large deformability, demonstrated for 3D printing of bioadaptive, puncture‐free cardiac electrodes and stretchable wireless coils for dynamic cardiac stimulation and long‐term electrophysiological monitoring.

title: Three‐Dimensional In Situ Tunable Mechanical Metamaterials
abstract: ABSTRACT Mechanical metamaterials with in situ, smooth, and broad‐range tunability of stiffness are highly anticipated in engineering, but existing designs are limited to unidirectional or bidirectional control. As the stiffness lacks the multi‐directional coupling effect for shape morphing, creating three‐dimensional (3D) metamaterials with triaxial tunability remains challenging in configuration design, fabrication, and actuation. Here we create two types of gear‐based 3D mechanical metamaterials that achieve in situ, wide‐range, continuous, reversible tunability of 3D stiffness. The first uses spherical gears containing ellipsoidal cavities as the variable‐stiffness components, while the second conceives planetary‐like 3D gear assemblies as the metacell. They feature orthotropic stiffness in three axes—all can be tuned in situ by about 30 times via synchronous rotation. Moreover, the nonlinear buckling properties are also tunable in 3D space. The integrated actuation methods are conceived to achieve robust and smooth control. We clarify the principles and demonstrate the properties of 3D in situ tunability by analytical, numerical, and experimental methods. Therefore, this work systematically proves the possibility of programmable metamaterials with in situ 3D tunability, offering feasible ways for conceiving advanced structures with actively controllable 3D static and dynamic properties.

title: An Inflammation‐Responsive and Biodegradable Microneedle Patch for Periodontal Soft and Hard Tissue Regeneration via Temporally Coordinated Sustained Release of Hydrogen and Calcium Ions
abstract: ABSTRACT Periodontitis progression is driven by a self‐perpetuating pathological microenvironment that couples inflammation, oxidative stress, osteoimmune disruption, and impaired regeneration, leading to alveolar bone resorption and periodontal tissue destruction. To address this challenge, we developed a reactive oxygen species (ROS)‐responsive microneedle system (CaSi 2 @PLGA MNs). By integrating CaSi 2 @PLGA microspheres, formed by encapsulating calcium silicide (CaSi 2 ) in poly(lactic‐ co ‐glycolic acid) (PLGA), into a ROS‐responsive microneedle matrix, we established a temporally coordinated therapeutic strategy featuring hierarchical release that couples two sequential processes: rapid microsphere release triggered by the inflammatory microenvironment, followed by gradual microsphere hydrolysis to enable sustained H 2 and Ca 2+ delivery over several days. This staged delivery enables an orderly transition from early periodontal inflammation to longer‐term tissue regeneration and repair. In vitro, the microspheres alleviated macrophage oxidative stress, promoted macrophage polarization toward a repair‐associated phenotype, and further supported osteogenic differentiation, cell migration, and angiogenesis. In vivo, CaSi 2 @PLGA MNs improved the periodontal inflammatory status, reduced alveolar bone resorption, promoted collagen remodeling and regeneration‐related marker expression, thereby demonstrating periodontal tissue repair potential. Overall, this study establishes a temporally coordinated local‐delivery platform that integrates inflammation control with regenerative support, providing a promising adjunctive strategy for periodontitis and demonstrating potential for extension to other inflammation‐associated osteolytic diseases.

title: NET‐Inhibiting Bio‐Orthogonal Gelated Neutrophils Reverse Maladaptive Trained Immunity and Protect Against Periodontitis Recurrence
abstract: ABSTRACT Maladaptive trained immunity (MTI) establishes pathogenic innate immune memory that amplifies the immune response to recurrent chronic inflammatory diseases such as periodontitis, but erasing this memory remains challenging. In this study, we identified neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) as key mediators of periodontitis‐induced MTI that reprogrammed bone marrow epigenetics and transcriptomics to amplify inflammation upon secondary challenge. Thus, we designed a NET‐inhibiting bioengineered platform (tPA@AGNs‐DNase I) to erase MTI and prevent recurrent inflammation. This platform was constructed by encapsulating tPA within activated gelated neutrophils (AGNs) and conjugating DNase I onto the surface by glycoengineering and click chemistry. Leveraging the inflammation‐homing property of AGNs, the platform enabled co‐delivery of two enzymes: DNase I degraded the DNA scaffold of NETs, while tPA disrupted fibrin‒neutrophil engagement to block NETosis, thereby achieving synergistic NET clearance. Local periodontal administration of tPA@AGNs‐DNase I not only resolved primary inflammation but also reversed established MTI by restoring aberrant bone marrow epigenetic and transcriptional reprogramming, thereby markedly attenuating recurrent hyperinflammation and alveolar bone loss in a religature‐induced periodontitis model. Collectively, this work provides a bioengineered platform that erases central MTI via in situ NET clearance, offering a paradigm‐shifting strategy to control chronic inflammatory disease recurrence.

title: Interfacial Amorphous Lithium Polysulfide Reservoir Design Enables High‐Power and Energy‐Dense All‐Solid‐State Li─S Battery
abstract: ABSTRACT All‐solid‐state Li─S batteries (ASSLSBs) promise ultrahigh energy density and safety but suffer from sluggish charge transfer kinetics at the triple‐phase (sulfur, carbon, and solid electrolyte) interface. Herein, we construct an amorphous lithium reservoir (ALR) made of short‐chained lithium polysulfides on sulfur particles to boost the interfacial sulfur redox kinetics and stability, thereby enabling high‐power and energy‐dense performance in ASSLSBs. Spectroscopic analyses (Raman, XPS, NMR, XAFS) reveal the ALR features a disordered Li─S bonding behavior, which store and anchor Li + ions surrounding the sulfur particles, creating rapid Li + conduction pathways and ensuring continuous Li + supply for accelerated S/Li 2 S conversion. Consequently, the ASSLSBs exhibit superior rate capability, achieving a high reversible capacity of 1115 mAh g −1 at 1C and 732.8 mAh g −1 at 2C, respectively, as well as excellent cycling stability with an ultralow capacity decay rate of 0.049% per cycle after 1000 cycles at 1C. Moreover, the ALR design also demonstrate a high practical capacity of 12.8 mAh cm −2 under high sulfur loading of 10 mg cm −2 , suggesting its promise to resolve the longstanding kinetics issue and paves a practical path for future high‐energy‐density ASSLSBs.

title: An Ultrarobust Dual‐Modal Neural Fiber With In‐Sensor Computing (Adv. Mater. 65/2026)
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: Smart Textile The cover shows a person touching a garment sleeve with luminous fibers visualizing tactile signals. The in-sensor-computing dual-modal (ID) neural fiber simultaneously senses pressure and position, fusing these features within the sensor while retaining flexibility, mechanical robustness, and seamless textile integration. Tapping and sliding gestures control music players and smart-home devices, transforming ordinary clothing into an intuitive human–machine interface. More details can be found in the Research Article by Xinqin Liao and co-workers (DOI: 10.1002/adma.75412).

title: Precisely Recyclable, Multifunctional, and High‐Performance Polyester Integrated by a Single Imidazolium‐Monomer
abstract: ABSTRACT Sustainable lifecycle management of polymer materials urgently requires integrating green synthesis, service‐stage desired properties, and end‐of‐life easy recyclability. Herein, by introducing a single imidazolium‐monomer, the all‐in‐one integration of green preparation (without solvents or additives), multifunctionality (flame retardancy and antistatic property), high performance (excellent chromaticity, high heat resistance and high strength), and precise recyclability (in mixed wastes) for polyesters is achieved, which also reduces the health risks caused by additive migration. The key is that the imidazolium unit can not only control the C(alkyl)─O cleavage at high temperature to hinder polyester combustion but also catalyze the C(carbonyl)─O cleavage at the ester site to achieve chemical recycling of polyester. Without halogen or phosphorus elements, the polyester exhibits excellent chromaticity (L* value > 89 and b* value 11 Ω), flame retardancy (the best UL‐94 V‐0 rating) and precise recycling in extremely complex mixed polymer wastes. This work successfully achieves lifecycle management of polyester materials via a single imidazolium‐monomer, providing a feasible platform for the next generation of sustainable, multifunctional and high‐performance polymer materials.

title: Heat‐Activated Reversible Conjugation Switching in Polymers Through Cooperative Ion Pairing
abstract: ABSTRACT Thermochromic conjugated polymers generally undergo transitions from colored to less‐colored states upon heating due to disruption of π‐conjugation. In contrast, heat‐triggered switching from a colorless state to a more intensely colored conjugated state remains largely unexplored. Here, we report a reversible conjugation‐switching polymer system governed by cooperative interactions between metal cations and counteranions. By incorporating lactone‐functionalized xanthene units directly into conjugated polymer backbones, weakly solvated Li + , Na + , and Ag + ions, acting cooperatively with their weakly coordinating counteranions, induce lactone ring opening and establish linear conjugation along the polymer backbone, thereby producing pronounced optical responses. Coordination of the metal ions by isopropanol reverses the process and restores the colorless state. A series of conjugated copolymers displayed thermally activated multicolor responses spanning blue, green, yellow, orange, red, magenta, and black, enabling rewritable invisible‐ink systems on paper substrates. Density functional theory calculations support a nearly barrierless Li + /PF 6 − ion‐pair‐cooperation‐promoted ring‐opening process and reveal reversible switching between twisted nonconjugated and planar linearly conjugated states. These results establish a metal‐ion‐regulated conjugation‐switching strategy for heat‐activated colorless‐to‐colored switching and responsive optical materials.

title: Standardization Transformation of Softwood Protolignin to Benzoxazole Molecule With Tumor‐Selective Cytotoxicity
abstract: ABSTRACT The protolignin standardization transformation into high‐value‐added pharmaceutical chemicals requires elaborate strategy design and catalytic system construction. Herein, a novel lignin valorization pattern to produce G‐lignin‐derived benzoxazoles from softwood is achieved, which involves the tandem CRF transformation of lignocellulose to C3‐alkyl guaiacol (C3‐G), stoichiometric diazotization‐reductive ammonification of C3‐G to aminophenol C3‐GAP, and photocatalytic cyclization of C3‐GAP to the benzoxazole C3‐GLB‐pCBA. The whole process can yield 6.2 wt% benzoxazole C3‐GLB‐pCBA from the aromatic guaiacyl rings of the original softwood lignin. Furthermore, the in vitro cytotoxicity assays with human osteosarcoma (HOS) cells, normal human osteoblast cells (hFOB1.19), and mouse 3T3 fibroblasts confirm the potential tumor‐selective cytotoxicity of the as‐synthesized G‐lignin‐derived benzoxazole C3‐GLB‐pCBA. Further TEA and LCA indicate the sustainability of the synthesis process of C3‐GLB‐pCBA from softwood. The success of the tandem pattern may inspire further studies on the high‐value utilization of lignin to produce pharmaceutical molecules.

title: Photoreduction of Chlorinated Volatile Waste Into C 2+ Hydrocarbons
abstract: ABSTRACT Chlorinated volatile organic compounds (Cl─VOCs) are a class of major environmental pollutants and potential human carcinogens. Dechlorination of Cl─VOC waste into harmless and value‐added chemicals under mild conditions is highly desirable yet challenging, and cannot be achieved using current photocatalytic methods. Here, we report the synthesis of the first nickel anthraquinone–thiolate complex for photoreduction of a variety of Cl─VOCs into unsaturated C 2+ hydrocarbons in good yields using visible light. Notably, the molecular system is capable of both reducing C 2 Cl─VOCs with high chlorine content into acetylene and C─C coupling of C 1 Cl─VOCs into ethylene and propylene. Mechanistic studies reveal that multielectron and multi‐proton reduction of the nickel complex is critical in generating the catalytically active species for various reductive dechlorination transformations. This study provides a blueprint for the conversion of chlorinated waste into highly valuable chemicals using solar energy.

title: An Acyclic Two‐Coordinate Stannyliumylidene Enables Sn II /Sn IV Redox Catalysis
abstract: ABSTRACT Main‐group redox catalysis hinges on a fundamental trade‐off, that is, reactive p‐block centres must be stable enough to isolate, yet flexible enough to cycle through oxidation states. In this regard, two‐coordinate stannyliumylidene ions with an accessible lone pair and vacant p‐orbital offer an attractive ambiphilic platform for engaging in redox processes. To date, most reported examples remain confined to π‐ or heteroatom‐donor‐stabilized rigid frameworks, and the isolation of a genuinely two‐coordinate acyclic stannyliumylidene has remained elusive. Herein, we report the synthesis and isolation of a two‐coordinate, acyclic, mono‐N‐heterocyclic‐carbene‐stabilized stannyliumylidene paired with a weakly coordinating [B(3,5‐(CF 3 ) 2 C 6 H 3 ) 4 ] − anion. Stripped of additional donor stabilization, the tin centre is rendered highly electrophilic while maintaining an accessible lone pair. This enhanced electrophilicity enabled capture of a stannyliumylidene–ketone adduct, the first structurally characterized ketone‐bound tetryliumylidene intermediate that is directly implicated in a catalytic cycle. Comprehensive mechanistic studies, combining experimental results with theoretical calculations, reveal an Sn(II)/Sn(IV) redox manifold that drives catalytic turnover. Together, these results significantly expand the landscape of tin‐based redox catalysis and highlight that accessing stable low‐valent stannyliumylidene ions with a minimal coordination number and weaker donor stabilization is a feasible approach for unlocking transition‐metal‐like redox behaviour at the tin centre.

title: Visible light drives bright extreme-ultraviolet high harmonics
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Coherent extreme-ultraviolet (XUV) light is a central tool in modern photon science, probing the electronic, chemical and structural properties of matter. High-harmonic generation can extend the reach of laser sources into this spectral range, but the achievable photon flux falls sharply as photon energy increases. We show experimentally and theoretically that plasma-core-induced self-guiding of a visible-wavelength driver in helium sustains high intensity and favorable phase matching over an extended propagation length. We achieve a conversion efficiency of up to 10−6 in a single high-harmonic line and phase-matched emission extending to 100 eV. With less than 10 W of average power at 516 nm from a frequency-doubled ytterbium laser, we generate 1.8 × 1011 photons s−1 within 2 % bandwidth at 13.5 nm (91.8 eV), exceeding previous reports by more than an order of magnitude. These results establish a power-scalable XUV platform for actinic metrology, spectroscopy and coherent imaging.
