title: Deep ultraviolet gallium-oxide avalanche photodiodes reaching an impulse-response-derived gain-bandwidth record of 152 GHz
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Solar-blind Ga2O3-based photodetectors, sensing deep ultraviolet (DUV) light (200–280 nm), offer unparalleled opportunities for secure non-line-of-sight optical communication. Yet their practical applications have been largely hindered by the relatively low gain-bandwidth product (GBP), due to the fundamental trade-off between response speed and photoelectric gain. Here, we report nanosecond-level-response solar-blind avalanche photodetectors based on β-Ga2O3/MgO/La0.8Ca0.2MnO3 (LCMO) n-Barrier-p heterojunctions with high apparent gain over 2.6×106, thereby achieving an impulse-response-derived record-breaking 152 GHz gain-bandwidth product — outpacing the state-of-the-art Ga2O3-based devices by 3 orders of magnitude. The MgO interlayer enables lattice matching and engineered conduction band offset to boost gain and suppress dark current, while the p-type LCMO layer introduces a large valence band offset and simultaneously establishes a hole-selective transport highway for ultrafast response. This work not only resolves the longstanding gain-bandwidth trade-off in DUV photodetection but also presents a universal band-engineering framework for next-generation optoelectronics.

title: Accelerating high-throughput catalyst screening by direct generation of equilibrium adsorption structures
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The adsorption energy serves as a crucial descriptor for the large-scale screening of catalysts. Nevertheless, the limited distribution of training data for the extensively utilised machine learning interatomic potential, predominantly sourced from near-equilibrium structures, results in unreliable adsorption structures and consequent adsorption energy predictions. In this context, we present DBCata, a deep generative model that integrates a periodic Brownian-bridge framework with an equivariant graph neural network to establish a low-dimensional transition manifold between unrelaxed and DFT-relaxed structures, without requiring explicit energy or force information. Upon training, DBCata effectively generates high-fidelity adsorption geometries, achieving an interatomic distance mean absolute error of 0.035 Å on the MamunHighT2019 dataset from Catalysis-Hub, which is approximately 70% lower than that of the current state-of-the-art machine learning potential models. Moreover, the corresponding DFT accuracy can be improved within 0.1 eV in 94% of instances by identifying and refining anomalous predictions through a hybrid chemical-heuristic and self-supervised outlier detection approach. We demonstrate that DBCata enables accelerated high-throughput computational screening for alloy catalysts in the oxygen reduction reaction, highlighting the potential of DBCata as a powerful tool for catalyst design and optimisation.

title: Shape conforming Janus hydrogel for preventing anastomotic leaks
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Anastomotic leaks are severe complications following gastrointestinal surgery. The shape conformability of powder-based hydrogels makes them potentially suitable for leak-sealing, but they typically cause undesirable tissue adhesion, prohibiting clinical applications. Here we present a powder-based Janus hydrogel that forms in situ to simultaneously prevent anastomotic leaks and tissue adhesions. By rational regulation of dissolution and gelation kinetics, a powder mixture of chitosan lactate and oxidized chondroitin sulfate rapidly forms an adhesive porous scaffold in situ via amine-aldehyde condensation. A zwitterionic anti-adhesive layer is synthesized on the peritoneal side of the porous layer, creating a stable Janus structure via mechanical interlocking. The chemical and structural asymmetry between the serosal and peritoneal surfaces reconciles the conflicting demands of robust tissue integration, leakage prevention, and anti-adhesive safety. Further, the Janus hydrogel improves short- and long-term survival by reducing immune responses and perianastomotic adhesions, highlighting its potential for clinical translation in gastrointestinal surgery.

title: [c2]Daisy-chain molecular turing machines with switchable fluorescence outputs
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Synthetic small-molecule machines capable of bidirectionally reading and writing information on molecular tapes with visual output remain elusive due to the challenge in amplifying molecular-scale motions into macroscopic signals. Herein, we report two [c2]daisy-chain molecular Turing machines that convert reversible mechanical motions into different fluorescence signals by developing novel aggregation-induced emission luminogens with an intramolecular charge transfer mechanism. Attributed to the collective and amplified shuttling motions triggered by anions or solvents, the [c2]daisy chains exhibit controllable and reversible fluorescence modulation in solution for up to 42 cycles. Moreover, incorporation of [c2]daisy chains into polymers yields fast-response macroscopic Turing machines capable of conformation-dependent fluorescence switching. Importantly, the [c2]daisy chains enable binary ASCII and nucleotide-base encoding, allowing visual representation of letters, digits, and 64 genetic codons. By mapping codons to fluorescence, they also enable visual decoding of DNA information, bridging molecular-scale motion to macroscopically readable information processing and advancing functional molecular computation.

title: Localized strain-engineered 1D electron guides in 2D MoS2 devices with synaptic memory and high-mobility transistor functionalities
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Local strain engineering has been studied as an effective strategy to modify the electronic band structure of two-dimensional (2D) semiconductors. However, using precisely controlled localized strain as a scalable tool for directing and controlling charge dynamics in 2D electronics remains largely underexplored. Here, we introduce wafer-scale localized strain engineering that applies periodically localized one-dimensional (1D) uniaxial strain to monolayer MoS2-based dual-functional electronics. By transferring MoS2 onto a line-patterned HfO2 substrate, we can deterministically generate a periodic localized 1D potential well. This approach creates a well-defined 1D potential landscape that facilitates dual functionality within a single material platform, depending on the alignment between the potential well orientation and the direction of carrier transport. Charge transport perpendicular to the 1D potential wells results in controlled charge trapping, thereby yielding a multibit synaptic memory device, whereas transport parallel to the potential wells experiences reduced lattice scattering and an effective mass with trap-free carrier conduction, leading to a high-mobility field-effect transistor. Systematic transport analyses elucidate how localized uniaxial strain modulates charge-trap density, lattice scattering, and effective mass, giving rise to direction-dependent charge transport. These findings highlight localized 1D strain as an effective design parameter for high-performance, scalable multifunctional 2D electronics.

title: Entropy-engineered polar heterogeneity enables near-decoupled polarization–strain behavior for high-density energy storage
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Dielectric energy-storage (ES) ceramics are central to pulsed power technologies, yet excessive polarization–strain coupling in lead-free systems induces electrostrain, compromising ES density and device reliability. Here, we introduce configurational entropy (Sconfig) as a quantitative design parameter to engineer polar heterogeneity and regulate polarization–strain interactions in lead-free relaxor ferroelectrics (RFEs). Entropy engineering generates chemical heterogeneity, local lattice distortions, strain-field fluctuations, and polar fragmentation, disrupting long-range polar coherence and reducing the spatial cooperativity of polarization-induced deformation while preserving large field-induced polarization. This entropy-mediated reconstruction of the polar landscape yields an ultralow electrostrictive coefficient Q33 of ~0.010 m4 C–2 in a (Bi0.5Na0.5)TiO3-based high-entropy RFE, enabling a near-decoupled polarization–strain response with high polarization and suppressed macroscopic electrostrain. Multilayer ceramic capacitors achieve a recoverable ES density of 21.5 J cm–3 at 1200 kV cm–1, together with a low electrostrain of 0.073% at 300 kV cm–1. Atomic-scale imaging reveals vortex and antivortex polarization configurations associated with entropy-induced structural heterogeneity and lattice distortions. Phase-field simulations demonstrate that heterogeneous polarization states redistribute elastic energy and reduce cooperative polarization-induced deformation. This work establishes Sconfig as a quantitative descriptor for engineering weak electromechanical coupling and high-ES-density performance in lead-free dielectric capacitors.

title: Mapping temperature using transmission Kikuchi diffraction
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: As electronic devices are engineered at increasingly smaller length scales, new nanoscopic metrologies are needed. Measuring nanoscale temperatures and pressures is challenging as physical contact inevitably perturbs the system, and collecting far-field thermal radiation limits the spatial resolution. Kikuchi diffraction thermometry (KDTh), a non-contact scanning electron microscope (SEM) technique, can sensitively map nanoscale temperatures. Local lattice changes measured by Kikuchi pattern fitting enable translating volumetric strain to temperature via the material’s coefficient of thermal expansion (CTE). Measurements on Joule-heated graphite come from rastering a 5.5-nm electron probe across the sample, achieving a ~ 0.01% fractional precision and 2.2 K/Hz" role="presentation">Hz\sqrt{{{\rm{Hz}}}} temperature sensitivity. KDTh offers superior sensitivity by fitting the entire Kikuchi pattern, instead of a particular Kikuchi band or interband angle. Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) techniques can achieve a similar precision, but electron-transparency limits their applications. KDTh can operate in both transmission and reflection modes to cost-effectively accommodate a variety of samples.

title: A highly distorted benzenium cation
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: In contrast to the well-explored peripheral functionalization of benzene, its skeletal alteration remains underdeveloped. Here, we report a highly distorted benzenium cation, 2,3-dihydroxy-1,4,6-triamino-5-nitrobenzenium (TANBC+), featuring a ring twist angle of 35.91° and a ring C-C bond length of 1.540 Å, both rank the highest among all benzenium cations. Such pronounced structural distortions endow TANBC+ with unique electronic properties, including a highly positive electrostatic charge on the warped carbon, weak aromaticity, and a low ring bond dissociation energy. Consequently, instead of undergoing peripheral functionalization like typical benzenium cations, TANBC+ participates in three distinct benzene ring reconstruction pathways or remains inert under standard electrophilic substitution conditions. Moreover, despite its distorted structure, TANBC+ exhibits excellent ambient stability, stabilized by extensive hydrogen bonding, and can be synthesized readily without harsh conditions usually required for conventional benzenium cations. This work not only introduces a new strategy for benzene reconstruction but also redefines the role of benzenium cations from mediators of peripheral functionalization to promoters of skeletal alteration, thereby advancing the fundamental chemistry of benzene.

title: Cryptochiral Circularly Polarized Luminescence Emerges From Cosolvent‐Regulated Pathway Complexity in Amyloidogenic Peptide Self‐Assembly
abstract: ABSTRACT Circularly polarized luminescence (CPL) is important for chiral photonics, optical encryption, bioimaging, and information processing. It is usually associated with an identifiable chiral ground‐state organization, and CPL without detectable ground‐state chirality remains comparatively unexplored. Herein, we report a rare “ cryptochiral CPL ” phenomenon arising from cosolvent‐regulated pathway complexity in the self‐assembly of a naphthalimide (NMI)‐amyloidogenic peptide conjugate (PEP‐L). In water, PEP‐L spontaneously forms thermodynamically stable, emissive nanofibers with pronounced supramolecular chirality and strong CPL. Adding a small amount of cosolvent redirects assembly toward kinetically trapped spherical nanoassemblies and shows no detectable Circular Dichroism (CD) response in the naphthalimide chromophore region, but retains pronounced CPL, which decouples ground‐state and excited‐state chiroptical responses. We term this behavior cryptochiral CPL . Thermal annealing or aging converts the spheres into thermodynamically favored nanofibers with distinct CD and CPL characteristics. The enantiomer PEP‐D shows mirror‐image chiroptical responses, which validates the phenomenon. Density functional theory (DFT) and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations under different conditions give molecular‐level insight into the conformation, noncovalent interactions, and supramolecular organization of the different assembly states. These findings establish a new conceptual framework for adaptive chiral photonic materials and open opportunities for hidden optical encoding and biomolecular photonic systems.

title: Solvent‐Removal‐Induced Lattice Reconstruction Enables Tunable Mn 2+ Luminescence in Hybrid [MnBr 4 ] 2− for 3D X‐Ray Imaging
abstract: ABSTRACT It is challenging to understand how noncoordinating lattice guests regulate Mn 2+ luminescence without changing the metal coordination environment. Herein, we report a solvent‐removal‐induced single‐crystal‐to‐single‐crystal (SCSC) transformation from ethanol‐containing (C 33 H 29 NP) 2 MnBr 4 ·EtOH (CZTPPM) to the solvent‐free phase (C 33 H 29 NP) 2 MnBr 4 (CZTPPM1). Ethanol removal preserves the configuration of isolated [MnBr 4 ] 2− tetrahedra while inducing lattice contraction, hydrogen‐bonding network reorganization, and enhanced tetrahedral distortion. As a result, the emission undergoes a distinct green (518 nm) to yellow‐green (543 nm) shift. Combined low‐temperature excitation spectroscopy, crystal‐field analysis, electron‐phonon coupling evaluation, and excited‐state decay kinetics establish a correlation between supramolecular lattice reconstruction, local ligand‐field modulation, and excited‐state relaxation. Furthermore, the solvent‐free phase retains efficient scintillation performance (including light yield of 56, 516 photons MeV −1 and detection limit of 59.97 nGy air s −1 ) and enables high‐resolution static X‐ray imaging and 3D X‐ray reconstruction. This work provides insight into noncoordinating‐guest‐mediated crystal‐field regulation and demonstrates its potential for developing multifunctional luminescent materials for radiation imaging.

title: Dual‐DUBTACs Enable Targeted Protein Stabilization via Multi‐DUB Engagement
abstract: ABSTRACT Targeted protein stabilization has emerged as a promising therapeutic strategy for restoring the abundance and function of disease‐relevant proteins. Deubiquitinase‐targeting chimeras (DUBTACs) offer a chemical approach to protein stabilization by recruiting deubiquitinases (DUBs) to promote target deubiquitination. However, current DUBTAC strategies generally rely on the recruitment of a single DUB, leaving the potential of engaging multiple DUBs through a common recruiter largely unexplored. Here, we report a dual‐DUBTAC strategy that enables targeted protein stabilization through the recruitment of two distinct DUBs. Using Degrasyn, a small‐molecule reversible covalent inhibitor of multiple DUBs, as a privileged scaffold, we engineered small molecules that selectively stabilize CFTR and cGAS and demonstrate that these compounds enhance target protein homeostasis through USP9X‐ and USP5‐mediated deubiquitination in cells. By decoupling substrate stabilization from reliance on a single DUB, the Dual‐DUB platform confers adaptability across diverse ubiquitin chain architectures and rewired proteostasis networks characteristic of heterogeneous tumors and could overcome potential drug resistance in future clinical applications. This strategy expands the chemical space for restoring protective proteins and establishes a general framework for functional reactivation of destabilized tumor‐suppressive pathways.

title: Entropy‐Compensated Electrolyte Enables Low‐Temperature 400 Wh Kg −1 Silicon‐Based Lithium‐Ion Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Electrolytes dictate the low‐temperature (LT) performance of Si‐anode lithium‐ion batteries, wherein bulk solvation governs Li + transport and interfacial stability. Especially, enlarged ionic clusters and strengthened ion pairing at LT hinder Li + migration, limiting Li + supply to the interface and destabilizing interfacial reactions. Herein, we propose an entropy‐compensation strategy to counteract LT‐induced solvation deterioration in Si‐anode electrolytes. Increasing the solvation entropy ( ΔS solv ) compensates for the LT‐induced increase in the Gibbs free‐energy change for ion‐cluster dissociation ( ΔG solv ), thereby raising the corresponding equilibrium constant ( K solv ) and suppressing ion pairing. Consequently, electrolytes preferentially form smaller anion‐rich ionic clusters, delivering an approximately threefold increase in ionic conductivity at −20°C. Enhanced bulk transport alleviates concentration polarization, stabilizes the interfacial solvation environment, and promotes uniform SEI‐forming reactions. Benefiting from this coupled bulk‐interfacial optimization, Ah‐level pouch cells retain 97.8% capacity after 165 cycles at −20°C and support sustained discharge at −81°C. This strategy enables high‐energy pouch cells to deliver 400 Wh kg −1 under ambient conditions and 339 Wh kg −1 at LT, while an Ah‐level pouch cell retains 80% capacity after 1150 cycles at 2 C. This work identifies ΔS solv as a critical thermodynamic descriptor for low‐temperature electrolyte design.

title: Localized Dipoles Enable Synergistic Kinetic and Thermodynamic Piezoreforming of Waste Plastics
abstract: ABSTRACT The piezocatalytic plastic wastes into clean fuels at ambient conditions offers considerable promise, but hindering by both rapid carrier recombination in kinetics and slow surface reactions in thermodynamics. Here, we present a conceptually distinct strategy to simultaneously tackle both core challenges by tailoring localized dipole via anchoring FeSe 2 nanoclusters onto MoSe 2 piezocatalysts. These clusters induce localized lattice distortions via strong metal‐support interaction, generating localized dipole that serve a dual function. Kinetically, localized dipole can effectively capture the electrons excited by piezoelectricity, suppressing recombination and establishing a dominant, long‐lived interfacial charge transfer channel directly to the reactants. Thermodynamically, localized dipole can lower the d‐band center of the active sites, enhance the adsorption of reaction intermediates, and significantly reduce the activation energy barrier of key intermediates. Therefore, the optimized catalyst exhibits carbon monoxide (CO) evolution of 87.65 µmol·g −1 with high selectivity in the piezocatalytic peroxydisulfate (PDS) system, 30.5 times that of MoSe 2 . Importantly, after simple pretreatment of polylactic acid (PLA), the CO production reaches 1886.55 µmol·g −1 with stable long‐term performance. This work elucidates the fundamental role of localized dipole in harmonizing charge dynamics with surface catalysis, providing an effective approach for designing highly efficient and durable piezocatalysts for challenging chemical transformations.

title: Molten‐Salt Surface Restructuring of 3D‐Printed Agitator Exposes Ni 0 Active Sites for Efficient Selective Alkyne Hydrogenation
abstract: ABSTRACT Three‐dimensional (3D) printing enables the integration of structural engineering with catalytic functionality, yet extending this concept to high‐pressure liquid‐phase hydrogenation remains challenging because catalytic efficiency, selectivity, and structural robustness are difficult to optimize simultaneously. Here, we report a strategy that couples additive manufacturing with molten‐salt activation to engineer a 3D‐printed bladed agitator catalyst (AB–MSL–H 2 ). Molten‐salt treatment selectively reconstructs the alloy surface while preserving the printed architecture, generating a Ni‐enriched interface with abundant exposed metallic Ni 0 active sites. Combined experimental and theoretical investigations reveal that surface reconstruction enriches accessible Ni 0 sites to direct the desired hydrogenation pathway while suppressing isomerization, cyclization, and hydrogenolysis, whereas the integrated bladed architecture simultaneously enhances gas‐liquid‐solid mass transfer and reactant accessibility. Consequently, AB–MSL–H 2 achieves complete conversion of 2‐butyne‐1,4‐diol with a 1,4‐butanediol yield exceeding 97%. This work establishes a general strategy for transforming additively manufactured structural alloys into catalytically active reactor components through molten‐salt‐induced surface reconstruction, expanding the scope of catalyst‐reactor integration for high‐pressure liquid‐phase catalysis.

title: Atomic‐Scale Origin of Charge Density Wave–Driven Metal–Semiconductor Transition in an Incommensurately Modulated Metal–Organic Framework
abstract: ABSTRACT Although metal–organic frameworks are widely recognized for their long‐range crystalline periodicity, they can also exhibit intrinsic aperiodic structures associated with incommensurate modulation, whose observation has been exceptionally rare. In low‐dimensional condensed matter physics, these unique structures often give rise to novel physical phenomena such as charge density wave. However, owing to limited direct experimental evidence, the relationship between incommensurate structural modulation and temperature‐dependent electronic transport in conductive metal–organic frameworks remains incompletely understood. Here, using high‐quality Pr 3 HHTP 2 (HHTP = 2,3,6,7,10,11‐hexahydroxytriphenylene) single crystals as a model system, we resolve the incommensurately modulated structure at 100 K (modulation vector q = 0.39143(12) c * ) via temperature‐dependent single‐crystal x‐ray diffraction. The observed reversible metal–semiconductor transition near 350 K occurs in a similar temperature range to the disappearance of the structural modulation, supporting a connection between lattice distortion and electronic behavior. The modulation reappears upon cooling, with guest water molecules influencing both the extent of its recovery and the electrical conductivity of the material. This work establishes a concrete experimental criterion for one‐dimensional charge density wave in metal‐organic frameworks and provides an ideal platform for probing coupled electronic–lattice modulations.

title: Biomimetic N ‐Terminal Homologation of Amino Acids
abstract: ABSTRACT Homologation is a key tactic used in the lead optimization of small‐molecule pharmaceuticals due to the potent impact such modifications can have on target affinity and physicochemical properties. However, while many elegant homologation strategies have been developed for the synthesis of β 3 ‐amino acids via decarboxylation, preparation of the β 2 ‐amino acid homologues remains underexplored. We report a general biomimetic strategy for the N ‐terminal homologation of amino acids using photoredox catalysis. Key to the success of this approach is a radical translocation cascade driven by single‐electron transfer. This methodology provides streamlined access to a range of cyclic and acyclic β 2 ‐amino acids and phosphonates, providing new synthetic opportunities within drug discovery programs.

title: Indirect Characterization of 14 N Nuclei via 1 H‐Detected Rotating‐Frame Relaxometry
abstract: ABSTRACT 14 N NMR is notoriously difficult to perform in liquids due to the very fast spin relaxation and the large quadrupolar couplings, which render many signals invisible. We show here how 14 N nuclei of biomolecular constituents can be probed indirectly by reintroducing the scalar relaxation of the second kind contribution as a relaxation pathway for J‐coupled protons in double resonance spin‐locking experiments. The enhanced 1 H relaxation rates in the rotating‐frame allow for direct evaluation of nitrogen chemical shifts and polarization lifetimes, from which one‐ and even two‐bond 1 H‐ 14 N scalar couplings as well as 14 N quadrupolar interactions can be determined. We demonstrate the versatility of this method by characterizing 1 H‐ 14 N spin pairs in several molecules of biological importance, showing proton relaxation enhancements beyond one order of magnitude. We further observe a pronounced effect from intermolecular hydrogen bonding. Our approach can be readily integrated into existing liquid‐state NMR methodologies, as demonstrated here for 1 H‐detected relaxation‐editing experiments with water suppression. This method provides access to nitrogen's picosecond‐modulated quadrupolar interaction via sensitive proton detection in systems that would otherwise yield almost no detectable direct 14 N signal even after averaging over thousands of transients.

title: Biosynthesis of iboga alkaloids
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Tabernanthe iboga (iboga) is the source of voacangine, which is widely used as a semi-synthetic starting material for the anti-addiction agent ibogaine. Despite extensive investigation of voacangine biosynthesis, production of this compound cannot be reconstituted in a heterologous host, suggesting that one or more enzymes required for biosynthesis are missing. Additionally, T. iboga produces ibophyllidine, a pyrroloindole alkaloid that utilizes the same upstream precursor as voacangine, but is a member of a structurally distinct alkaloid class. Here we use bulk and single cell gene expression from leaf and root tissue to identify the unknown enzymes from these two pathways. We identify two additional enzymes that enable biosynthesis of voacangine in a heterologous host. The missing enzymes includes a pathogenesis-related (PR)10 family protein that likely catalyzes cyclization of a transient intermediate. Careful analysis of gene expression profiles in leaf and root also enabled the discovery of four additional enzymes that convert an upstream intermediate to ibophyllidine. This work reveals the chemical logic that generates two distinct alkaloid scaffolds in this important medicinal plant.

title: Influenza A virus orchestrates ciliated cell fate and injury during the mucociliary damage repair cycle
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Influenza A virus causes acute damage to airway epithelium, yet the damage–repair cycle and mechanisms underlying persistent mucociliary clearance (MCC) dysfunction long after viral clearance remain unclear. Here, using longitudinal in vivo quantitative micro-optical coherence tomography, we show that global MCC impairment persists for more than 14 days, marked by impaired ciliary activity and sustained mucus hypersecretion in male mice infected with the H1N1 influenza A/Puerto Rico/8/1934 (PR8) strain. Through lineage tracing and multi-omics analyses, we identify an immune-mediated transdifferentiation program in which IFN signaling activates the IDO1–AhR axis to drive ciliated-to-mucous cell fate transition and chronic muco-obstruction after H1N1 PR8 infection in a reconstructed human bronchial epithelium model. In parallel, we identify the viral M2 protein as a key driver of ciliary loss, suppressing the host TP73–FOXJ1–RFX3 regulatory axis and promoting proteasomal degradation of FOXJ1. Together, these findings uncover host- and virus-driven pathways that cooperatively impair airway epithelial homeostasis and sustain MCC failure beyond active infection, highlighting therapeutic targets for post-influenza muco-obstructive disease.

title: Structural basis for constitutive activation of oncogenic gp130 mutants found in human inflammatory hepatocellular adenomas
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Inflammatory hepatocellular adenomas (IHCAs) are benign liver tumors primarily driven by somatic mutations in the gp130 receptor, resulting in its constitutive activation. To uncover the structural mechanisms underlying this activation, we employ cryo-electron microscopy and mutagenesis to study five representative IHCAs-associated gp130 mutants and two engineered mutants with ligand-independent activity. Most mutants form “X”-shaped dimers through a 3D domain-swapping mechanism, characterized by large separations between juxtamembrane domains and reliant on D1 domain-mediated “tip-to-tip” interactions for dimer clustering and activation. A rare mutant displays a distinct “Y”-shaped dimer conformation, with closely aligned juxtamembrane domains enabling direct activation independent of dimer clustering. These findings highlight the diversity of gp130 mutant activation mechanisms and provide a foundation for developing therapeutic strategies targeting aberrant gp130 signaling in IHCAs.

title: G3BP1-induced retrograde transport blockade triggers HSC activation and liver fibrosis via COPI alternative splicing
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The molecular mechanisms underlying hepatic stellate cell (HSC) activation and subsequent liver fibrogenesis remain incompletely elucidated. Here, Ras GTPase-activating protein-binding protein 1 (G3BP1) is identified a significant upregulation in liver specimens from patients with liver fibrosis and experimental murine fibrosis models. G3BP1 promotes HSC activation in human LX-2 cells, primary mouse HSCs, and CCl4-/BDL-induced fibrotic mouse models, acting independently of stress granules (SGs). Genetic ablation of hepatic G3BP1 attenuates HSC activation and fibrotic progression. Integrative transcriptomic and APEX‑mass spectrometry analyses in HSCs reveal that G3BP1 regulates alternative splicing of coat protein complex Ⅰ (COPI) subunits through functional interaction with the splicing factor heterogeneous nuclear ribonucleoprotein M (hnRNPM). The consequent accumulation of exon 2-deficient COPG1 and exon 8-deficient COPB2 isoforms impairs COPI-dependent retrograde transport and induces endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress, which drives HSC activation and fibrogenesis. Further studies demonstrate that G3BP1 recruits SRPK1 to phosphorylate hnRNPM, thereby promotes alternative splicing of COPI subunits. Pharmacological intervention of G3BP1/SRPK1/hnRNPM improves liver fibrosis. In conclusion, these results uncover an unrecognized role of G3BP1 in HSC activation by promoting COPI alternative splicing, and provide a potential therapeutic target for liver fibrosis.

title: Functionalized Interface Engineering of Cellulose-Based Electrolytes for Safety and Long-Life Li–Metal Batteries
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Cellulose-based electrolytes are low-cost, eco-friendly solid-state electrolyte candidates owing to renewability and biodegradability. However, their flammability raises safety concerns, and crystallinity leads to low ion conduction. Herein, a dual-functionalization strategy is proposed, which grafts phytic and sulfate groups onto cellulose via a ternary deep eutectic solvent system. Phytic groups provide flame retardancy, and sulfate groups realize fast Li-ion conduction. The resulting electrolyte delivers a Li-ion conductivity (1.48 × 10–3 S cm–1) and an oxidation potential (5.2 V), and the fabricated electrolyte membrane shows a uniform structure, enhanced mechanical flexibility, and strong tensile stress. It also shows good compatibility with the Li metal, enabling stable cycling and long cycle life for solid-state Li–metal cells, including the LiFePO4 and LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2 cells over 542 and 409 cycles, respectively. Moreover, this solid-state electrolyte exhibits self-extinguishing properties, helping solid-state cells work stably under extreme thermal conditions. This research offers an approach for developing safe cellulose-based electrolytes for next-generation Li–metal batteries.

title: A global atlas of digital dermatology to map innovation and disparities
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Artificial intelligence promises democratized access to dermatological care, but model reliability depends on the quality and comprehensiveness of the underlying data. Despite rapid growth in publicly available dermatology images, the field lacks quantitative indicators to measure whether new datasets expand clinical coverage or merely replicate what is already known. Existing collections are widely assumed to be biased, yet the scale and topography of these gaps have remained unquantified, leaving the community without a road map for strategic data acquisition. Here, we show, by unifying 1.1 million images from 29 public datasets into a queryable semantic atlas, that the global archive is markedly skewed and increasingly redundant: darker skin tones (Fitzpatrick V–VI) constitute only 11.0% of images, pediatric patients only 2.3%, and informational novelty has plateaued despite exponential growth, revealing where targeted data acquisition is most needed.

title: The missing dimension of European energy sovereignty: The geopolitics of market infrastructure
abstract: European energy-security analysis has focused mainly on physical supply. This paper examines a less-examined dimension of European energy sovereignty: exposure to the mechanisms through which prices are formed, risks are managed and uncertainty is transmitted across interconnected markets. We distinguish physical dependence on a fuel from exposure to its price, and argue that the combination of weather-driven renewable variability, gas prices and carbon prices is closer to a Keynesian uncertainty than to a sum of insurable risks: their relationships are unstable, policy responses alter the rules of price formation, and hedging can turn price risk into liquidity risk. Nordic annual day-ahead prices for 2015–2025 illustrate the mechanism. In 2022, southern Norway (NO2) and southern Sweden (SE4), with almost no gas-fired generation, averaged €211/MWh and €152/MWh, against €24/MWh (NO4) and €59/MWh (SE1) in the north. This suggests that exposure depends on interconnection and congestion more than on national generation mix, although annual data cannot separate these from hydrology and nuclear availability. Norway and Sweden have since politically responded to this shock by postponing or withdrawing new interconnector investment. We then examine the infrastructure of price formation: Germany's retention of a single bidding zone despite the 2025 Bidding Zone Review, and the concentration of trading, clearing and benchmark functions across electricity, gas and carbon markets notably around EEX Group and ICE. We argue that limiting and distributing this uncertainty, rather than eliminating it, deserves treatment as a dimension of European energy sovereignty alongside security of physical supply.

title: Radical Buffering by Isolated Ru and Fe Sites in ZSM‐5 for Selective Methane Oxidation to Formic Acid
abstract: ABSTRACT The selective conversion of methane under mild conditions is limited by the uncontrolled reactivity of radical intermediates (·CH 3 , ·OH) generated during Fe‐catalyzed oxidation with H 2 O 2 . Here we report a radical buffering strategy in which atomically dispersed Ru is co‐loaded with Fe in ZSM‐5 as an ·OH reservoir, steering intermediates toward selective Eley‐Rideal‐type coupling in the micropores. The Ru‐Fe/ZSM‐5 catalyst achieves an oxygenate productivity of 37.5 mmol·g cat −1 ·h −1 at 70°C with 95.7% oxygenate selectivity and 92.3% formic acid selectivity among liquid products, a 2.2‐fold improvement over Fe/ZSM‐5. Extended X‐ray absorption fine structure analysis shows that Ru and Fe exist as two independent populations of single atoms with no metal–metal bonding. Electron paramagnetic resonance and in situ infrared spectroscopy show that Fe activates CH 4 to ·CH 3 while Ru activates H 2 O 2 and holds part of the resulting ·OH. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations show that Ru binds ·OH more strongly than Fe (−3.130 compared to −2.738 eV), and dissociates H 2 O 2 nearly thermoneutrally (+0.077 eV). Therefore ·OH is held on Ru rather than on the Fe. This work establishes radical buffering by independent single‐atom populations in confined micropores as a design principle for controlling selectivity in radical‐mediated catalysis.

title: Advancing C3 Polymerization of Alkynylcyclopropanes via a Synergistic Lewis Acid/Brønsted Base/C(sp 3 )–H Bond System
abstract: ABSTRACT The integration of cyclopropane chemistry with polymer science could offer access to unique all‐carbon polymers. However, the ring‐opening polymerization (ROP) of cyclopropanes generally requires strong electron‐donating and ‐withdrawing substituents, limiting the use of electronically less activated monomers such as 2‐alkynylcyclopropane‐1,1‐dicarboxylates (ACPs). Here, we demonstrate that the synergistic combination of a Lewis acid and a Brønsted base overcomes the electronic limitations imposed by carbon–carbon triple bonds, including their high electronegativity and strong coordinating ability, enabling the unprecedented C3 ROP of ACPs. This process is regulated by a reversible‐deactivation equilibrium mediated by chain‐end C(sp 3 )─H bonds, affording well‐defined polymers bearing alkyne side groups. The resulting functional polymers provide a versatile platform for applications ranging from stimulus‐responsive sensing to Raman imaging.

title: Alternating Terpolymerization of CO 2 With Cyclosilanes and Epoxides to A‐B‐C‐Sequenced Recyclable Poly(silyl ether–ester)
abstract: ABSTRACT Carbon dioxide (CO 2 )‐derived polyesters represent an attractive yet underdeveloped class of sustainable polymers, with most existing CO 2 ‐based polyesters relying on carbonate linkages in their backbones with statistical or block sequences. Here, we introduce terpolymerization of CO 2 with cyclosilanes and epoxides to access poly(silyl ether–ester) with perfectly alternating A‐B‐C (CO 2 ‐ alt ‐cyclosilane‐ alt ‐epoxide) sequences. This terpolymerization is enabled by the thermodynamically favored formation of Si─O bonds, providing a driving force for efficient incorporation of both silalactones and epoxides into the terpolymer backbone in an alternating fashion. A range of epoxide and silacyclobutane substrates can be incorporated into the polyester, affording structurally diverse terpolymers. Notably, these polymers are stable thermally ( T d up to 313°C) and hydrolytically (in neutral water) but can slowly degrade under acidic or basic conditions and be chemically depolymerized under mild catalytic conditions to recover the silalactone monomer.

title: Greenhouse gas responses to coastal wetland land use change vary by ecosystem and conversion pathway
source: Earth and environmental sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Land-use and land-cover change (LULCC) is altering greenhouse gas (GHG) dynamics in coastal wetlands, yet how these responses vary among ecosystems and conversion pathways remains uncertain. Here, we synthesized 276 studies and applied multilevel meta-analysis to paired LULCC comparisons. GHG responses varied with pre-conversion wetland type, destination land use, hydrology, and soil carbon and nitrogen status. Pooled sustained-flux global warming potential (SGWP) was ‒122.41 ± 81.99 mg CO2e m‒2 h‒1 for natural coastal wetlands and 250.60 ± 101.06 for LULCC sites, corresponding to 0.17 ± 0.06 Gt CO2e of cumulative emissions over two decades. The descriptive SGWP contrast with pooled LULCC sites was larger for vegetated wetlands ( + 309.32%) than for tidal flats ( + 165.02%). Ecologically restored wetlands showed negative pooled SGWP ( − 33.03 ± 114.70 mg CO2e m‒2 h‒1), contrasting with the positive pooled LULCC estimate. Our results indicate that GHG responses to coastal wetland conversion are ecosystem- and pathway-specific, underscoring the importance of conserving vegetated wetlands and targeting restoration.

title: Plankton ecological complexity amplifies climate-driven weakening of the ocean biological pump
source: Earth and environmental sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The ocean biological pump regulates atmospheric carbon dioxide, yet Earth system projections may miss how plankton food-web complexity shapes its response to warming. Here we use a single Earth system model framework with three progressively more complex plankton ecosystems to show that ecological complexity amplifies the climate-driven weakening of future carbon export. Across historical and future emission scenarios, warming and stratification cause only modest changes in global net primary production but persistent declines in net community production and export fluxes. This weakening increases systematically with ecosystem complexity across scenarios. Under SSP5-8.5, late-century global net community production falls by 5.8% in the default configuration, compared with 8.8% and 12.8% in the more complex configurations. The amplification arises from climate-driven shifts towards smaller phytoplankton and stronger zooplankton grazing, retaining more fixed carbon in the upper ocean. Coarse plankton representations may therefore underestimate future biological-pump weakening and climate-carbon feedbacks.

title: Coupling Iodine Regulation With Hole‐Selective Interfaces for Efficient and Stable Perovskite Solar Cells
abstract: ABSTRACT Operational instability remains a major barrier to the practical application of perovskite solar cells (PSCs), where the formation and volatilization of molecular iodine (I 2 ) cause irreversible degradation of both the perovskite and adjacent hole‐transport layer (HTL). Existing iodine‐trapping or reducing agents can mitigate this degradation, but often compromise interfacial charge transport. Here, we develop two amidinium‐based interfacial modifiers, PTZ‐PEFAI and PXZ‐PEFAI, that combine iodine regulation, favorable energy‐level alignment, and defect passivation. Density functional theory calculations and experiments show that the S/O sites of phenothiazine (PTZ) and phenoxazine (PXZ) interact with I 2 through halogen bonding, enabling I 2 capture and dissociation. The direct identification of I 3 − in modifier‐iodine cocrystals further supports the regeneration of iodide ions. At the perovskite surface, these interactions suppress iodine loss, replenish iodide, and promote healing of iodine‐vacancy defects. Meanwhile, the p‐type PTZ/PXZ functionalities improve energy‐level alignment and facilitate hole extraction at the perovskite/HTL interface. Consequently, PTZ‐PEFAI‐treated n–i–p PSCs achieve a power conversion efficiency of 26.34% and a T 85 lifetime exceeding 1500 h under maximum‐power‐point tracking at 65°C. This work provides a molecular design strategy for simultaneously regulating interfacial iodine chemistry and charge transport toward efficient and stable PSCs.

title: [8+4]‐Connected Ether‐Oxygen‐Based 3D COF Redox Mediators for Durable Light‐Assisted Indirect Electrocatalysis
abstract: ABSTRACT Ether‐oxygen is a type of functional group with high chemical stability, electronic modulation capability, and imparted molecular flexibility, yet incorporating ether‐oxygen groups into high‐connectivity covalent organic frameworks (COFs) to explore their extended applications remains a challenge. Herein, we have designed a series of [8+4]‐connected 3D COFs with scu topology, named TADM–TAPP–COF(M) (M = Ni, Mn, and Cu), by introducing eight‐connected ether‐oxygen based building blocks and metalloporphyrin nodes, which can be applied in high‐stability light‐assisted indirect electrocatalysis. These 3D COFs exhibit good crystallinity, nanosheet morphology, flexible 3D pore structure, abundant ether‐oxygen groups and active metal sites, and excellent electrolyte affinity, which can act as efficient redox mediators. Impressively, the Ni‐incorporated structure TADM–TAPP–COF (Ni) demonstrates high yield in the condensation cyclization reaction of aromatic aldehydes and 2‐aminobenzenethiol to produce 2‐phenylbenzothiazole (yields up to 96%), coupled with the simultaneous production of gas‐phase H 2 product (∼1.15 mmol g −1 h −1 ). Notably, it also shows remarkable stability (continuous reaction for 300 h), high recyclability (8 cycles), and scale‐up production ability (about 2 g in a 12 h batch experiment) and wide substrate applicability, providing a valuable example for the structural design of catalysts toward light‐assisted indirect electrocatalysis.

title: Dual‐Force Strategy for Universal Clusteroluminescence in Non‐Conjugated Small Molecules
abstract: ABSTRACT Non‐traditional luminophores (NTLs) without extended π‐conjugation are attractive for bio‐applications, yet an effective strategy to impart bright emission to non‐luminescent small molecules remains challenging. In this work, we report a modular strategy based on the diethylenetriamine (DETA)‐induced universal luminescence (DIUL) effect, which converts simple non‐conjugated precursors into highly emissive cluster‐based small molecules via synergistic dual‐force: ionic (─BF 4 − /─NH 2 + ) and hydrogen‐bonding (─NH─/─NH 2 ) interactions. The resulting seven derivatives exhibit >70% photoluminescence quantum yield (PLQY) in water, with emission independent of ring/chain structure, demonstrating a robust dual‐force mechanism that advances beyond hydrogen‐bond‐dominated aggregation‐induced emission (AIE) models. These probes show excellent water solubility, low cytotoxicity, and efficient cellular uptake, enabling high‐contrast dual‐color cellular and deep 3D tumor spheroid imaging, along with long‐term biocompatible zebrafish imaging. This work establishes a versatile modular functionalization platform for bright NTLs, offering fundamental insights into cooperative non‐covalent interactions and opening new avenues for designing multifunctional optical materials in bioimaging, sensing, and encryption.

title: Interfacial Molecular Engineering Mediated Intramolecular Inter‐Group Relay Effect Enables Efficient Acidic CO 2 ‐to‐C 2+ Conversion
abstract: ABSTRACT Electrochemical CO 2 reduction reaction (CO 2 RR) in acidic media represents an attractive strategy for improving carbon utilization efficiency by suppressing carbonate formation. However, achieving highly selective C 2+ products at high current densities remains a formidable challenge due to the competing hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) and sluggish C─C coupling process. Here, we introduce the surface‐adsorbed bifunctional organic molecule on Cu (Cu─SBMA), which delivers a Faradaic efficiency of 90.4% for C 2+ products at 0.8 A cm −2 under acid media and pure CO 2 flow, together with a single‐pass carbon efficiency (SPCE) of 92.8% at 0.6 A cm −2 . Furthermore, under diluted CO 2 flow (15 vol% CO 2 ), Cu─SBMA still maintains a high C 2+ Faradaic efficiency of 85.3% at 0.4 A cm −2 . Operando spectroscopy and DFT calculations uncover an intramolecular inter‐group relay mechanism that governs asymmetrical OC─CHO coupling toward C 2+ productions. Specifically, the quaternary ammonium (─N + (CH 3 ) 2 ─) group promotes CO 2 activation and stabilizes *CO intermediate, the adjacent sulfonate (SO 3 − ) moiety mediates protonation of *CO toward *CHO. The intramolecular inter‐group relay effect facilitates C─C coupling and suppresses HER. Our findings provide novel insights for the precise design of catalysts to regulate the reaction selectivity of complex multi‐step energy conversion process.

title: Single‐Atom Multi‐Hydrogen Adsorption Enables Ultrafast Charge Transfer for Boosting Photocatalytic H 2 Production
abstract: ABSTRACT Single‐atom cocatalysts with near‐100% atom utilization are widely studied for boosting photocatalytic H 2 evolution, but their mechanistic insights remain largely restricted to idealized mono‐hydrogen adsorption models. Such simplified frameworks fail to capture the complexity of operando reaction environments, where the high coordination unsaturation of single atoms inevitably drives a transition toward multi‐hydrogen adsorption states. Here, we demonstrate that an N‐coordinated Ni single‐atom cocatalyst (Ni SA ‐N) forms a multi‐hydrogen adsorption state during actual photocatalytic H 2 evolution, significantly accelerating ultrafast charge transfer kinetics. Research results demonstrate that the adsorption of multiple hydrogen triggers spontaneous free‐electron delocalization, rendering the Ni center into a unique electron‐deficient (δ + ) feature. This dynamic electronic reconfiguration enhances the interfacial d‐p orbital hybridization between Ni SA and S of CdS, effectively shortening the interfacial Ni–S bond to construct a highly conductive channel that facilitates ultrafast electron transfer from the CdS to Ni SA cocatalyst, as elucidated by femtosecond transient absorption spectroscopy. Consequently, the Ni SA ‐N/CdS system achieves an exceptional H 2 evolution rate of 20.20 mmol h −1 g −1 . This work identifies the multi‐hydrogen adsorption state as a pivotal nexus linking surface chemistry to ultrafast dynamics, providing a conceptual framework for engineering high‐performance catalysts for artificial photosynthesis.

title: The heterogeneous transmission of geopolitical energy shocks: A structural framework
Physical field coupling in hydrogen production: A critical review from single-field to multi-field synergistic mechanisms
abstract: Hydrogen production technologies play a critical role in the global transition toward sustainable energy systems. However, their practical deployment is often constrained by the inherent limitations of catalysis driven by the single physical field, resulting in insufficient hydrogen-production efficiency. While existing reviews have extensively examined individual hydrogen production pathways, a unified framework that systematically bridges single-field fundamentals and multi-field coupling mechanisms with quantitative assessment of field-induced performance enhancement remains lacking. This work systematically reviews the developmental trajectory of hydrogen production technologies from single-physical-field catalysis to multiphysical-field coupling. Firstly, the fundamental principles and latest advances in hydrogen production driven by single physical fields—including photocatalysis, thermocatalysis, electrocatalysis, piezocatalysis, and microwave-assisted catalysis—are summarized, with detailed discussion of their reaction mechanisms and representative catalytic systems. Building upon this foundation, the review further focuses on multiphysical-field coupling strategies aimed at overcoming the above limitations. Coupled-field hydrogen production systems are broadly categorized into external-field-enhanced photocatalysis (including photo-thermal, photo-electrical, photo-magnetic, and photo-acoustic coupling), external-field-enhanced thermocatalysis (including microwave-assisted and plasma-enhanced systems), and external-field-enhanced electrocatalysis (including thermo-electrical, magneto-electrical, electric-field-enhanced, and stress-enhanced systems). The synergistic mechanisms by which auxiliary external fields regulate charge-carrier dynamics, surface reaction energy barriers, and overall hydrogen production intensification are discussed in depth. Notably, the performance enhancement induced by different physical-field coupling strategies is quantitatively assessed relative to the corresponding baseline systems, providing quantitative insight into the strengthening effects of auxiliary physical fields. Finally, the major challenges currently facing multiphysical-field-coupled hydrogen production technologies, as well as their future prospects, are highlighted. This review aims to provide a systematic framework for understanding the evolution of hydrogen-production technologies and the mechanisms of multiphysical-field coupling, while offering guidance for the mechanistic interpretation, quantitative evaluation, practical implementation, and sustainable development of coupled hydrogen-production systems.

title: Data center cooling in the AI era: cross-scale challenges and system-level outlook
abstract: The rapid growth of artificial intelligence (AI) is fundamentally reshaping data center thermal and energy requirements, driven by increasing power densities and heterogeneous workload characteristics. This review provides an integrated cross-scale and temporal perspective that connects AI heat generation with chip-, rack-, and facility-scale thermal management and their interactions with external energy, water, and grid infrastructures. Modern AI workloads, enabled by accelerator-based hardware, can generate highly localized and temporally dynamic heat fluxes, challenging traditional assumptions of uniform and steady-state cooling design. Accordingly, a range of cooling technologies is examined, including air-based systems, liquid cooling approaches, hybrid configurations, and heat-reuse strategies, with emphasis on their performance limits and deployment constraints. The analysis further identifies key cross-cutting barriers to scalability and efficiency, including thermodynamic irreversibility, coupled water–energy–grid dependencies, cross-scale thermal interactions, reliability and maintainability constraints, and technology-specific trade-offs. Building on these observations, future cooling systems are expected to shift toward integrated and adaptive designs that prioritize multi-objective optimization rather than isolated performance improvements. Emerging directions include grid-responsive and water-aware operation, thermal storage-enabled temporal decoupling, co-designed computing and cooling infrastructures, and predictive closed-loop thermal management enabled by digital twins and data-driven control. Collectively, the findings highlight a transition from component-level optimization toward fully integrated system architectures that jointly optimize energy efficiency, resource utilization, operational resilience, and computational performance across spatial and temporal scales.

title: Robotic inspection and maintenance for energy infrastructure: a systematic review and future perspectives
Water-energy-carbon nexus footprint of seawater desalination and transfer for industrial development: a hybrid life cycle -node-flow framework
abstract: Seawater desalination is becoming increasingly important in arid, industrializing regions, but planning assessments often consider the embodied energy of supply chains and the operational energy of water transfer separately. This study presents a hybrid life cycle and node-flow framework that combines embodied energy and carbon emissions with a spatially explicit model of pumping energy based on elevation gain and hydraulic head losses. The framework is applied to Iran's Persian Gulf Seawater Desalination and Transfer (SDT) project, which supplies 138.76 million m 3 of water annually. Two strategies are compared: Water Transfer (WT), which pumps water inland while transporting products to the coast, and Industrial Transfer (IT), which relocates industries to the coast and transports raw materials from inland areas. Rail and truck freight represent the best- and worst-case transport scenarios, respectively. Pumping-energy intensity ranges from 333.2 to 21,462.4 MWh per million m 3 , depending mainly on transfer distance and elevation. Although industrial relocation reduces long-distance pumping-energy by 99.4%, transporting raw materials offsets much of this saving. Under the grid-average electricity scenario, rail transport results in nearly unchanged total energy use (+0.9%) but reduces carbon emissions by 22.7%. With truck transport, energy use and carbon emissions increase by 121.9% and 53.8%, respectively. Under low-carbon electricity, relocation increases carbon emissions with both transport modes. Benefits also vary by industry: relocation reduces energy use at the steel site under both modes and at the pelletizing site by rail, but not at the copper sites, where raw-material requirements are substantially greater than product output. The water footprint changes only slightly (−4.4%). This framework supports integrated assessments of energy and carbon trade-offs in desalination-dependent industrial systems.

title: Spatial patterns of hybrid PV–CSP–TES configurations for green hydrogen production across Algeria
abstract: Existing studies have optimized hybrid PV–CSP plants or mapped suitable locations for solar hydrogen production, but the spatial dependence of the optimal hybrid architecture remains insufficiently resolved. This study develops a national-scale framework that couples GIS–FAHP screening with hourly PV–CSP–TES–electrolyzer simulation and site-specific NSGA-II optimization to determine how the cost-optimal system design changes across Algeria. At each meteorological location, PV capacity, CSP power-block capacity, TES duration, and solar multiple are jointly optimized for a fixed 50 MW electrolyzer, with the final configuration selected as the lowest levelized cost of hydrogen (LCOH) solution satisfying annual demand satisfaction (ADS) ≥ 90%. The resulting architecture varies substantially across the country: optimal PV capacity ranges from 70.03 to 168.86 MW, CSP power-block capacity from 50.00 to 92.98 MW, and solar multiple from 2.35 to 3.40, while annual hydrogen production remains comparatively stable at 7.58–7.65 kt H₂ yr −1 . Unconstrained LCOH ranges from 6.00 to 10.78 € kg −1 H₂ and narrows considerably after GIS-based deployment constraints are imposed. At Hassi R'Mel, the selected architecture combines approximately 100 MW PV, 50 MW CSP, SM = 2.80, and 16 h TES, achieving an LCOH of 6.53 € kg −1 H₂, 90.3% ADS and approximately 7.6 kt H₂ yr −1 . Sensitivity analysis identifies the discount rate and CSP capital cost as the strongest economic influences within the examined parameter ranges. A matched-output comparison shows that PV-only production can achieve lower LCOH when intermittency is acceptable, whereas PV–CSP–TES substantially increases electrolyzer utilization and production continuity. The results demonstrate that site-specific optimization is necessary to capture how economically preferred generation capacities and solar-field sizing adapt to local solar-resource conditions.

title: Data-driven distributionally robust planning of coastal distribution networks and PV-storage-EV stations for low-carbon energy transition
abstract: Coastal distribution networks (DNs) are becoming key infrastructure for the low-carbon energy transition as electric vehicle (EV) charging, photovoltaic (PV) generation, energy storage, and marine renewable procurement are increasingly coupled at the planning stage. Existing planning models, however, usually treat network expansion, PV-storage-EV station (PSES) deployment, low-carbon operation, and coastal asset degradation separately. This paper proposes a data-driven distributionally robust planning framework for coastal DNs and PSESs. The framework jointly optimizes radial network topology and PSES siting while incorporating salt-spray degradation costs, carbon-emission-flow (CEF)-based nodal carbon accounting, and tidal-generation-driven procurement costs. To represent heterogeneous uncertainty, the model combines continuous box uncertainty for load and PV availability with probability ambiguity over EV-charging scenarios generated from historical charging profiles. The resulting two-stage distributionally robust optimization problem is reformulated through exact relaxation of ESS mode binaries and KKT-based decomposition, and is solved by an inexact column-and-constraint generation (i-C&CG) algorithm. Case studies on a realistic 47-node coastal feeder show that salt-spray exposure can alter the selected topology and PSES siting, while the proposed planning scheme improves voltage quality, reduces annualized total cost, and reveals the cost--carbon trade-off of tidal procurement. The tailored i-C&CG algorithm obtains the same optimal design as conventional C&CG with about an order-of-magnitude reduction in solution time.

title: Secure microgrid formation–oriented uncertainty-aware frequency-constrained proactive scheduling in resilient distribution systems
Beyond facility-level metrics: A whole-system energy–water nexus analysis of data centre integration in Great Britain’s net-zero transition
abstract: The rapid proliferation of hyperscale data centres (DCs) presents compounded challenges to Great Britain (GB)’s net-zero energy transition, superimposing large, continuously growing electricity loads on an energy system simultaneously aiming to be net-zero by 2050. However, existing assessments of DC sustainability rely largely on facility-level metrics such as Power Usage Effectiveness (PUE) and Water Usage Effectiveness (WUE), which provide limited insight into indirect water use and the cross-sector effects of DC integration on power-system infrastructure and decarbonisation pathways. Here, we develop a spatially explicit whole-system energy–water nexus optimisation model for 13 GB regions, representing air-cooled, water-cooled, and direct-to-chip (D2C) cooling architectures. The model uses 24-hour resolution within weighted representative days and a rolling-horizon solution approach with a one-period look-ahead, with weather-dependent PUE and WUE derived from regional typical-meteorological-year data. Under the modelled scenarios, 21.7 GW of installed DC IT capacity adds 124–133 TWh/yr of electricity demand to the GB energy system by 2050, and water-cooled configurations consume 297 × 10 9 litres/yr of direct, on-site cooling water, compared with 31 × 10 9 litres/yr for air cooling. DC integration also increases indirect water consumption by 229 -- 255 × 10 9 litres/yr through the additional generation required, almost entirely from nuclear generation. Relative to water cooling, D2C cooling reduces total system water consumption by 322 × 10 9 litres/yr, almost entirely through the elimination of direct water use, while differences between the three configurations in electricity generation ( 6 TWh/yr between D2C and water cooling), indirect water and heat supply lie within the numerical variability of the optimisation. Under hypothetical water-availability constraints, the air-cooled configuration remains feasible down to 70% of its unconstrained regional water consumption, at which system cost rises by 4.7% (from £593 to £621 billion), solar capacity increases by 25 GW, nuclear capacity falls by 11 GW, and DC capacity relocates from NT and SW towards SO, WN, NO and SC. The water-cooled configuration remains feasible only down to 95% availability, because its direct cooling water cannot be reduced without changing the installed DC capacity. In an exploratory analysis, integrating DC waste heat with Direct Air Capture (DAC) installs 59 MtCO 2 /yr of fully utilised DAC capacity by 2050, using 87% of the available waste heat and adding 11 TWh/yr of electricity demand. Relative to the D2C, net CO 2 emissions decrease from − 9 to − 68 MtCO 2 /yr, system cost (excluding the reserve-margin penalty) rises by £4–5 billion, while changes in generation and installed capacity remain within the variability between independent solutions, reflecting that DAC deployment is driven by the carbon price applied to net emissions rather than by the net-zero constraint, which is already met without DAC. These results indicate that the system-level consequences of DC deployment can differ from those inferred from facility-level PUE and WUE metrics alone, highlighting the importance of jointly considering electricity, water, cooling, heating, and negative-emissions interactions in planning future DC infrastructure.

title: A retrieval-augmented generation (RAG)-enhanced framework for knowledge-guided campus-scale building retrofit design
abstract: Urban-scale building envelope optimization is constrained by the computational burden of iterative simulation. This study proposes a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)-enhanced framework that replaces the search phase of conventional optimization: literature-screened envelope solutions are retrieved from a curated corpus and then cross-checked through physics-based EnergyPlus simulation, rather than located through exhaustive parametric search. The corpus comprises 20,247 initially identified publications screened to a core of 338 studies, together with an experimentally characterized database of 502 envelope materials, of which 65 were used in the assemblies evaluated here. A three-stage progressive retrofit strategy — conventional high-performance insulation; vacuum insulation panels, aerogel and phase change materials (PCMs); and optimized PCM hybrid assemblies — was applied to seven reference buildings on Yonsei University's 86-building campus in Seoul, Korea. A systematic literature review established that whole-building field-measured savings are systematically 0.25–0.75× of simulation-only upper bounds, a correction embedded directly in the retrieval thresholds and screening criteria. The seven reference buildings produce a simulated mean building-level EUI reduction of 21.5%, ranging from 9.5% in high window-to-wall-ratio modern buildings to 39.6% in thermally deficient heritage structures, while campus-wide analysis of all 86 buildings yields 15.7% (124.4 to 104.9 kWh/m 2 ·year). EnergyPlus models were not calibrated against sub-metered operational data, so all reported reductions are simulation-based screening estimates. The framework offers a scalable, computationally efficient route to envelope retrofit planning for large institutional portfolios and urban decarbonization programs.

title: A probabilistic region-based model for evaluating the integrated hosting capacity of photovoltaics and electric vehicles in power distribution networks
Comparative analysis of PV allocation rules in heterogeneous energy communities for collective self-consumption
abstract: This paper investigates how photovoltaic (PV) electricity allocation rules shape the technical, economic, and distributional performance of collective self-consumption schemes at both community and individual levels. A unified analytical framework is developed to compare four allocation mechanisms—static, hourly-variable, dynamic, and priority-based—across three community configurations: a prosumer-only community, an expanded community with fixed PV capacity, and an expanded community with PV capacity scaled to demand. The study is based on a real-case study of the CERCA energy community in Spain, using one year of measured hourly consumption, meteorological, and tariff data. Results show that allocation rules significantly influence both technical and economic outcomes. In the reference scenario, self-consumption ( SC ) rises from 0.39 to 0.41 (static, hourly-variable) to 0.45 (dynamic, priority), while IRR increases from 10.0% to 11.7% and payback decreases from 8.1 to 7.2 years. Community expansion with unchanged PV capacity improves local PV utilization, reaching SC values of 0.58–0.59, maximum IRR of 12.7% and payback of 6.7 years. At the individual level, priority allocation achieves the highest returns but the greatest dispersion of benefits (the coefficient of variation ( CV ) of individual SC is in the 20.7%–41.8% range), whereas dynamic allocation delivers comparable performance with a more balanced distribution ( CV of individual SC up to 9.2%). Sensitivity analysis shows that, for fixed PV capacity, profitability is maximized with 13–15 additional consumers, yielding an IRR of up to 13.3%. Overall, allocation rules are crucial in shaping both efficiency and equity in energy communities, with direct implications for policy and market design.

title: Evacuation route optimization for mixed bus fleets nder energy consumption uncertainty prior to typhoon landfall
Elucidation of the Final Step in the Biosynthesis of Bacillithiol Reveals tRNA-Dependent Ligation of Cysteine
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Bacillithiol is a physiologically significant low-molecular-weight thiol that contributes to the maintenance of redox homeostasis in most Gram-positive bacteria. While the biosynthesis of its sugar scaffold (GlcN-Mal) has been established, the final cysteine–transfer reaction remains unresolved. In this study, a chemical synthesis of bacillithiol and the GlcN-Mal intermediate is achieved in order to characterize the cysteine incorporation reaction catalyzed by BshC, which is encoded outside the bacillithiol biosynthetic gene cluster. Our results show that BshC requires cysteinyl-tRNA derived from the translational machinery to mediate amide bond formation with the sugar scaffold. In fact, BshC appears to be the first characterized enzyme that utilizes tRNA for carboxylate activation during amide bond ligation between the cysteinyl-tRNA electrophile and a nucleophilic substrate outside of ribosomal protein synthesis. Further analysis reveals that BshC exhibits selectivity with regard to both the stereochemistry of malate and the aminoacyl-tRNA donor, likely reflecting precise substrate binding and tRNA recognition. Collectively, this study completes the biosynthetic description of bacillithiol and reveals a rare tRNA-dependent amidation reaction in thiol metabolism that underpins bacterial redox homeostasis.

title: Geopolitical exposure in cross-border electricity transmission: Evidence from Baltic desynchronization and interconnection disruptions
Unified regime partitioning and dominant energy-domain identification for heterogeneous energy-coupling systems
Local optimization of CHP plant operation: an adaptively updated digital twin and linear programming
A continental dilemma: Is centralized or decentralized renewable hydrogen cheaper?
abstract: Hydrogen is a strong candidate on the path towards the decarbonization of the transportation, energy, and industry sectors. In addition to being a well-known element, hydrogen is mainly produced from fossil fuels, with the renewable production chain still requiring development. In this context, this work evaluates the technical and economic potential of hydrogen production using solar photovoltaic (PV) energy and electricity purchased from the Brazilian grid, and evaluates two layouts: (i) centralized production of solar PV energy and hydrogen at the same site and (ii) decentralized production of energy and hydrogen powered by the Brazilian interconnected grid (SIN). The use of PV energy is found to decrease the levelized cost of hydrogen ( L C O H ) when compressed, from 14.00 USD / kg to 13.24 USD / kg in the centralized case and to 9.11 USD / kg in the decentralized case. However, a system powered only by P V energy had a cost of 18.23 USD / kg ; this corroborates the fact that the highest verified cost is from the purchase of energy from the grid. From the analysis of the design parameters, increasing the electrolyzer power and the size of the PV field reduces the L C O H , due to the economies of scale of both pieces of equipment. The optimization shows that it is possible to reach an L C O H for compressed hydrogen of 9.89 USD / kg for the centralized system and values of 5.88 USD / kg for the decentralized system.

title: Stochastic assessment of eight emergency electricity supply configurations for urban shelters: Performance limits and the role of vehicle-to-shelter
abstract: Emergency electricity planning for urban shelters requires comparing heterogeneous supply resources under uncertain, time-varying demand. This study assesses eight specified emergency electricity-supply configurations, including two Vehicle-to-Shelter (V2S) arrangements, for a 1000-person shelter during a 72-h grid outage. A common framework combines paired Monte Carlo simulation, hourly supply–demand matching, continuous resource-state evolution, and access-conditioned variance decomposition, while retaining configuration-specific constraints on power, usable energy, infrastructure continuity, resource access, and deployment timing. Across nine demand and disaster-severity scenarios, adequacy declined as shelter services expanded and cold-season demand increased, while access-dependent resources were additionally constrained by infrastructure continuity, allocation, and arrival. High coverage of the specified diesel-generator configuration depended strongly on its usable energy in the most demanding scenario, where a 20% stock reduction lowered mean energy coverage ratio (ECR) from 0.819 to 0.659. Similar aggregate coverage also concealed different temporal risks. Under hot conditions with moderate disaster severity, a mobile power-supply truck and a local-plus-external V2S arrangement had nearly identical mean ECRs (0.368 and 0.367) under baseline access assumptions but different temporal shortfall patterns. The truck provided no support before allocation and arrival, whereas locally parked EVs supplied limited early power. Access-state differences accounted for most observed ECR variance for the access-dependent configurations in the two examined scenarios, distinguishing conditional resource capability from unconditional shelter adequacy. These findings support mechanism-based screening by power, endurance, immediate availability, and credible access arrangements, while suggesting a potential role for V2S as a conditional supplement rather than a universal substitute for dedicated backup supply.

title: Operating-point-dependent power-flow linearisation for joint siting, sizing, and dispatch of long-duration energy storage in distribution grids
abstract: Long-term energy-storage planning in distribution grids involves long time series, non-linear network constraints, and mixed-integer siting and sizing decisions. Especially detailed AC formulations are computationally challenging for long optimisation horizons. To address this challenge, we propose an operating-point-dependent linearisation of the AC power-flow equations using sensitivity coefficients and integrating them into a mixed-integer linear program for the joint siting, sizing and dispatch of different flexibility options over long time horizons. An iterative AC power-flow validation and relinearisation procedure is used to ensure approximation accuracy. Different approaches to select the linearisation points are benchmarked, either by using each operating point or by clustering approaches, using k -medoids while retaining the original injection and network data. The method is evaluated on SimBench distribution networks and benchmarked against non-linear AC-OPF formulations. Operating-point-dependent linearisation enables computationally tractable storage planning over long time horizons while preserving detailed network information. Clustering can reduce computational effort by about 40 % , provided that the original operating-point data are retained. The linearised model deviates from the lossless AC-OPF benchmark by approximately 0.3 % in storage power and 0.6 % in energy capacity. To demonstrate the use of the method, we develop a case study where household flexibility and grid scale storage are co-optimised in a full-year planning problem. The results show that aggregate household flexibility primarily affects storage sizing, whereas its spatial distribution influences local grid conditions and optimal siting.

title: Hydroxamate Reticular Chemistry beyond Metals: Single-Crystalline Two- and Three-Dimensional Boron–Hydroxamate Covalent Organic Frameworks
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Hydroxamate chelation has already enabled robust metal–organic frameworks. Here, to move the corresponding reticular chemistry beyond metal nodes, hydroxamate chelation has been integrated within heteroleptic tetracoordinate B(O,O)(N)(C) centers to construct four single-crystalline boron–hydroxamate covalent organic frameworks, namely SUM-306–SUM-309. Bayesian optimization enabled the growth of diffraction-quality SUM-306 single crystals, while linker isomerism and functionalization yielded a series spanning two-dimensional hcb and three-dimensional pcu-h frameworks. Structural comparison reveals extended anti-B–phenylene–B arrangements in SUM-306 and SUM-307 and folded syn arrangements in SUM-308 and SUM-309, associated with their respective two- and three-dimensional propagation. Solid-state NMR spectroscopy, B K-edge XANES, and electronic-structure calculations support tetracoordinate boron formation and differentiated yet substantial bonding throughout the B(O,O)(N)(C) environment. As a representative of the series, SUM-308 retains accessible microporosity, exhibits a BET surface area of 1279.9 m2 g–1, and preferentially adsorbs and dynamically separates CO2 from N2. These results extend hydroxamate reticular chemistry beyond metals and establish a mixed-linkage strategy combining chelation, donor–acceptor coordination, and covalent anchoring for single-crystalline boron-based framework construction.

title: Advances in sorption-based thermochemical energy storage: from material properties to prototype-level performance
Cascade Synthesis of Alternating Thiolactone–Episulfide Copolymers via Multi-Site Single-Unit Monomer Insertion
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Alternating copolymers are fundamental sequence-controlled polymers, but their synthesis from two independently polymerizable monomers remains challenging because conventional methods rely on selective cross-propagation, limiting monomer combinations and structural diversity. Here, we report a two-step cascade strategy that decouples sequence control from direct alternating copolymerization. We target thiolactones and episulfides, important sulfur-containing heterocycles accessible from biobased or low-cost feedstocks. However, competing homopolymerization pathways in many thiolactone–episulfide combinations complicate their direct alternating copolymerization. In our approach, controlled thiolactone ring-opening polymerization affords well-defined polythioesters, followed by selective episulfide single-unit monomer insertion (SUMI) at every thioester linkage to yield perfectly alternating poly(thioether-thioester)s. This transformation is enabled by S-aryl thioester-mediated SUMI, wherein facile aryl thiolate departure promotes efficient single insertion while suppressing further propagation.
