Using inexpensive quaternary onium salts without stringent stoichiometric or reaction-time control, the method furnishes 23 new sulfur-rich alternating copolymers with molecular weights up to 157.1 kDa, tensile strengths up to 75.2 MPa, and Young’s moduli up to 2.24 GPa. This cascade route expands the accessible sequence-defined polymer space and creates new opportunities to tailor their properties and functions.

title: Cd Vacancy‐Mediated Orbital Hybridization and Ultrafast Charge Separation in Pt Single‐Atom Photocatalysts
abstract: ABSTRACT Zn x Cd 1−x S (ZCS) solid solutions are promising photocatalysts for H 2 evolution but suffer from rapid electron‐hole recombination. Density functional theory (DFT) predicts that Cd vacancies narrow the band gap and reduce the hole effective mass from 0.80 to 0.59 m 0 , suppressing bulk recombination. Guided by this, Cd vacancies (V C ) were introduced into ZCS as anchoring sites for Pt single atoms (Pt SA ), forming Pt SA /V C ‐ZCS. Aberration‑corrected high‐angle annular dark‐field scanning transmission electron microscopy and X‑ray absorption fine structure confirm atomic Pt dispersion. Femtosecond transient absorption spectroscopy shows Cd vacancies localize photogenerated holes at defect states while Pt single atoms dominate ultrafast electron extraction (ca. 4.10 ps, 81.5% pre‐exponential weight). This vacancy‐mediated synergy switches the dominant carrier pathway from intrinsic interband recombination to spatial charge separation. DFT further shows that p–d hybridization optimizes hydrogen adsorption free energy to −0.11 eV and delocalizes electrons at adjacent sulfur sites. The optimal Pt SA /V C ‐ZCS achieves a H 2 evolution rate of 142.86 mmol g −1 h −1 under visible light, 16.8 times that of pristine ZCS, with an apparent quantum yield of 7.48% at 420 nm and >90% activity retention after cycling. This work reveals how cation vacancies and single atoms enhance charge separation and surface kinetics, guiding atomically dispersed photocatalyst design.

title: Optimal integration of Power-to-Vehicle and Power-to-Heat systems to support renewable deployment in smart urban energy districts
abstract: Decarbonising smart urban energy districts through distributed renewable generation requires planning frameworks able to capture sector-coupling flexibility, while accounting for the multidimensional trade-offs among technical, economic and environmental objectives. This study aims to address the complexity of energy district planning by applying a multi-objective optimisation framework to assess how Power-to-Heat and Power-to-Vehicle strategies can jointly enhance renewable integration. A residential district is modelled in EnergyPLAN comparing a reference configuration based on electricity grid and gas boilers with electrified scenarios including heating, cooling and transport demand under five electric vehicle penetration levels. For each scenario, photovoltaic, small-scale wind, electric batteries, and thermal storage capacities are optimised by minimising annual costs, critical excess electricity production, and CO 2 emissions. Results show that increasing electric vehicle penetration reduces emissions and annual costs, while lowering stationary battery requirements through smart charging flexibility. Beyond a certain level of on-site renewable deployment, further decarbonisation depends primarily on the combined electrification of mobility and domestic end-uses, rather than on additional renewable capacity alone. At intermediate electrification levels, thermal storage supports a solar-dominated mix, whereas higher electric vehicle penetration favours a more balanced renewable mix with reduced storage needs. The fully electrified configuration decreases primary fossil energy consumption, achieving 90% CO 2 abatement and reduces annual costs by about 7% compared with the reference case, while reaching 67% self-sufficiency and 79% self-consumption. The findings demonstrate that exploiting heat pumps and electric vehicles for system flexibility can enhance renewable integration and limit local excess electricity production.

title: From “KGeP” to the Protonated P4-like Anion (HGe3P)2– and the Endohedral Zintl Cluster [Mn@Ge10P2]3–
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract P4-like Zintl anions (Tt2Pn2)2–, which combine the properties of the formally underlying homoatomic units, Tt44– or Pn4 (Tt = tetrel, group 14 element; Pn = pnictogen, group 15 element), are versatile starting materials for ternary clusters. However, not all of the theoretically possible Tt/Pn elemental combinations are accessible, and not all of them show decent reactivity. A particularly challenging elemental combination is that of Ge and P, in contrast to homoatomic P4 or Gen4– (n = 4, 9) that are widely used for corresponding reactions. The only report on a trinuclear complex, [Cd3(Ge3P)3]3–, obtained by reacting a “(Ge2P2)2–” anion, raised questions about the assumed 2:2 ratio of the atoms in the starting material. Herein, we aimed at clarifying the mystery about the composition and identifying a means of accessing new M/Ge/P-based cluster architectures. Regarding the first, we disclosed that the anion is actually not a 2:2 unit, but the first protonated version of a binary P4-like Zintl anion, (HGe3P)2–, which finally rationalizes the composition of the previously reported trinuclear complex. The anion was obtained as its [K(crypt-222)]+ salt by the extraction of “KGeP” with ethane-1,2-diamine (en), acting as a Brønsted acid toward the Zintl anion. 1H NMR spectroscopy and computations of NMR chemical shifts confirmed the presence of the protonated anion in the salt and in solution. As (HGe3P)2– did not show the desired reactivity, we used the more reductive extraction solution of “KGeP” in situ for a follow-up reaction with [Mn(Cp*)2], yielding the first Ge/P-based endohedral Zintl cluster, [Mn@Ge10P2]3–.

title: Continual reinforcement learning for adaptive ship energy efficiency optimization: A LoRA-enabled low-parameter incremental framework
Electrothermal Coupling Strategy Enables Catalytic Unsaturated Acid Production through Highly Selective Oxidation on Modified Heteropolyacids
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract High-value unsaturated acid production from thermally catalytic oxidation of unsaturated aldehydes still faces difficulty in controlling undesired deep oxidation on metal oxide composites or simple P–Mo–V heteropolyacids. Herein, we propose an effective electrothermal coupling strategy by combining a mild electric field with the traditional fixed-bed reactor, without an elaborate catalyst design, to improve selective oxidation. Using the methacrolein oxidation to methacrylic acid on a Keggin-type pyridine-modified P–Mo–V heteropolyacid in steam as a probe, the catalytic rate (0.62 mmol·gCat–1·h–1) and selectivity (95.7%) are, respectively, promoted by ∼25% and ∼15% under an electric field (0.2 W), exceeding comparable literature benchmarks. Mechanistic studies reveal the favorable influence of the applied electric field on the surface adsorption/desorption and diffusion kinetics, catalyst structure and properties, interfacial H2O structure (competitive adsorption with aldehydes/acids), and activation barrier. Additionally, techno-economic analyses reveal that the operation cost, energy consumption, and carbon emission are reduced by ∼22%, ∼21%, and ∼95%, respectively, while the profit is increased by ∼31%, compared with conventional thermal catalysis. This strategy also shows generality across diverse heteropolyacid catalysts and substrates, offering a feasible avenue to improve oxidation selectivity.

title: From accelerated aging to standard cycling: timescale-aligned state-of-health trajectory prediction for lithium-ion batteries
Strategic autonomy and the energy transition: Rethinking Europe's geopolitical alignment
abstract: Europe's geopolitical alignment, its enduring deference to a US-led unipolar order, has come at the expense of its energy security and its ability to carry out the energy transition. This paper argues that greater strategic autonomy, the capacity and willingness to make economic and foreign policy decisions according to its own interests, would allow Europe to pursue both goals more effectively. It develops this argument in four parts. First, it characterises Europe's geopolitical alignment as a pattern of deference to US strategic priorities, sustained despite mounting costs to Europe's material interests, its standing and the multilateral order it claims to uphold. Second, it traces how this alignment shaped Europe's response to Russia's invasion of Ukraine, contributing to a partly self-inflicted energy crisis followed by an abrupt and costly pivot to American liquefied natural gas that failed to resolve Europe's energy dependency. Third, it argues that on the energy transition Europe's interests are more closely aligned with Beijing's than with Washington's, although closer engagement deepens its dependence on Chinese clean technologies and critical raw materials. Europe should manage this trade-off by maintaining its de-risking approach and extending it to all its strategic dependencies, including those on the US. Finally, it argues that Europe will be unable to recalibrate its alignment and exercise strategic autonomy without building up its industrial and technological capacities and increasing its investment. Europe's choices will help determine the pace of the global energy transition, and with it, the world's chances of meeting its climate goals.

title: Geopolitical sequencing in Europe's energy transition: infrastructure, legitimacy and finance
abstract: Europe's energy transition is increasingly shaped by geopolitical competition, strategic dependence and investment uncertainty. This conceptual paper develops the concept of geopolitical sequencing to explain how geopolitical pressures interact with strategic infrastructure, political legitimacy and transition finance. The central argument is temporal: political commitments, infrastructure development and financing arrangements evolve at different speeds, generating misalignment between strategic ambitions and implementation capacity. Institutional risk compression is introduced as the governance mechanism through which socio-political durability, regulatory credibility and financial arrangements interact to contain or amplify uncertainty. The framework is explored through a case study of Sicily, a strategic Mediterranean energy node connecting North African gas corridors, renewable development, grid interconnections and prospective EU–Africa energy partnerships. Evidence on infrastructure investment, renewable permitting and cross-border financing illustrates how geopolitical priorities interact with territorial distributional tensions, regulatory constraints and investment conditions. The analysis highlights three interconnected challenges: aligning commitments across different time horizons, reconciling system-wide infrastructure benefits with local legitimacy and distinguishing genuine risk reduction from the redistribution of financial exposure. The paper contributes a framework for understanding how geopolitical pressures are transmitted through regional energy transitions and identifies implications for EU energy security, infrastructure governance and transition finance.

title: Al/F Co‐Doped Sulfide Electrolyte for Durable All‐Solid‐State Lithium‐Organic Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Carbonyl‐containing organic cathodes offer a sustainable route to high‐energy storage, but their reaction with conventional sulfide electrolytes (SEs) causes interfacial degradation in all‐solid‐state lithium‐metal batteries (ASSLMBs). Here we develop an electrolyte‐first strategy that stabilizes both carbonyl cathodes and lithium metal through dual‐site Al/F substitution of an argyrodite SE, Li 5.7 Al 0.1 P 0.9 S 4.5 Cl 1.2 F 0.3 (LPSC‐AF). Hard‐soft acid‐base theory (HSAB) guided local‐bonding reconstruction increases the basicity and hard‐base character of SE ligands, strengthens P‐S coordination and passivates reactive P‐centered sites. Consequently, the 1,2,5,6‐anthracenetetrone (ATO) adsorption energy decreases from −4.41 to −0.15 eV, suppressing interfacial acid‐base coordination, nucleophilic attack and coupled redox reactions. LPSC‐AF retains an ionic conductivity of 3.8 mS cm −1 and supports stable lithium plating/stripping for over 3000 h. ATO‐based ASSLMBs deliver 358.3 mAh g −1 with 100% initial Coulombic efficiency and retain 81% capacity after 2000 cycles at 5 C and 60°C. The approach is also applicable to C4Q cathodes, establishing HSAB‐guided SEs redesign as a route to stable all‐solid‐state lithium‐organic batteries.

title: Cu Aerogel Doped with Dual-Functional AgNi Sites Enables Selective CO2 Electroreduction to Ethanol via Boosted *CO and *OH Generation
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Selective electrocatalytic CO2-to-C2H5OH conversion remains challenging, due to intricate multielectron transfer, complex C–C coupling, and Cu-based catalysts inherently favoring C2H4 over C2H5OH for lack of *OH-generating sites. Herein, we propose a bifunctional dual-doping strategy that simultaneously stabilizes *CO intermediates and facilitates *OH generation to regulate bond cleavage toward selective C2H5OH. As a prototype, Cu metal aerogel doped with Ag and Ni atoms is designed, in which Ag sites facilitate *CO formation with enhance *CO adsorption strength, while Ni sites boost *OH generation through water dissociation. Their synergy shifts *CHCOH bond cleavage preference from C–O to Cu–C bonds, thus switching the dominant C2 product from C2H4 to C2H5OH, confirmed by in situ infrared spectroscopy and in situ Raman spectroscopy. Thus, AgNi dual-doped Cu aerogel achieves a C2H5OH Faraday efficiency of 47.4%, with C2H5OH/C2H4 ratio of 3.1, outperforming most state-of-the-art Cu-based catalysts under constant current density. This work provides critical insights for designing high-performance Cu-based aerogel catalysts with precisely regulated bond cleavage, advancing practical CO2-to-C2H5OH technology.

title: Ligand Curvature Controls the Size of Self-Assembled Twisted Metallacycles
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Coordination-driven self-assembly often yields dynamic libraries of metallacycles whose size distribution is difficult to control, and ligand-design strategies for directing such equilibria have so far been limited to discrete changes in coordination angles. Here we introduce the first twisted metallacycles, in which ligand curvature is tuned through the tether-to-twist approach. Two twistacene dipyridyl ligands with only a 6° difference in the overall bend: the nearly planar Pl (14° twist) and the twisted Tw (34° twist) assemble with (dppp)Pd(II) and (dppp)Pt(II) corners {M} into dynamic equilibria between rhomboidal {M}2L2 and hexagonal {M}3L3 metallacycles. NMR, nanoESI-MS and X-ray crystallography show that racemic ligands self-sort with high fidelity: socially, into heterochiral meso {M}2L2 rhomboids, and narcissistically, into homochiral {M}3L3 hexagons. Van ‘t Hoff analysis shows ring expansion to be endothermic and entropy-driven throughout, with an enthalpic cost rising from 6–10 kJ mol–1 for Pl to 17–18 kJ mol–1 for Tw. This is explained by increased strain energy for mismatched planar ligands in {M}2L2 assemblies. A few degrees of backbone curvature therefore reshape the free-energy landscape of coordination-driven self-assembly.

title: Photoaffinity Capture of Unit-Resolved Ubiquitin–Decoder Contacts Underlying Topology-Selective Recognition of Heterotypic Chains
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Heterotypic K63/K48 polyubiquitin chains encode diverse cellular outcomes, ranging from proteasomal degradation to nonproteolytic signaling. Although chain topology is increasingly recognized as a critical determinant of these functions, how architectures composed of the same linkage types are decoded into distinct outputs remains poorly understood. This gap has persisted because molecular technologies capable of both chemically capturing topology-selective decoders and defining the unit-resolved contacts underlying selective recognition remain undeveloped. Here we report diazirine-functionalized K63/K48 triubiquitin probes that resolve the unit-specific ubiquitin–decoder contacts essential for topology-selective decoding of the K63/K48 chains with distinct branch architectures. Site-specific installation of a single diazirine moiety into defined ubiquitin units enabled systematic interrogation of the contributions of individual ubiquitin units to topology-selective recognition by quantifying their engagement with decoders through photo-cross-linking efficiency. Specifically, the mixed K63/K48 tribuiquitin (Ub3) probes with diazirine on the K63-linked segment captured a previously unrecognized preference of OTUB1 and RAD23B for mixed K63/K48 chains through more efficient photo-cross-linking than the corresponding branched K63/K48 Ub3 probes. In addition, liquid chromatography–tandem mass spectrometry (LC–MS/MS) analysis of the cross-linked products identified auxiliary contacts of the K63-linked segment in mixed K63/K48 Ub3 as the molecular basis for the topology-selective recognition by OTUB1 and RAD23B. Thus, these chemically defined photoaffinity K63/K48 chains provide a versatile platform for dissecting the molecular logic by which heterotypic ubiquitin-chain topologies are decoded into distinct intracellular outputs.

title: Geopolitical risk and energy transition in the European Union: Can institutional quality mitigate geopolitical shocks?
Water-Soluble Pd12 Multicomponent Cage Enables Selective Separation of 1,4-Dibromonaphthalene from 1,5-Dibromonaphthalene and Regioselective Bromination of Naphthalene
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The synthesis of intricate supramolecular architectures is driven by the desire to translate structural complexity into functional specificity. Herein, we report the formation of an unusual M12L4L′4 cage (MCC) with double-walled knotted architecture via multicomponent self-assembly of a tripyridyl ligand (L), a tricarboxylate ligand (L′), and a cis-Pd(II) acceptor (M). The structure of the MCC resembles a truncated tetrahedron with two overlaid walls enclosing a distorted cavity. The cavity selectively encapsulates polyaromatic hydrocarbons with two fused rings like naphthalene (G1) and its derivatives [1,4-dibromonaphthalene (G5) and 1,5-dibromonaphthalene (G6)], while it is repellent to larger guests in aqueous media. Interestingly, it shows high selectivity for 1,4-dibromonaphthalene (G5), which enabled the purification of 1,4-dibromonaphthalene and 1,5-dibromonaphthalene (G6) from their mixture in aqueous media. Furthermore, selective bromination of naphthalene to 1,4-dibromonaphthalene could be achieved within the hydrophobic cavity of MCC in aqueous media under ambient reaction conditions driven by the high specificity of the cavity for G5, while the same bromination in the absence of the cage yields a mixture of dibromo and monobromo derivatives. Thus, the newly designed cage (MCC) could be utilized for developing an efficient strategy for the regioselective bromination of naphthalene, overcoming the challenges associated with separating the product mixture generated in conventional bromination. Moreover, the cage enables efficient separation of the dibromo isomers of naphthalene formed in conventional synthesis.

title: Dopant-Free Octahedral-Distorted Spinel Cobalt Oxide for High-Performance Proton Exchange Membrane Water Electrolysis
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Developing efficient and stable transition-metal catalysts for acidic water oxidation requires the exploration of multiple structural regulation factors. Although foreign-element doping and morphological engineering have been widely employed, they often complicate the catalyst structure and obscure the origin of activity. Here, we demonstrate that octahedral cobalt–oxygen–octahedral cobalt bond-angle distortion is a key structural parameter correlated with the intrinsic OER activity of spinel cobalt oxides. Through in situ X-ray spectroscopic and imaging techniques, we identify that this long-overlooked Co-octahedra-distortion-induced structural regulation can effectively modulate Co-3d electronic structures and Co–O hybridization. This optimization weakens the adsorption of key oxygen intermediates and increases the propensity toward the oxide path mechanism. The resulting undoped cobalt oxide exhibits high activity in the acidic oxygen evolution reaction, achieving 2.31 V at 3 A cm–2 in a proton exchange membrane electrolyzer. This discovery provides a new perspective to reevaluate cobalt spinel oxides and establish a novel structure–activity relationship between bond angle distortion and performance.

title: A Cryptic Cytochrome P450 Radical Cyclase Catalyzes Naphthalene-Ring Closure in Rifamycin Biosynthesis
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The enzymatic assembly of the 8-hydroxynaphthalene chromophore in rifamycins presents a classic biosynthetic paradox: the off-PKS precursor, prorifamycin A (1a), readily suffers nonenzymatic deoxygenative collapse in solution into the aberrant product 8-deoxynaphthoquinones. Here, using in cellulo genetic manipulation, stepwise pathway reconstitution, in vitro enzymatic assays, molecular docking, and DFT calculations, we identified Rif-Orf0 to be a cytochrome P450 radical cyclase. Rif-Orf0 converted 1a to the 8-hydroxy-7,8-dihydronaphthalenoid intermediate prorifamycin B (1b) through a low-barrier biradical cyclization, and the RifS/RifT dehydrogenase pair rapidly captured and oxidatively aromatized 1b to 34a-deoxyrifamycin W (2). This Rif-Orf0 and RifS/RifT enzymatic cascade outcompeted the spontaneous deoxygenative shunting that afforded 8-deoxynaphthalene-type rifamycins, thereby enforcing the production of 8-hydroxynaphthalenoid rifamycins. This study expanded the catalytic repertoire of cytochrome P450 enzymes and resolved a long-standing question in rifamycin biosynthesis by characterizing how tailoring enzymes canalized reactive intermediates from spontaneous reactions toward defined natural product architectures.

title: Exceptionally Strong Helix Induction Translates a Fast Negative Photochromic Response into Rapidly Self-Erasing Structural Color
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Dynamic modulation of structural color in cholesteric liquid crystals requires strong helix induction to achieve visible selective reflection and rapid, reversible modulation of the helical pitch. Although photochemical control of selective reflection is well established, achieving large wavelength shifts at low dopant concentrations with rapid spontaneous recovery remains challenging. Here, we investigate the structural features associated with the exceptionally high helical twisting power (HTP) of a binaphthyl-based chiral dopant. Systematic structural comparisons reveal that mesogenic substitution at the 7,7′-positions and the presence of imidazole units at the 2,2′-positions are associated with strong helix-inducing ability. The resulting dopant exhibits an HTP of 827 μm–1, enabling red, green, and blue selective reflection at concentrations below 0.5 mol %. Combining this high-HTP dopant with a fast negative photochromic binaphthyl-bridged imidazole dimer enables large, reversible shifts in the selective-reflection wavelength under visible-light irradiation. Upon cessation of irradiation, spontaneous thermal recovery of the photochromic dopant restores the helical pitch on a time scale of seconds, resulting in rapid self-erasure of photopatterned structural colors without an additional stimulus. These findings demonstrate how exceptionally strong helix induction can be combined with rapid negative photochromism to achieve dynamically tunable and spontaneously self-erasing structural colors in cholesteric liquid crystals.

title: Tuning the Reversible E – Z Photoisomerization of a Stilbene-like Ligand via Lanthanide Complexation
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The segmental stilbene-like ligand E- DiL1 displays only an irreversible E → Z photoisomerization under UV-light irradiation due to the overlapping of its absorption spectrum with that of its isomer Z-DiL1, which is further hampered by competing prejudicial intra/intermolecular photoreactions. These limitations can be overcome by exploiting the conformational and electronic changes induced upon connecting E-DiL1 to [Y(hfac)3] rare earth cargoes. In the target {E-DiL1[Y(hfac)3]2} adduct, the connection of the electron-withdrawing Y(III) guest extends the aromatic delocalization and shifts the absorption band to the red. This restores a clean E-to-Z isomer switching of the bridging stilbene-like unit upon visible light irradiation at 420 nm or by simple exposition to room light. The steric hindrance induced by the [Y(hfac)3] containers also prevents detrimental competing photoreactions. The electronic decoupling of the two terimine units in the photoisomerized {Z-DiL1[Y(hfac)3]2} adduct gives rise to a blue shift of the ligand-centered 1π* ← 1π transition and the operation of reverse Z-to-E photoisomerization upon selective near-UV excitation at 380 nm. The guest-induced enlargement of the amplitude of specific excitation wavelengths for inducing E-to-Z and Z-to-E photoisomerizations paves the way for selective signaling in biocompatible environments.

title: Learnable delay-stability coupling for energy-information co-optimization in smart grids
N‐Doped Coral Carbon for Synergistic Iodine Anchoring in High‐Capacity and Long‐Life Aqueous Zinc‐Iodine Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Aqueous zinc‐iodine batteries (AZIBs) are promising energy storage candidates owing to their high capacity and environmental friendliness. However, reported cathode materials suffer from low energy density and rapid capacity decay. In this study, a coral‐like N‐doped carbon with in situ grown surface carbon nanotubes (CNC‐CNT) was synthesized as iodine host material through the pyrolysis of bimetallic core‐shell metal‐organic frameworks. This nitrogen‐doped hollow carbon framework with well‐developed micro/mesopores enables both chemical adsorption of C–I species and physical immobilization of iodine, while providing substantial additional electric double‐layer capacitive contributions. The specific capacity reaches 690.00 mAh g −1 at 1 A g −1 , significantly surpassing that of the AC cathode host of 558.00 mAh g −1 . Consequently, the I2@CNC‐CNT cathode delivers stable cycling over 8000 cycles and retains 464.40 mAh g −1 even at 5 A g −1 . The pouch cell delivers an iodine‐normalized capacity of 501.33 mAh g −1 at 0.2 A g −1 , yielding a material‐level energy density of ∼780 Wh kg −1 at 1.55 V including host capacitance. The host‐subtracted iodine‐redox capacity is 422.00 mAh −1 . This study presents a CNC‐CNT‐derived carbon cathode strategy with facile synthesis, which leverages its hierarchical coral‐like architecture to significantly enhance the specific capacity and cycling stability of AZIBs.

title: Tailored Mn Doping Enables Substantially Boosted Fluorescence Emission in 2D Hybrid Perovskite Ferroelectric Scintillator
abstract: ABSTRACT Organic‐inorganic ferroelectric materials, due to their advantages such as spontaneous polarization, controllable electric domains and multi‐physical field coupling effects, are widely applied in fields including sensors, actuators and optoelectronics. However, there are few successful cases that combine ferroelectricity with dopant‐induced efficient luminescence effects in ferroelectric materials. Herein, through delicate Mn 2+ ion doping, we have successfully designed a multifunctional luminescent ferroelectric material, (GABA) 2 CdCl 4 :4%Mn 2+ (GABA = γ‐aminobutyric acid) which retains its excellent ferroelectric properties with a spontaneous polarization of 4.0 µC cm −2 . Meanwhile, its photoluminescence intensity can be systematically modulated by varying the Mn 2+ doping concentration, demonstrating excellent controllability and functional versatility. Notably, Mn 2+ doping induces a distinct bulk orange‐red luminescence at 610 nm, dramatically boosting the quantum yield from 0.11% to 67%. Leveraging such superior bulk luminescence, (GABA) 2 CdCl 4 :4%Mn 2+ delivers a high light yield of 52 170 photons MeV −1 and a low detection limit of 62.3 nGy s −1 , along with good environmental and radiation stability, marking the first Mn 2+ ‐doped organic‐inorganic hybrid perovskite ferroelectric x‐ray scintillator.

title: Molecular Regulation of Excited‐State Dynamics Enables Photochemically Stable Organic Semiconductors
abstract: ABSTRACT Photochemical degradation fundamentally limits the operational stability of organic photovoltaics (OPVs), yet the molecular processes linking excited‐state dynamics to irreversible chemical reactions remain poorly understood. Here, we show that excited‐state vibrational processes represent a previously underexplored molecular degree of freedom governing photochemical stability and can be regulated to suppress degradation. By incorporating melatonin into the donor layer of an OPV device, excited‐state molecular motions are effectively modulated, reducing vibrationally induced structural fluctuations, suppressing radical generation, and mitigating subsequent photochemical degradation under prolonged illumination. Comprehensive characterization reveals that molecular regulation modifies excited‐state relaxation pathways, thereby decreasing the probability of irreversible chemical transformations while preserving efficient charge generation and transport. As a result, D18/L8‐BO based binary device achieves a power conversion efficiency of 21.10% (certified as 20.6%), together with a more than threefold enhancement in T 80 lifetime under continuous illumination. The effectiveness of this strategy is further validated across multiple systems, demonstrating its general applicability. These findings establish a molecular connection between excited‐state vibrational dynamics and photochemical degradation, and identify regulation of excited‐state molecular motions as an effective strategy for simultaneously achieving high efficiency and long‐term stability in OPV devices.

title: Encapsulating Metal–Organic Cluster in Metal–Organic Framework Film for Tandem Amplifying Third‐Order Nonlinear Optics
abstract: ABSTRACT Metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) and metal–organic clusters (MOCs) are promising platforms for third‐order nonlinear optics (NLO) because their inorganic–organic components enable designable structures and tunable photo/electronic properties. However, integrating MOFs and MOCs for tandem third‐order NLO remains unexplored. Here, we combine MOF and MOC for third‐order NLO by encapsulating MOC in a porous MOF film. A [001]‐oriented conductive MOF Ni‐HHTP film (HHTP = 2,3,6,7,10,11‐hexahydroxytriphenylene) is prepared by liquid‐phase heating drop‐coating and shows excellent electro‐regulated third‐order NLO. Furthermore, iron‐based MOC (FeOC) is encapsulated into the ordered nanochannels of Ni‐HHTP film (Ni‐HHTP@FeOC) using an immersion strategy. The results show that the encapsulation of FeOC in the Ni‐HHTP film can enhance charge transfer and improve excited‐state absorption, with the nonlinear absorption coefficient ( β ) increasing from 4.9 × 10 −6 to 9.7 × 10 −6 m/W after loading. An applied electric field further modulates carrier concentration and excited‐state lifetime, enabling dynamic adjustment of the third‐order NLO response; β increased to 19.6 × 10 −6 m/W for Ni‐HHTP@FeOC‐2 V. This work is the first to combine MOF and MOC materials for high third‐order NLO performance and provides a synergistic strategy for regulating third‐order NLO performance through tandem encapsulation and electronic stimulation, offering new design concepts for adaptive optoelectronic devices.

title: A Room‐Temperature Fluorescent‐Free Imidazol‐2‐Ylidene: A Versatile Platform for Fluorophore Diversification
abstract: ABSTRACT N ‐Heterocyclic carbenes (NHCs) have become key ligands in luminescent transition‐metal complexes, yet the intrinsic photophysical properties of free NHCs remain largely unexplored. Herein, we report the synthesis of the first isolable free imidazol‐2‐ylidene exhibiting room‐temperature fluorescence in both solution and solid states, through the incorporation of a tetrahedral boron moiety into the backbone of the emblematic 1,3‐dimesityl‐2 H ‐imidazol‐2‐ylidene (IMes) scaffold. Theoretical calculations reveal direct involvement of the carbene center in the lowest singlet excited state and therefore in the emission process. Exploiting the specific reactivity of the carbene center, conversion into the corresponding borane, urea, thiourea, and selenourea adducts enables systematic modulation of the emission wavelength, quantum yield, and photostability. These combined experimental and theoretical results establish free conventional NHCs as a previously unrecognized class of intrinsically emissive organic molecules and identify carbene molecular engineering as a viable strategy for functional luminophores.

title: One‐Step Conversion of Thermoplastic Elastomers into Ionic Ordered Mesoporous Polymers via Interface‐Directed Chain Scission: A Plastic Upcycling Strategy for Atmospheric Water Harvesting
abstract: ABSTRACT As a cornerstone of the circular materials economy, chemical recycling typically breaks commodity plastics down into small molecular building blocks. While this strategy is reasonable for most plastics, styrenic thermoplastic elastomers (TPEs) can be a notable exception. These materials can intrinsically self‐assemble into ordered nanostructures, yet most upcycling methods discard this morphological asset, leaving TPEs a compelling but underexploited feedstock for high‐value applications. Here, we report a one‐step approach that upcycles TPEs into ionic ordered mesoporous polymers (OMPs) in their solid state, through interface‐directed chain scission. Adding a small amount of radical initiator (dicumyl peroxide) during the sulfonation of polystyrene‐ block ‐poly(ethylene‐ran‐butylene)‐ block ‐polystyrene (SEBS) leverages a diffusion‐controlled reaction front to selectively cleave the minority polystyrene domains, while crosslinking and sulfonating the majority phase. This one‐step process at 145°C installs ionic character and establishing uniform mesoporosity without the high‐temperature calcination (typically > 350°C) that conventionally erodes functional groups. Furthermore, the resulting OMPs act as high‐performance sorbents for atmospheric water harvesting, demonstrating rapid kinetics, solar‐driven regeneration, and excellent cycling stability, while a simple lithium chloride (LiCl) encapsulation step enhances their water uptake capacity to 2.46 g/g.

title: Enantioselective Radical Hydrosilylation of Electron‐Deficient Alkenes Enabled by Metallaphotoredox Catalysis
abstract: ABSTRACT Catalytic enantioselective hydrosilylation of electron‐deficient alkenes remains an outstanding challenge due to difficulties in simultaneously controlling chemo‐, regio‐, and enantioselectivity. Herein, we report a general and practical strategy enabling the first enantioselective radical hydrosilylation of α,β‐unsaturated esters via metallaphotoredox catalysis. This approach integrates photocatalytically generated bromine radical‐facilitated hydrogen atom transfer to convert hydrosilanes into silyl radicals with a chiral nickel catalyst that stabilizes carbon‐centered radical intermediates and directs asymmetric protonation. The method circumvents alkene coordination and migratory insertion steps, and effectively overrides racemic background radical addition. By decoupling Si─C bond formation from the enantioselectivity‐determining step, it accommodates a broad substrate scope. The redox‐neutral, fully atom‐economical protocol proceeds under mild conditions without stoichiometric organometallic reagents or external oxidants/reductants, delivering β‐silylated carbonyl compounds with high chemo‐, regio‐, and enantioselectivity. Furthermore, the strategy extends to enantioselective hydrogermylation and is amenable to gram‐scale synthesis. This work provides a conceptually distinct blueprint for enantioselective hydrosilylation and establishes a mechanistic rationale for controlling enantioselectivity in radical conjugate addition.

title: Steering C–C Coupling via Amorphous Nd 2 O 3 Pinning for Efficient CO 2 Electroreduction to Ethylene
abstract: ABSTRACT Copper‐catalyzed electrochemical CO 2 reduction provides a sustainable route for carbon fixation. However, the undercoordinated Cu active sites that facilitate C–C coupling readily undergo rapid, detrimental structural reconstruction under negative potentials. To tackle this challenge, we introduce amorphous Nd 2 O 3 nanostructures pinned at the Cu 2 O interface to stabilize the undercoordinated Cu sites. Electron microscopy and spectroscopy reveal that this pinning interface not only refines the Cu 2 O grains by approximately half but also stabilizes the high density of defect sites generated during reconstruction. Density functional theory further unveils that the interface thermodynamically redirects the coupling pathway from the energy‐demanding CO–CO dimerization towards the more favorable CO–CHO asymmetric coupling (*CO + *CHO → *COCHO). The desired catalyst achieves a peak C 2 H 4 Faradaic efficiency of 59.5% at 1.1 A cm −2 and a record partial current density of 762.5 mA cm −2 at 1.5 A cm −2 in a flow cell, with stable operation over 30 hours. We showcase a facile yet effective material design strategy that breaks the selectivity‐stability trade‐off of Cu catalysts, paving the way for industrially viable CO 2 ‐to‐C 2 H 4 electrolysis.

title: Constructing Dynamic Interfacial Hydration Network Channel for Efficient Co‑Transport of OH − and H 2 in Water‑Electrolysis Cathodes
abstract: ABSTRACT Efficient mass transport at the electrode–electrolyte interface of anion‐exchange membrane water electrolysis (AEM‐WE) is fundamentally constrained by antagonistic hydration requirements. Drawing inspiration from biological channels that mediate hydrophilic yet non‐retentive transport, we designed a series of covalent organic frameworks (COFs) with tunable sulfone densities as synthetic nanochannels. Combined experimental and theoretical investigations revealed that the sulfone moiety (O═S═O) established weak, labile hydrogen bonds with water, engendering a highly dynamic hydrogen‐bonding network. This unique hydration environment established a surface‐wetting yet bulk‐open state within the COF nanochannels, wherein a dynamic interfacial hydration network channel was maintained within the pores for efficient OH − conduction, while the bulk pore volume remained non‐flooded for unobstructed H 2 evacuation. When incorporated into the cathode catalyst layer, the sulfone‐rich 2S‐COF delivers a current density of 10.30 A cm −2 at 2.0 V under industrially relevant conditions (1 M KOH, 80°C), representing a 48% enhancement over the COF‐free electrode. This work establishes a bio‐inspired strategy for molecular‐level control of interfacial hydration, providing a generalizable platform for designing high‐performance electrochemical interfaces that require concurrent ion and gas management.

title: Terminal Engineering Drives Compact π–π Stacking to Suppress Electron–Phonon Coupling in Narrow‐Bandgap Electron Acceptors
abstract: ABSTRACT Ultranarrow‐bandgap organic semiconductors are attractive for short‐wavelength infrared (SWIR) photodetection, yet their extended spectral response is accompanied by strong electron–phonon coupling and substantial nonradiative energy losses. Herein, we reveal that intermolecular π–π stacking provides an effective molecular handle for regulating electron–phonon coupling in ultranarrow‐bandgap organic semiconductors. A series of ultranarrow‐bandgap acceptors with systematically varied terminal groups are developed, enabling progressive shortening of the π–π stacking distance from 3.74 to 3.53 Å. The resulting compact intermolecular packing strengthens intermolecular interactions and suppresses electron–phonon coupling, thereby reducing vibrational relaxation, prolonging exciton lifetimes, and mitigating nonradiative energy losses. Consequently, the BIP‐M8‐based organic photodetector delivers a responsivity of 0.29 A W −1 and a specific detectivity of 1.84 × 10 12 Jones at 1180 nm, with a detectivity exceeding 10 11 Jones over 400–1300 nm. These results establish intermolecular π–π stacking as a molecular design parameter for controlling vibronic interactions and mitigating nonradiative energy losses in ultranarrow‐bandgap organic semiconductors, offering a general strategy for high‐performance SWIR optoelectronics.

title: Stabilizing High‐Voltage Oxygen Holes via π‐Bonding Mediated Frontier‐Orbital Character Inversion in Intermediate‐Regime Oxide Cathodes
abstract: ABSTRACT Oxygen redox chemistry offers a promising route to higher energy densities in layered oxide cathodes. However, it is commonly plagued by unstable O─O dimerization that leads to voltage hysteresis and capacity loss. While oxygen hole can mitigate these degradation pathways, its lower operating voltage results in reduced energy density. Herein, high‐voltage oxygen‐hole states are stabilized in Li 2 RuO 3 through precisely tailoring the Ru─O π‐bonding interaction. The successful modulation arises from a dynamic evolution of the electronic structure during delithiation, the so‐called frontier‐orbital character inversion, which has been experimentally validated through combined analysis of the elemental contributions to states near the Fermi level. Oxygen oxidation subsequently involves an O 2p‐dominated antibonding state, avoiding the pronounced bond destabilization associated with electron removal from bonding orbitals. Such behavior is attributed to the unique position of ruthenates within the intermediate regime between Mott–Hubbard and charge‐transfer insulators. And this specific electronic state positioning facilitates a dynamic transition toward a stable negative charge‐transfer regime. This boundary‐crossing effect is especially pronounced in high‐valent systems owing to intense covalency modulations upon oxidation. These insights establish a clear electronic‐structure‐based design principle, highlighting the importance of orbital engineering in boundary‐regime systems to achieve stable and high‐voltage anionic redox.

title: Amphiphilic Interface‐Mediated Dual‐Domain Architecture Enhances Phosphatase‐Like Activity for Plastic Additives Assay
abstract: ABSTRACT Plastics are ubiquitous, and their performance depends on phosphate ester additives used as plasticizers and flame retardants. Leaching of these additives causes environmental persistence and biotoxicity, demanding efficient detection. To overcome the polarity mismatch in detecting plastic additives, we developed amphiphilic F127‐modified Pt with Pt‐OH sites (Pt‐OH/F) for colorimetric detection of mixed plastic additives. Pt‐OH/F outperforms alkaline phosphatase and works directly in water, with catalytic efficiency 2–6 orders of magnitude higher than reported nanozymes. The integration of F127 with Pt‐OH sites creates a functionally distinct dual‐domain architecture composed of an amphiphilic enrichment domain and a catalytic domain, thereby overcoming the polarity restriction of natural phosphatases. Within this architecture, the spatial separation of adsorption sites from catalytic sites prevents competitive occupancy and enhances catalytic activity. Finally, the developed nanozymes can achieve simultaneous qualitative and quantitative detection of leached plastic additives in real samples, showing the potential for on‐site analysis of plastic waste.

title: Unraveling Synergistic Substrate–H 2 Activation and Tunable Counteranion Effects in Ru‐Catalyzed Asymmetric Hydrogenation of 2‐Substituted Quinolines: An Integrated Kinetic and DFT Study
abstract: ABSTRACT Although the asymmetric hydrogenation of N ‐heteroarenes has achieved remarkable synthetic advances, the underlying mechanism remains incompletely understood. Herein, we combine kinetic and DFT studies to reveal a novel synergistic substrate–H 2 activation mode in the Ru‐catalyzed asymmetric hydrogenation of quinolines. Both the quinoline substrate and the in situ generated dihydroquinoline intermediate act as sequential proton acceptors, causing a dynamic shift in the rate‐determining step between the first and second H 2 heterolytic cleavage events. This conclusion is strongly supported by Hammett analysis ( ρ = −1.19) and saturation kinetics. Notably, we identify a pronounced and tunable counteranion effect that plays two non‐spectator roles: (i) facilitating active‐site formation via anion dissociation, and (ii) stabilizing the charge‐separated H 2 ‐cleavage transition state through electronic effects, affording up to a 13‐fold rate enhancement. DFT calculations confirm that substrate‐assisted H 2 activation and anion‐assisted direct proton transfer are energetically favorable. This synergistic, anion‐regulated mechanism has also been validated in indole hydrogenation, and offers an improved understanding of the outer‐sphere catalytic hydrogenation manifold that diverges from the traditional concerted H − /H + transfer pathway. This work thus provides a unified theoretical framework for the asymmetric hydrogenation of diverse N ‐heteroarene substrates.

title: Bidirectional Sulfur Redox Regulation Enabling Ultra‐Stable High‐Sulfur‐Loading All‐Solid‐State Lithium‐Sulfur Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT All‐solid‐state lithium‐sulfur batteries are promising for high‐energy storage but are limited by sluggish sulfur redox and poor cycling stability. Herein, we design a new amorphous‐crystalline Li 6.05 P 0.95 Nb 0.05 S 5 Cl 0.8 I 0.2 electrolyte that reconstructs interfacial Li + transport and enables bidirectional regulation of sulfur redox. The amorphous structure improves solid‐solid contact and creates additional continuous Li + pathways around sulfur, while the crystal framework maintains fast Li + ion‐conducting channels. During the discharge, we further uncover an Nb reduction mechanism in which Nb 4+ is reduced to Nb 3+ , generating Li‐rich sites that promote Li 2 S nucleation and sulfur reduction. During the charge, I − is oxidized to I 2 , which acts as the redox mediator for Li 2 S oxidation, while I 3 − formation helps stabilize unconsumed I 2 . This bidirectional regulation enables 84.2% sulfur utilization at a high sulfur loading of 6 mg cm − 2 and retains 736 mAh g − 1 with 93.1% capacity retention after 1500 cycles at 0.5 C. These findings provide a mechanistic strategy for high‐sulfur‐loading all‐solid‐state Li‐S batteries.

title: Coupled Self‐Alkalization and Chelation Chemistry Enables Highly Reversible Zn Anodes and Rechargeable Alkaline Zn–I 2 Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT The practical development of alkaline rechargeable zinc‐based batteries (ARZBs) is fundamentally limited by the intrinsic trade‐off among redox potential, high Zn 2+ concentration, and Zn anode stability. Herein, we report a synergistic “self‐alkalization + chelation chemistry” electrolyte using ethylenediamine (EN) as a multifunctional co‐solvent. Acting simultaneously as an organic base and a Zn 2+ chelating ligand, EN enables in situ OH − generation while forming soluble five‐membered Zn chelates, thereby reconstructing Zn dissolution chemistry in alkaline media. The resulting electrolyte achieves a Zn 2+ concentration of 1 M at pH 12.45, transforming Zn transport from diffusion‐limited to migration‐assisted behavior. Meanwhile, preferential adsorption and in situ decomposition of EN generate an organic–inorganic hybrid interphase that effectively suppresses corrosion and parasitic reactions. As a result, Zn||Zn coin cells exhibit stable Zn plating/stripping for 380 h. Furthermore, EN stabilizes reactive I + intermediates through coordination chemistry, enabling rechargeable alkaline Zn||I 2 batteries with a high energy density of 812.9 Wh kg −1 . More importantly, the exceptionally high Zn 2+ flux and interfacial reversibility enable the first demonstration of anode‐free alkaline Zn||I 2 batteries, which operate stably for 860 cycles. This work establishes a general electrolyte engineering strategy for decoupling the long‐standing electrolyte trilemma in ARZBs and advancing high‐energy aqueous batteries.

title: Catalytic Aziridination With Simple Acyl Azides via Validated Copper‐Acyl Nitrenes
abstract: ABSTRACT Terminal copper‐nitrenes are widely proposed as reactive intermediates in catalytic N‐group transfer, but well‐defined copper‐acyl nitrenes remain largely unexplored. We show that simple aryl acyl azides serve as effective precursors to terminal copper‐acyl nitrenes that catalytically convert styrene into N‐acyl aziridines in yields of up to 76%. Ten copper‐acyl nitrenes were generated, detected, and characterized by spectroscopic, kinetic, and computational methods. The active species exhibits a singlet ground state, as supported by Evans NMR and EPR spectroscopy, and multireference calculations. Mechanistic studies reveal predominantly polar nitrene transfer together with a spin‐crossover event leading to a persistent radical intermediate. The use of readily available acyl azides broadens the scope of copper‐catalyzed aziridination beyond nitrene precursors bearing strongly electron‐withdrawing substituents and identifies copper‐acyl nitrenes as competent and mechanistically distinct nitrene‐transfer agents.

title: Autonomous Scanning Electrochemical Cell Microscopy Enables Rapid Exploration of Large Compositionally Complex Material Spaces
abstract: ABSTRACT Alloying is a central strategy in electrocatalysis, enabling fine‐tuning of the electronic structure. In particular, compositionally complex solid solutions (CCSSs), often called high‐entropy alloys, are of high interest. However, the “combinatorial explosion” in the number of possible compositions poses a critical bottleneck for the discovery of CCSS electrocatalysts. We present an autonomous scanning electrochemical cell microscopy (SECCM) system for ultrahigh‐throughput and large‐scale CCSS activity screening. The platform rapidly establishes composition–activity relationships across multiple thin‐film CCSS materials libraries via active learning and automated library exchange. Embedding analytical expressions of voltammetry in the algorithm enables the learning of whole voltammograms rather than a single selected metric. As a demonstration, we investigated hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) activities of Au–Ir–Rh, where Ir and Rh exhibit strong metal‐hydrogen binding and Au exhibits weak binding as derived from the HER volcano plot. The activity trend was accurately predicted after measuring only 15% of all 966 measurement areas. Au 30 Ir 20 Rh 50 and Au 10 Ir 35 Rh 55 exhibit the highest activities with standard rate constants of ∼0.012 cm s −1 , demonstrating positive synergistic contributions from elemental mixing. The proposed platform is broadly applicable to a wide range of electrocatalytic reactions, providing a general pathway for accelerating CCSS electrocatalyst discovery.

title: Ligand‐Engineered Metal‐Organic‐Covalent‐Organic Frameworks Enable Red‐Light‐Driven H 2 O 2 Photosynthesis and Tunable Biomass Upgrading
abstract: ABSTRACT Harvesting low‐energy photons, particularly in the deep‐red and near‐infrared regions, for artificial photosynthesis remains a significant challenge due to the inherent difficulty in driving multi‐electron redox processes with limited photon energy. Herein, we reported a tunable ligand engineering strategy to construct a series of isostructural metal‐organic‐covalent‐organic frameworks (MOCOFs), namely MOCOF‐phen x ( x = 0, 1, 2 and 3). By gradient increasing the number of phenanthroline ligands around the Ru(II) center, we precisely modulated the electronic structures and excited‐state properties of the resulting MOCOFs. Remarkably, the ligand‐engineered MOCOFs showed excellent red‐light‐driven H 2 O 2 generation coupled with switchable biomass upgrading, in which the reaction selectivity of furfuryl alcohol oxidation was profoundly governed. MOCOF‐phen 0 preferentially affords 6‐hydroxy‐2H‐pyran‐3(6H)‐one (PN) with 91.4% selectivity, whereas MOCOF‐phen 3 steers the reaction towards 5‐hydroxy‐2,5‐dihydrofuran‐2‐one (FN). This work establishes a molecular‐level design blueprint for low‐energy‐light‐driven photocatalysis, demonstrating ligand engineering in crystalline framework materials for optimizing activity and selectivity towards sustainable photosynthesis.

title: Covalent Organic Framework‐Templated Spatial Confinement of Self‐Assembled Monolayers for High‐Performance Perovskite Solar Cells
abstract: ABSTRACT Self‐assembled monolayers (SAMs) have emerged as efficient hole‐contacting layers for p‐i‐n perovskite solar cells (PSCs). However, incomplete SAM coverage and weak bonding with the substrate result in heterogeneous buried interfaces. Herein, a covalent organic framework (COF)‐templated spatial confinement (CTSC) strategy is developed by employing a newly designed phosphonate–carbazole‐based COF, namely COF‐TPACz , to regulate the buried interface. The nanoscale island‐like COF domains could restrict the penetration of aggregated SAM molecules and allow well‐distributed ones to anchor on exposed substrates. Meanwhile, hydrogen‐bonding and π–π interactions between COF‐TPACz and SAM favor a more uniform molecular arrangement on the COF domains. These adjustments synergistically suppress molecular aggregation and improve surface coverage, yielding a denser and more homogeneous SAM interface. Furthermore, the improved interface optimizes upper perovskite crystallization, promotes compact and vertically extended grains, and strengthens buried interfacial contact, thereby suppressing nonradiative recombination and facilitating charge extraction and transport. Consequently, the CTSC‐based PSCs achieve a peak efficiency of 27.03%, together with enhanced long‐term stability. We believe these findings provide a conceptual advance for realizing homogeneous SAM via spatial confinement and a viable route toward efficient and stable PSCs.

title: Selective Oxidation of Toluene to Benzaldehyde Driven by Electroreduction of Oxygen to Hydrogen Peroxide Coupled With In Situ Electro‐Fenton Reaction
abstract: ABSTRACT Selective toluene oxidation is a pivotal reaction in the fine chemical industry. While electrooxidation at high anodic potentials shows promise, the low efficiency of the generation of reactive oxygen species limits the product yield. Herein, we describe a cathodic strategy for selective oxidation of toluene to benzaldehyde via coupling the electrosynthesis of hydrogen peroxide from oxygen reduction with an in situ electro‐Fenton reaction (eH 2 O 2 ‐EF). Among the different metal–nitrogen–carbon single‐atom catalysts (M‐NC SAC, M = Fe, Co, and Ni), Co‐NC SAC stands out as the best catalyst, featuring a benzaldehyde selectivity of 90.63% and a yield of 21.9 mmol h −1 at −0.3 V versus RHE with stable operation over 23 cycles. In situ spectroscopy and radical scavenging and quantification experiments indicate that the eH 2 O 2 ‐EF proceeds via toluene adsorption, ·OH‐mediated oxidation, and desorption of products, where the ·OH generation and intermediate adsorption/desorption jointly determine the benzaldehyde yield. Theoretical analysis indicates that the Co‐NC SAC thermodynamically facilitates H 2 O 2 generation, accompanied by moderate benzaldehyde adsorption and an uphill further‐oxidation step, leading to selective benzaldehyde production. This work establishes a novel cathodic paradigm for the selective oxidation of inert aromatic ‐H bonds under mild conditions.

title: Engineering Synthetic Molecular Operations Controlled by DNA‐Binding Proteins Through Templated Proximity
abstract: ABSTRACT We describe a DNA‐based molecular framework that enables DNA‐binding proteins (DBPs) to perform diverse synthetic operations beyond their natural functions. We introduce templated proximity as a mechanism through which DBP–DNA recognition events are converted into programmable DNA strand displacement reactions. In this architecture, protein binding templates the spatial colocalization of split DNA components, generating functional nucleic acid outputs that can be propagated into downstream processes. Using representative DBPs, including EGR1, YY1, and p53, we couple protein recognition to DNA strand displacement, activation of a fluorogenic RNA aptamer, regulation of CRISPR–Cas12a and Cas13 activity, and DBP‐triggered activation of hierarchical CRISPR cascades. These results establish templated proximity as a general transduction principle for integrating DNA‐binding proteins into modular nucleic acid reaction networks and demonstrate that DBPs can function as programmable interfaces connecting natural biomolecular recognition with engineered DNA‐based information processing, enabling modular communication layers with tailored synthetic functionality.

title: Selective Reductive Amination of Long‐Chain Diols to Primary Diamines Over Nitrogen‐Modulated Ru 0 /Ru δ+ Dual Sites
abstract: ABSTRACT Linear primary diamines (DAs) are essential monomers for nylon and polyamide. Sustainable production of DAs from bio‐diols via reductive amination (RA) requires to achieve the tandem diols dehydrogenation (rate‐determining), aldimine condensation and imine hydrogenation, which remains challenging due to low efficiency, poor selectivity, and rapid catalyst deactivation under ammonia‐rich conditions. In this study, we report an efficient and durable catalytic system for the RA of linear primary bio‐diols to DAs by constructing a Ru n ‐N x ‐C catalyst with N‐modulated Ru 0 /Ru δ+ dual sites. In the RA of 1,9‐nonanediol, a high yield of 1,9‐nonanediamine up to 98.5% is achieved under mild conditions (170°C, 0.3 MPa H 2 , 0.7 MPa NH 3 ) for at least 10 cycles. Mechanistic studies reveal that Ru δ+ and Ru 0 sites cooperatively drive diol dehydrogenation through O─H and Cα─H bond activation, respectively, while their synergistic interplay further promotes the subsequent RA toward DAs formation. DFT and AIMD simulations reveal that N‐modulated Ru δ+ sites exhibit weaker NH 3 adsorption than pristine Ru δ+ surfaces, thereby mitigating the excessive deposition of imine‐derived intermediates and improving catalytic stability. Ru n ‐N x ‐C was further evaluated for the conversion of selected biomass‐ and polyester‐derived substrates into value‐added DAs.

title: Strain‐Inversion Strategy Enables MOCVD Growth of 53 µm Ultra‐Thick, Stress‐Free, Buffer‐Free III‐Nitride Heteroepitaxial Films
abstract: ABSTRACT As the semiconductor industry increasingly pivots toward “More than Moore” and “More Moore” paradigms, heterogeneous integration has emerged as a pivotal strategy for achieving system‐level performance breakthroughs. However, residual stress inherent to the integration of dissimilar materials represents a critical bottleneck, directly threatening the integrity and reliability of these advanced systems. Heteroepitaxy, as a representative example, is inherently constrained by stress accumulation, which limits epilayer thickness, increases threading dislocation density (TDD), and degrades device reliability. Here, we present a strain‐inversion strategy that effectively transfers misfit‐induced stress from the epilayer into the substrate stack. Through co‐designed theoretical modeling and experimental validation, we introduce 4H‐SiC/SiO 2 /polycrystalline‐ceramic‐AlN integrated substrates, and demonstrate metalorganic chemical vapor deposition (MOCVD) growth of 53‐µm‐thick, stress‐free heteroepitaxial GaN films. The films exhibit outstanding structural quality, with full‐width‐at‐half‐maximum (FWHM) values of x‐ray rocking curve of 83 and 119 arcsec for the (002) and (102) planes, respectively, and a TDD of 5 × 10 7 cm −2 . These results not only set a new thickness record for MOCVD‐grown heteroepitaxial GaN but also achieve crystal quality comparable to state‐of‐the‐art benchmarks. Our approach establishes strain‐inverted epitaxy as a highly promising platform for high‐performance nitride devices and paves the way for producing low‐cost and strain‐free GaN and AlN substrates.

title: Safranine T‐Derived Activable Photosensitizer to Synergistically Regulate the RSS/ROS Dynamic Equilibrium for Boosted Photosensitization
abstract: ABSTRACT Photodynamic therapy (PDT) eliminates lesions like tumors via reactive oxygen species (ROS)‐mediated oxidative damage. However, tumors overexpress reactive sulfur species (RSS) that scavenge cytotoxic ROS, endowing cancer cells with strong antioxidant resistance and weakening PDT efficacy. We fabricated a biosafe, readily available activatable photosensitizer ST‐DNBS based on safranine T (ST). ST‐DNBS selectively consumes RSS overexpressed in tumors and recovers photochemically active ST to produce massive ROS. For example, 6 µM ST‑DNBS depletes substantial glutathione (GSH), leading to a marked reduction in the characteristic absorbance of TNB 2− (5‐thio‐2‐nitrobenzoate dianion) at 412 nm in the DTNB (Ellman's reagent) assay relative to the control; ROS produced after 24 s of irradiation causes a 6.2‐fold decrease in the UV absorbance of 1,3‐diphenylisobenzofuran (DPBF). Tumor‐activatable ST‐DNBS depletes intracellular RSS to collapse tumor antioxidant systems, blocking ROS clearance and boosting intracellular ROS buildup. This RSS/ROS redox balance remodeling greatly enhances photodynamic activity, achieving a 90% tumor inhibition rate. Our RSS‐scavenging, tumor‐activated photosensitizer offers a practical strategy to overcome tumor antioxidant barriers and improve PDT antitumor performance.

title: PCET beyond p K a : Disaggregation and Additional Base Effects as Neglected Key Factors for Unlocking Inaccessible Substrates in Direct Intermolecular Photocatalytic Ring‐Opening Remote Alkylation of Cycloalkanols
abstract: ABSTRACT Photocatalytic oxidative multisite proton‐coupled electron transfer (MS‐PCET) reactions have emerged as a promising tool for the activation of strong O─H bonds in (cyclo)alkanols. However, these methods often require the use of e‐rich arene‐containing derivatives ( para ‐methoxyphenyl (PMP), etc.) — a factor that greatly restricts their broader applicability. In this study, we report the successful implementation of targeted modulation of the base partner in photocatalytic cascade reactions of cyclic alcohols, unlocking previously rather inaccessible, nonactivated substrates. This approach successfully bypasses the prevalent limitations of ring‐opening transformations of cycloalkanols by disaggregation of the bulk alcohol and strategic base selection. As a result, we here demonstrate an operationally simple and widely applicable protocol for the redox‐neutral transformations of cycloalkanols into terminally C(sp 3 )‐C(sp 3 )‐coupled, functionalized open‐chain products. NMR‐based mechanistic studies, comprising in‐depth H‐bond analysis as well as DOSY and ROESY experiments, have elucidated the previously unrecognized crucial role of substrate disaggregation in this multisite PCET, along with (pyridine) base effects surpassing typical p K a ‐related and/or steric effects. Ultimately, our insights, for the first time, reveal the critical importance of the aggregation state and the design of productive alcohol‐base pre‐organization beyond p K a and enabled us to successfully pioneer remote alkylative Giese‐type C─C‐bond formations of previously challenging alkyl‐substituted cycloalkanols.

title: Electronic Polarization in Covalent Organic Frameworks With Alternating Hetero‐Linkages for High‐Performance H 2 O 2 Photosynthesis
abstract: ABSTRACT Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) hold considerable promise for photocatalytic H 2 O 2 production, yet achieving efficient carrier separation and transport to achieve excellent performance remains a significantly challenge. Herein, we constructed a library of polarized COFs featuring alternating hetero‐linkage C═N and C─N linkages, which establish continuous local charge gradients at molecular level. Remarkably, driven by the localized electronic polarization microenvironment, the optimal material (TPPZ‐BC) showed a photocatalytic H 2 O 2 production rate as high as 11.06 mmol g −1 h −1 , outperforming most reported COF‐based photocatalysts. Mechanistic studies revealed that the spatial alternation of electron‐withdrawing C═N and electron‐donating C─N linkages induced a strong intramolecular charge polarization. This effect significantly modulates the surface electrostatic potential distribution, increasing the proportion of highly positive regions and thereby enhancing the adsorption and activation of oxygen molecules. Moreover, this structural design breaks molecular symmetry and promotes the synergistic alignment of local dipoles, generating a robust intrinsic electric field. This work provides a new strategy for the development of crystalline porous photocatalysts toward highly efficient photosynthesis.

title: Short‐Range Molecular Ordering Enables Efficient and Stable Recombination Junction in Monolithic Perovskite/CIGS Tandem Solar Cells
abstract: ABSTRACT Monolithic perovskite/Cu(In,Ga)Se 2 (CIGS) tandem solar cells have made remarkable progress in recent years and are highly promising for next‐generation photovoltaics. The recombination junction (RJ) linking the top and bottom subcells is an essential component that governs both device efficiency and operational stability. However, depositing a uniform RJ on the complex CIGS substrate while simultaneously achieving charge transport and operational robustness remains a formidable challenge. Here, we construct a short‐range ordered (SRO) hole‐selective architecture for the RJ by exploiting π–π interactions between a self‐assembled molecule (SAM) and a polymeric SAM (PCCP). The SRO architecture shortens the intermolecular π–π stacking distance to accelerate carrier transport, while the surrounding amorphous regions effectively interrupt ion migration pathways. Furthermore, this strategy enables conformal coverage over the complex CIGS topography, improves interfacial robustness, and enhances structural resilience in service. Consequently, monolithic perovskite/CIGS tandem solar cells employing the SRO‐RJ achieve a maximum power conversion efficiency of 29.60% (certified 28.94%, 0.2036 cm 2 ) and retain 98% of its initial efficiency after 1000 h of maximum power point tracking. Our findings establish short‐range molecular ordering as an effective strategy for engineering efficient and durable recombination junctions in monolithic tandem photovoltaics.

title: Gold‐Catalyzed “Anti‐Baldwin” Cyclization of Unactivated Alkenes
abstract: ABSTRACT Owing to the unfavorable orbital alignments and geometric constraints, 5‐ endo‐trig cyclizations are kinetically disfavored as stated by Sir Jack Baldwin. Consequently, reports of such cyclization are scarce and primarily rely on the use of activated alkenes. Herein, we report a rare example of “anti‐Baldwin” cyclization of unactivated alkenes. The key to the success of this transformation is that the kinetically favored 4‐ exo ‐ trig cyclization is reversible, thereby enabling equilibration to the thermodynamically favored 5‐ endo‐trig cyclization intermediate, which then undergoes reductive elimination to form the product.

title: A Route to High‐Temperature Creep Resistant Ultra‐High Molecular Weight Polyethylene
abstract: ABSTRACT High‐performance lightweight polymers for load‐bearing applications at elevated temperatures demand strong creep resistance to ensure long‐term dimensional and mechanical stability. Conventional uniaxial drawn polyethylene tapes and fibers suffer from poor creep resistance owing to intrinsically weak van der Waals intermolecular forces, especially above their α ‐relaxation temperature (∼90°C) as chain mobility is enhanced. Here we demonstrate that introducing as little as 0.2 mol% 1‐decene branches into low‐entangled ultra‐high molecular weight polyethylene (UHMWPE) profoundly suppresses high‐temperature creep. Solvent‐free solid‐state processing at a draw ratio of 250 yields branched and linear UHMWPE tapes with a specific tensile strength of 4.5 N/tex and a specific modulus of ∼200 N/tex. For the constant load of 250 MPa (∼2500 kg/cm 2 ), the linear UHMWPE tape at 110°C accumulates a creep strain of 15%, whereas the branched UHMWPE tapes maintain a negligible creep strain even at 150°C. This exceptional creep resistance is attributed to the ability of the branches to suppress the entropy‐driven relaxation of the oriented chains under constraints. This work resolves the long‐standing high‐temperature creep bottleneck of high‐performance PE, enabling high‐value, sustainable applications in automotive, energy distribution/storage, and advanced structural applications.

title: Nonpolar Micro‐Environment‐Induced Solvation Field Engineering Enables 600 Wh Kg −1 High‐Voltage Lithium Metal Pouch Cells
abstract: ABSTRACT Conventional‐carbonate electrolytes cannot simultaneously stabilize lithium metal interfaces and sustain fast ion transport. Existing designs mitigate interfacial degradation but compromise ion transport, low‐temperature fluidity, or salt dissociation. Herein, we propose a solvation field engineering strategy via a nonpolar micro‐environment‐induced electrolyte (NME) that overcomes this trade‐off at conventional salt concentration. Propyl propionate serves as an amphiphilic inducer: its carbonyl oxygen coordinates Li + , while its propyl chain extends outward to create a Li + ‐centered nonpolar micro‐environment that engineers the local solvation field by attenuating dielectric shielding and strengthening Li + –PF 6 − interactions, thereby driving a contact‐ion‐pair‐dominated solvation structure. Fluoroethylene carbonate and 2,2,2‐trifluoroethyl methyl carbonate ensure sufficient salt dissociation and high‐voltage oxidative stability. The resulting electrolyte combines rapid ion transport with a robust LiF/LiPO 2 F 2 interphase, suppressing electrolyte decomposition and enabling uniform Li plating/stripping. Consequently, a 4.2 Ah Li||LiNi 0.88 Co 0.07 Mn 0.05 O 2 pouch cell (∼425 Wh kg −1 ) retains 87.7% capacity after 200 cycles, and a 23.5 Ah Li||LiNi 0.95 Co 0.02 Mn 0.03 O 2 pouch cell achieves 604 Wh kg −1 . The strategy is further applicable to graphite‐based batteries, enabling a 3.6 Ah Graphite||LiNi 0.5 Co 0.2 Mn 0.3 O 2 pouch cell to deliver 81.5% retention after 100 cycles at −20°C. NME offers a novel principle to regulate solvation and interfacial stability for high‐energy batteries.

title: Programmable Amino Migration−Enabled Diversification of Allylamines
abstract: ABSTRACT Migration−enabled alkene functionalization offers an attractive strategy for accessing molecular architectures beyond the reach of conventional alkene transformations. Yet existing approaches typically channel translocated radical intermediates into a single reaction manifold, limiting the broader potential of migration chemistry for divergent synthesis. Here, we establish a programmable migration−enabled synthesis platform that redirects allylamines from passive alkene substrates into versatile synthons for divergent molecular construction. Through the integration of radical functionalization with amino migration, this strategy generates a migratory radical intermediate that undergoes selective diversification via complementary radical−trapping, atom−transfer radical addition (ATRA), and radical−polar crossover (RPC) pathways under mild photocatalytic conditions, enabling divergent 1,2,3−trifunctionalization of allylamines. Broad compatibility with radical precursors, bifunctional reagents, nucleophiles, and diverse allylamine scaffolds provides access to more than 70 densely functionalized, C(sp 3 )−rich amino architectures, including molecules bearing quaternary carbon centers. More broadly, this work establishes radical migration as a programmable design principle for molecular diversification and expands the synthetic utility of allylamines as modular synthons for the systematic exploration of structure−function relationships.

title: Ni‐Embedded Carbon Fibers Enable Synergistic Confinement and Catalytic Conversion of Iodine Species for Zn–I 2 Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Due to their affordability, safety and high capacity, aqueous Zn–I 2 batteries show great potential for large‐scale energy storage. Nevertheless, the dissolution of I 3 − intermediates leads to the iodine shuttle effect, which results in irreversible capacity loss and poor cyclability, thus hindering practical deployment. Here, we propose a synergistic strategy combining hierarchical pore confinement with catalytic iodine conversion to suppress the shuttle effect. A self‐standing cathode is synthesized, consisting of Ni nanoparticle‐embedded carbon nanoboxes enclosed within carbon macroporous fibers (Ni@CNBs‐CMFs). The abundant hierarchical porous structure provides physical confinement for iodine species, while Ni nanoparticles serve as active centers to accelerate iodine conversion via d–p orbital interactions. Benefiting from the synergistic enhancement in iodine accommodation and reaction kinetics, the self‐standing Ni@CNBs‐CMFs iodine cathode delivers a cycle life of 16 000 cycles with a capacity of 144.5 mAh g −1 and maintains a Coulombic efficiency of 90.0% after a 168‐h resting period. Moreover, the cathode also achieves a capacity of 382.8 mAh g −1 at a current of 2 A g −1 via the I − /I 0 /I + redox pathway.

title: Photoinduced Homolytic Carbon–Palladium Bond Cleavage of Zwitterionic π ‐Allylpalladium Species and Annulation with 1,3‐Dienes and 1,3‐Enynes
abstract: ABSTRACT The zwitterionic π ‐allylpalladium species are versatile intermediates in modern annulation chemistry, yet their assembling partners have been largely limited to electrophilic reagents or dipolarophiles. Herein, we report a previously inaccessible (4 + 2) annulation reaction of common π ‐allylpalladium(II) dipoles with electron‐neutral 1,3‐dienes and 1‐aryl‐substituted 1,3‐enynes via a distinct cooperative photo‐induced pathway. Mechanistic studies indicate that the process proceeds through visible light‐promoted homolytic cleavage of the allylic C–Pd bond to generate Pd(I) and allylic radicals, which undergo addition to polyunsaturated systems. Subsequent Pd(I)–radical recombination and intramolecular allylic substitution furnish a broad array of multifunctional oxa‐ and aza‐heterocycles, as well as carbocyclic frameworks, in moderate to good yields. In addition, their assemblies with electron‐poor dienes are also applicable, whereas the regioselectivity is distinct from that observed in traditional dipole‐based annulations. Furthermore, the asymmetric version is successful by employing chiral bisphosphine ligands, with fair to good enantioselectivity achieved.

title: Surfactant‐Induced Morphology Reconstruction for High‐Performance Near‐Infrared Perovskite Light‐Emitting Diodes
abstract: ABSTRACT High‐performance near‐infrared (NIR) perovskite light‐emitting diodes (PeLEDs) require the simultaneous suppression of nonradiative recombination and efficient photon extraction, in which additive often play a vital role. However, molecular design rules that connect additive structure with both crystallization control and optical morphology remain poorly defined. Here, we employ a series of hydroxyl‐functional quaternary ammonium surfactants—TMPAC, HDPAC, and DDPAC—with different alkyl‐chain lengths while retaining a common polar headgroup. This molecular design reveals how hydrophobic‐tail length regulates precursor organization and governs the balance among emissive quality, optical outcoupling, and charge transport. Increasing the alkyl‐chain length alters the phase‐conversion kinetics, suppresses lateral grain coalescence, and promotes anisotropic out‐of‐plane growth, thereby producing corrugated FAPbI 3 films. The intermediate‐chain HDPAC provides sufficient interfacial organization to improve radiative efficiency and photon extraction while maintaining favorable charge‐transport balance. HDPAC‐based devices achieve a peak external quantum efficiency (EQE) of 27.0%, exhibit markedly suppressed efficiency roll‐off, and deliver a maximum radiance exceeding 513 W sr − 1 m − 2 . These results establish hydrophobic‐tail length as an effective molecule‐level modulator for coupling interfacial crystallization control with photon management in perovskite emitters.

title: N‐Type Organic Ultraviolet Sensor
abstract: ABSTRACT Ultraviolet radiation monitoring is important for health, industrial, and environmental applications. Commercial inorganic UV photodetectors offer high selectivity and stability, yet rely on rigid materials and high‐temperature processing, whereas organic UV photodetectors are solution‐processable and flexible but suffer from instability and complex stacking architectures. In this study, we demonstrate ambient‐operated organic UV sensors based on an n‐type conducting polymer, poly(benzodifurandione) (PBFDO). We propose that thermal treatment promotes oxygen‐mediated carrier trapping that lowers the carrier concentration, while 365 nm UVA illumination induces carrier release and increases conductivity, yielding a two‐terminal device with a broad irradiance range (0.02–500 mW/cm 2 ), large current changes (65%), well‐defined intensity‐time dependence, and reversible reset via trap reconfiguration. We achieve flexible sensors, high‐density arrays, and optoelectronic information encryption. Increasing the degree of dedoping with stronger oxidants raises the relative current change to as high as 17200% under prolonged irradiation, while retaining a reproducible UVA response. We further present organic photoelectrochemical transistors that couple light signals with electrochemical gating to achieve synapse‐like functions. This strategy offers broad application prospects and a versatile design framework for next‐generation organic optoelectronic systems.

title: Synergistic Salt‐Bridge and Hydrophobic Interaction‐Driven Supramolecular Adhesives Enable Ultrastrong Dry/Underwater Bonding and Broad Harsh‐Condition Adaptability: Polyelectrolyte‐Templated Multi‐Promoting Effects
abstract: ABSTRACT Developing advanced amphibious adhesives that perform well in both dry and underwater environments is critical yet challenging for unlocking diverse underwater applications.
