Here, we propose a general polyelectrolyte‐templated multi‐regulation strategy to establish a new cooperative salt‐bridge/hydrophobic interaction‐driven supramolecular adhesive that overcomes long‐standing water‐adhesive conflicts and attains rapid yet ultrastrong dry/underwater adhesion with broad harsh‐environment adaptability. By engineering branched‐polycationic electrolytes with dense interaction sites as versatile templates, this strategy exerts multi‐promoting effects of polyelectrolytes on dense salt‐bridge formation, precursor wetting and ultrafast solvent‐free curing, which, in cooperation with flexible hydrophobic moieties, optimizes cohesion/interfacial adhesion, balances flexibility‐rigidity and inhibits water‐erosion and interface hydration within cured network. Thus, the optimized b‐PAE achieves ultrahigh dry and underwater bonding strengths up to 20.9 and 13.2 MPa on safety glass within 10 s—a performance integration rarely reported in previous adhesives. It further demonstrates robust adhesion in harsh underwater conditions (seawater, acidic, alkaline solutions), excellent cryogenic tolerance (−196°C) and versatile utility including oil tank leakage repair and rapid pipeline sealing. Mechanistic studies reveal that the synergy of salt‐bridge and hydrophobic interactions governs amphibious adhesion. This universal approach, applicable to various hydrophobic moieties, paves the way for developing diverse amphibious adhesives to advance underwater technologies.

title: Concentration‐Driven Solvation Reorganization Featuring Viologen Clustering Enables Air‐Tolerant Aqueous Organic Redox Flow Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Viologen derivatives are promising anolytes in aqueous organic redox‐flow batteries (AORFBs), but long‐term stability under ambient air remains challenging. Using 1,1′‐bis[3‐(trimethylammonio)propyl]‐4,4′‐bipyridinium tetrachloride (BVCl 4 ), we show through physicochemical characterization and molecular dynamics simulations that increasing BV concentration beyond a critical threshold induces a solvation transition characterized by viologen clustering. Controlled O 2 exposure of bulk‐electrolyzed BV 4+ /BV 3+• solutions using a carbon felt electrode, together with air‐exposed AORFB full‐cell cycling, shows that BV is converted to redox‐inactive byproducts via OH–/reactive oxygen species (ROS) generated by BV 3+• ‐O 2 galvanic reactions and electrode‐driven hydrogen evolution reaction (HER). The degradation is suppressed in a nonmonotonic manner governed by the solvation‐transition threshold. We suggest that the enhanced air tolerance of concentrated BV electrolytes arises from this solvation reorganization, associated with viologen‐clustering‐induced steric shielding against O 2 /OH − /ROS attack and restricted BV hydration that limits Grotthuss‐type OH − transport to reactive BV sites. Additionally, electrochemical quartz crystal microbalance measurements at an Au electrode directly visualize BV 2+ as the most degradation‐prone state, forming redox‐inactive deposits through reactions with OH − /ROS generated locally by HER and oxygen reduction reaction; this pathway is strongly attenuated once electrolyte solvation reorganizes. Voltammetry at an Au ultramicroelectrode further reveals that solvation‐transition‐driven clustering suppresses BV 3+• disproportionation.

title: Rare‐Earth‐Modulated Fe–Tb Dual‐Metal Single‐Atom Site Catalyst Enables Enhanced Activity and Durability for Acidic Oxygen Reduction
abstract: ABSTRACT The critical dependence on Pt in proton‐exchange membrane fuel cells (PEMFCs) remains a bottleneck for commercialization. Single‐atom‐site catalysts, such as Fe‐NC, show comparable activity for the oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) in PEMFCs, yet their inferior stability constrains practical applications. In this work, we introduced the rare‐earth element Tb as a single‐atom site into the Fe‐NC system and constructed a dual‐metal single‐atom site catalyst (denoted as FeTb‐NC). Theoretical calculations and experiments suggest that Tb centers, with strong oxophilicity and unique electronic structure, synergistically regulate *OH binding on adjacent FeN 4 sites, thereby lowering the energy barrier for *OH desorption. This elevates the activity of Fe centers and, more importantly, significantly lowers *OH coverage on FeN 4 , mitigating its detrimental effects. The optimized FeTb‐NC catalyst displays improved performance: The half‐wave potential is as high as 0.89 V (vs. RHE), retaining 88% of its initial current density after 100 h at 0.8 V. The PEMFC assembled with FeTb‐NC as the cathode catalyst exhibits competitive performance and durability; the peak power density reaches 1.10 W cm −2 under H 2 /O 2 conditions, and the device maintains 80% current‐density retention after 100 h under H 2 /air conditions. This work offers new insights into performance optimization of Fe–NC‐based materials and supports development of Pt‐free PEMFCs.

title: Rational Design of a Chiral Hybrid Ge(II) Halide With Giant Chiroptical Activity for Circularly Polarized Light Detection
abstract: ABSTRACT Chiral hybrid metal halides integrate semiconducting optoelectronic functionality with intrinsic chirality, offering new opportunities in the field of next‐generation chiral photonics and spintronics. However, the incorporation of chiral organic ligands alone is often insufficient to induce pronounced chiral structural distortions, thereby limiting the resulting chiroptical activity. Herein, we demonstrate for the first time that the stereochemically active 4s 2 lone‐pair of Ge 2+ can serve as an internal structural amplifier of chirality. We rationally designed and synthesized a pair of enantiomeric chiral hybrid Ge(II) halides, denoted as ( R / S ‐MBA)GeI 3 (MBA is methylbenzylammonium). Specifically, the strong lone‐pair expression in ( R / S ‐MBA)GeI 3 drives significant chirality‐favorable distortions, manifested by a large asymmetric bond angle variance and projected deflection angle of the chiral [−Ge−I−] ∞ chains. This enhanced structural chirality increases the circular dichroism (CD) anisotropy factor ( g CD ) of ( R / S ‐MBA)GeI 3 to 2.66 times that of the Pb(II) homologs. Benefiting from the superior chiroptical activity, ( R / S ‐MBA)GeI 3 further exhibits second‐harmonic generation (SHG)‐CD anisotropy factor ( g SHG‐CD ) values of −1.17/1.09, while the corresponding devices achieve photocurrent anisotropy factors ( g Iph ) of −0.403/0.391. Finally, we demonstrated a proof‐of‐concept circularly polarized light‐encrypted optical communication system. Our work provides a new insight into the rational design of high‐performance chiral functional materials.

title: Black Titanium‐Oxo Cluster as a Dual‐Mode Catalyst for Regioselective Protein Editing
abstract: ABSTRACT Atomically precise titanium‐oxo clusters are discrete molecular analogues of TiO 2 and structural building blocks of many metal–organic frameworks. Combining features of homogeneous and heterogeneous catalysis, they provide a versatile platform for catalyst design. However, due to limited stability in aqueous media, they remain largely unexplored in biologically relevant catalysis. Here, we report a structurally engineered hexanuclear titanium‐oxo cluster (tBu‐Ti 6 ) with promising photophysical properties, including a very low optical gap of 1.56 eV. Using β‐lactoglobulin as a model protein, we demonstrate that tBu‐Ti 6 is an effective heterogeneous catalyst in aqueous solution, promoting both hydrolytic and photooxidative protein cleavage via two distinct pathways: Lewis acid‐mediated hydrolysis and reactive oxygen species‐driven photocatalysis. Nano‐scale liquid chromatography‐tandem mass spectrometry (nLC‐MS/MS) reveals preferential cleavage near negatively charged regions of the protein, indicating electrostatic substrate recognition. Under 370 nm irradiation, tBu‐Ti 6 induces oxidation of tyrosine, tryptophan, and methionine residues in the intact β‐lactoglobulin, underscoring its potential as a photocatalyst for selective protein modifications. During reactions in aqueous solutions, the cluster remains structurally intact, shows no decomposition or dissolution, and is reusable without loss of activity. Together, these results establish TOCs as versatile molecular catalysts for controlled protein modifications and underscore their potential in bioinspired catalysis.

title: Synergistic Lewis Base Organocatalysis and Electrocatalysis for the Enantioselective Construction of α‐Fluorinated Quaternary Stereocenters
abstract: ABSTRACT The construction of α‐fluorinated quaternary stereocenters—a structural motif of high value in pharmaceuticals and bioactive molecules—remains a formidable synthetic challenge due to inherent steric and stereoelectronic constraints. Herein, we report a synergistic strategy combining chiral isothiourea (ITU) organocatalysis with electrochemistry, enabling the direct and highly enantioselective α‐alkylation of bench‐stable fluorinated acetic esters with both silyl enol ethers and allylsilanes. This approach integrates anodic single‐electron oxidation with asymmetric Lewis base catalysis, converting in situ‐generated disubstituted C1‐ammonium enolates into configurationally well‐defined, chiral ITU‐bound α‐carbonyl tertiary radical intermediates. Subsequent stereocontrolled radical cross‐coupling with SOMOphilic partners furnishes a broad range of esters bearing α‐fluorinated quaternary stereocenters in high yields (up to 95%) and excellent enantioselectivities (up to 99% ee). This work not only fills a significant gap in the single‐electron chemistry of disubstituted C1‐ammonium enolates but also provides a versatile platform for the rapid assembly of optically active α‐fluorinated quaternary carbonyl compounds, with significant potential in drug discovery and complex molecule synthesis.
